news.summaryZh: OpenAI发布Astra for Law，这是其最新模型GPT-6 Astra针对法律工作配置的版本，包含专用法律搜索索引以及用于法律分析和写作的自定义指令。Astra for Law将很快向API客户开放，包括Harvey和Legora，并至少初期通过新的“Trusted Access”计划向部分律所提供，该计划针对Am Law 200律所，通过ChatGPT及其软件工程代理Codex授予专门访问权限。Trusted Access计划包括API新的零数据保留政策，以及ChatGPT Enterprise不被OpenAI任何人员人工审查。获得访问权限的律所和法律技术公司可在其基础上构建，无需自行组装和维护底层法律搜索与指令。OpenAI还推出了一系列新插件，使ChatGPT在法律工作中更实用和可扩展，包括来自Thomson Reuters、Harvey、Legora和iManage等供应商的26个插件、由律师和法律工程师构建的9个插件，以及47项自定义技能。此外，OpenAI宣布ChatGPT for Word正式可用，律师可在Word内使用ChatGPT进行校对、获取建议编辑并标记格式问题。此前，OpenAI于6月聘请合同生命周期管理公司Ironclad的联合创始人兼前CEO Jason Boehmig领导法律行业产品开发。在该招聘之前，竞争对手Anthropic已通过推出Claude for Legal大举进军法律领域。昨日，Boehmig和领导法律产品开发的OpenAI工程师Sherwin Wu就Astra for Law向媒体作了简报。Boehmig强调这不是新模型，而是为法律工作定制模型的配置，包括法律写作等任务的领域特定指令、响应长度等设置以及法律行业特定工具，这些都将随时间增长。
news.bodyHtml:
Calling it the beginning of its long-term investment in law, ChatGPT developer OpenAI today released Astra for Law, a version of its latest model, GPT-6 Astra, configured for legal work, including a dedicated legal search index and custom instructions for legal analysis and writing.

“Today, we’re introducing Astra for Law: a new foundation for law firms and legal technology companies to build AI products and workflows around their expertise,” the company said in a blog post announcing the product. “It combines GPT-6 Astra, our latest and most powerful model, with settings, tools, and context tailored for professional legal work — from researching complex cases to structuring consequential deals.”

The company said that Astra for Law will be available soon to API customers, including Harvey and Legora, and offered, at least initially, to selected law firms through a new “Trusted Access” program targeting Am Law 200 firms that grants specialized access through ChatGPT and Codex, its software engineering agent.

The Trusted Access program includes a new zero data retention policy for the API and exclusion of ChatGPT Enterprise from human review by anyone at OpenAI.

Firms and legal technology companies with access to Astra for Law will be able to build on its foundation without having to assemble and maintain the underlying legal search and instructions on their own, the company said.

In addition to launching Astra for Law, OpenAI said it is launching a series of new plugins designed to make ChatGPT more useful and extensible for legal work, including 26 from vendors such as Thomson Reuters, Harvey, Legora and iManage and nine built by lawyers and legal engineers, as well as 47 custom skills.

Also, OpenAI announced the general availability of ChatGPT for Word, enabling lawyers to use ChatGPT within Word to proofread, get suggested edits, and flag formatting issues.

All of this follows the company’s hiring in June of Jason Boehmig, the cofounder and former CEO of contract lifecycle management company Ironclad, to lead development of products for the legal industry.

Ahead of that hiring, OpenAI competitor Anthropic had announced its own major push into legal with the launch of Claude for Legal.

Related: On LawNext: Inside Claude for Legal — Anthropic’s Mark Pike on AI’s Next Frontier in Law.

Embedded Legal Research

Yesterday, Boehmig and Sherwin Wu, the OpenAI engineer who has led the development of the legal product, provided a briefing for the media on Astra for Law.

Boehmig emphasized that this is not a new model, but rather a model configuration to customize the model for legal work. It includes domain-specific instructions on tasks such as legal writing, settings such as the length of responses, and tooling specific to the legal industry, all of which will grow over time.

The first major implementation of that tooling is its Legal Search Index, a legal research capability that allows it to search U.S. case law, statutes, regulations, court rules and administrative decisions across a corpus of more than 230 million URLs.

To create its collection of legal research materials, OpenAI drew from CourtListener, the legal research library maintained by the nonprofit Free Law Project.

Beyond simply conducting legal research, OpenAI says that Astra for Law is designed to use that Legal Search Index to help lawyers apply the law to the facts of a matter, to develop arguments or deal terms, and to identify weaknesses or uncertainty.

During the briefing, Wu demonstrated three tasks, in which he used Astra for Law in ChatGPT to draft a motion to dismiss for a hospital defending a disability-discrimination and retaliation claim, a stockholder challenge to an asset sale rushed through over a holiday weekend, and for a sales-commitment dispute.

Product Benchmarking

OpenAI says it tested Astra for Law’s legal research capabilities against 200 U.S. legal research questions from the private validation set of Vals AI’s Legal Research Bench, a benchmark that measures how well the model can find relevant sources and passages, and how well its research answers meet the evaluation criteria.

At the highest reasoning effort for both systems, the company says, Astra for Law passed the evaluation’s overall correctness check on 54% of questions, compared with 38.7% for GPT-6 Astra using web search alone – an increase of 15.3 percentage points, or a 40% relative improvement.

Astra for Law also produces more comprehensive answers, roughly twice as long on average as the Astra web-only baseline across the tested reasoning settings, the company says.

On case-law-focused questions, Astra for Law found 24% more reference cases than GPT-6 Astra using web search alone at the highest reasoning effort. On the audited set of target passages, it retrieved up to 54% more relevant passages from the correct court opinions, when comparing the systems at the same reasoning effort.

New Partner and Community Plugins

As part of today’s announcement, OpenAI is also launching a series of vendor- and community-developed plugins designed to help legal professionals do more with ChatGPT, including 26 developed by partners such as Thomson Reuters, Harvey, Legora and iManage.

As examples of what the vendor plugins will enable, OpenAI said iManage’s will allow a lawyer to draft a negotiation brief in ChatGPT and save it to the matter file, Intapp’s will surface activities that may need a time entry for review, DeepJudge’s will bring prior deals into a comparison, and Thomson Reuters’ will bring HighQ matter context into ChatGPT and later include a connector to CoCounsel Legal.

There are also nine community plugins developed by lawyers and legal engineers at LegalQuants, LegalEng Consulting Group (LECG), and Skills.law, and 47 custom skills that legal professionals can adapt, extend or draw inspiration from to do work in ChatGPT. OpenAI said these custom skills were developed by legal “power users,” not by OpenAI.

New ‘Trusted Access Program’

As part of the new offering, the company is creating a special Trusted Access Program under which eligible law firms will be able to give lawyers and people working under their supervision access to Astra for Law for professional legal work.

The program is targeted at Am Law 200 programs. For firms that qualify, the offering includes zero data retention on the API and usage of ChatGPT enterprise is excluded from human review.

In addition, OpenAI said it is working with the law firm Latham & Watkins to design for information permissions, ethical walls, client instructions, and firm oversight.

Asked by a reporter whether there were any exceptions to the zero data retention policy, Boehmig said that is a one-sentence summary of the full access-program agreement, which runs some 30 pages. But he said OpenAI has worked with the industry to validate that it works in this context. “It’s definitely more complicated than the one sentence,” he said, “but we also feel extremely confident that the 30 pages do meet the need.”

Building On Firms’ Own Knowledge

OpenAI’s announcement stresses the importance for law firms of building AI around their own precedents, methods and judgment, and offers several examples of how its forward-deployed engineers — OpenAI engineers who are embedded within a law firm — have been adapting ChatGPT Enterprise through custom integrations with firms’ proprietary data and workflows.

It says that Sullivan & Cromwell, for example, built an agreement analyzer that uses the firm’s negotiating playbooks and selected precedents in the review of a new deal. Another firm, Ropes & Gray, built an M&A diligence system around how its lawyers work through a data room and decide what matters to the deal.

Still another, Cooley, built GO Public to bring its capital markets expertise into how companies prepare to go public, from drafting the IPO filing to identifying the risks that deserve management’s attention.

“With frontier intelligence and the right controls, firms can turn their own precedents, methods, and judgment into AI tools and workflows built to their standards,” OpenAI says.

Just the Beginning

“OpenAI is investing in law for the long term,” the company said in making these announcements.

It said that it will continue to improve ChatGPT as a platform for firms to build around their expertise and connect the tools they already use, and to conduct rigorous evaluations and collect user feedback to monitor where improvements are needed and what to bulid next.

In response to a question at the media briefing, Boehmig said the company’s commitment to legal includes a commitment to access to justice, which he said is a “paramount concern” to him personally and to OpenAI as a company, but that today’s news is focused on Astra for Law and that there will be more to share in the future related to A2J.

“We’re committed to working with this ecosystem so firms can bring their own expertise, standards, and judgment to AI – and serve clients in ways only they can,” the company said.

news.titleEn: AI in the Jury Box: Promise, Limits and the Role of Human Deliberation
news.titleZh: AI进入陪审团席：前景、局限与人类审议的作用
news.summaryZh:
北卡罗来纳大学教堂山分校法学院据报在基于真实少年案件的模拟审判中，使用ChatGPT、Claude和Grok担任陪审员。与此同时，AI驱动的陪审团研究平台正进入诉讼咨询市场，为律师和理赔专业人员提供责任、比较过失和潜在损害赔偿的快速评估。这些工具有助于法律团队测试竞争性叙事、识别能引起共鸣的主题，并标记可能不受欢迎的论点，且比传统陪审团研究更快、成本更低。

但律师应区分可靠性与有效性。AI模拟可能稳定测量个人对案件摘要的反应，却仍无法捕捉实际陪审团达成裁决的方式。真实陪审员会讨论证据、质疑彼此假设，并通过审议修正观点。特定审判地的态度和社区规范也会影响结果，而广泛的模拟人群可能无法反映这些因素。因此，AI陪审团研究最好被视为筛选工具，而非焦点小组、模拟审判或其他互动方法的替代品。它可以为早期案件评估提供信息，帮助律师决定何处需要更深入研究，但其精美的百分比和损害赔偿范围不应被误认为实际裁决的预测。对法律团队而言，关键问题不是AI或传统研究哪个绝对更好，而是所选方法是否衡量了重要问题。当案件取决于有争议的证据、群体动态和集体判断时，人类审议仍然至关重要。
news.bodyText: Find Your Next Job ! Last fall, the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill School of Law reportedly used ChatGPT, Claude, and Grok as jurors in a mock trial based on a real juvenile case. At the same time, AI-powered jury research platforms are entering the litigation consulting market, offering attorneys and claims professionals rapid assessments of liability, comparative fault, and potential damages. These tools can provide valuable early insights. They may help legal teams test competing narratives, identify themes that resonate and flag arguments that could be poorly received, all faster and at a lower cost than traditional jury research. However, lawyers should distinguish reliability from validity. An AI simulation may consistently measure individual reactions to a case summary yet still fail to capture how an actual jury reaches a verdict. Real jurors discuss evidence, challenge each other’s assumptions, and revise their views through deliberation. Venue-specific attitudes and community norms also shape outcomes in ways that broad simulated populations may not reflect. AI jury research is therefore best viewed as a screening tool rather than a substitute for focus groups, mock trials, or other interactive methods. It can inform early case assessment and help counsel decide where deeper research is warranted, but its polished percentages and damages ranges should not be mistaken for predictions of an actual verdict. For legal teams, the key question is not whether AI or traditional research is categorically better, it is whether the chosen method measures the issue that matters. When a case turns on contested evidence, group dynamics, and collective judgment, human deliberation remains central. news.summaryZh: 昨日，“Google Legal”展示了Gemini Enterprise如何为律师部署，涵盖日常提示、NotebookLM使用及自定义应用开发。演示由Google Cloud法律顾问Xavier Polidoro主持，重点是他所称的“高级”用途，包括“云端法律AI助手”。这些定制解决方案似乎与更具体品牌的“Gemini Enterprise for Legal”相关联——该近期宣布的产品附带多个代理，但此处使用了不同措辞。展示内容概述如下，其中许多仅涉及律师如何使用Gemini LLM能力以及NotebookLM进行法律工作。最后，Polidoro介绍了可连接任意来源并执行特定任务（如红线标注文档或协助撰写简报）的定制代理开发。他们还提及Harvey使用Gemini，以及Freshfields和Inspira。演示包括：一般提示——使用Gemini Enterprise聊天加速合同摘要、风险标记和初步客户沟通；基于来源的研究——使用Gemini Notebook搜索、交叉引用和总结密集法律库及多修订协议，并完全基于来源；自定义助手——云端法律AI助手演练，展示法律团队如何构建和部署用于交易管理的自定义聊天机器人。在介绍如何充分利用Gemini标准提示后，Polidoro转向NotebookLM。它提供许多功能，包括将工作成果转为音频“播客”——这很疯狂，但主要好处是连接Notebook到多个来源然后开始工作。谷歌强调可添加300个来源，每个最多50万字。简言之，律所或法律团队可将Notebook连接到大量文档和数据，这非常有用。
news.bodyText: Yesterday, ‘Google Legal’ gave an inside look at how Gemini Enterprise can be deployed for lawyers, from everyday prompting, to NotebookLM use, to custom app development. Artificial Lawyer was there. The demonstration was led by Xavier Polidoro, Legal Counsel, Google Cloud, and the highlight was what he called the ‘advanced’ uses, which covered ‘Cloud Legal AI Helpers’. These customised solutions appear to connect to the more specifically branded ‘Gemini Enterprise for Legal’ – the recently announced offering that comes with a number of agents, although in this case they used a different wording. Here’s an overview of what was on show – with a lot of it simply about how lawyers can use the Gemini LLM capability and also NotebookLM for legal work. At the end, Polidoro covered the development of customised agents that can be connected to whatever sources you want, and then steered to perform certain tasks, e.g. redline a document, or help to write brief. They also interestingly mentioned Harvey’s use of Gemini, as well as Freshfields – which they have mentioned before, and also Inspira. So, first an overview of what they showed, then NotebookLM, then the Legal AI Helpers Live In-Tool Demonstrations: ‘General Prompting: Accelerating contract summaries, risk flagging, and preliminary client communications using Gemini Enterprise chat. Grounded Research: Using Gemini Notebook to search, cross-reference, and summarize dense legal repositories and multi-amendment agreements with full source grounding. Custom Helpers: A walkthrough of the Cloud Legal AI Helpers, showing how legal teams can build and deploy custom chatbots for deal management.’ – After an introduction on how to get the most out of standard prompting with Gemini, Polidoro moved onto NotebookLM. It’s got a lot on offer, including turning your work product into an audio ‘podcast’ – which is wild, but the main benefit is simply the way that you can connect Notebook to multiple sources and then get to work. Google highlighted that you can add in 300 sources, each up to 500,000 words. In short, a law firm or legal team could connect Notebook to a huge trove of documents and data. And that’s really useful.

research.titleEn: Structured Four-Stage Legal Translation: From Natural-Language Traffic Rules to PROLOG
research.titleZh: 结构化四阶段法律翻译：从自然语言交通规则到PROLOG
research.abstractEn: Traffic regulations are written for human interpretation and therefore rely on shared background knowledge and flexible phrasing, which inherently introduce ambiguity, context dependence, and semantic underspecification. These linguistic characteristics conflict with the precision required by computational reasoning engines such as Prolog, which demand explicit logical structure. This study evaluates two baseline translation approaches, Natural Language to Prolog ($NL\rightarrow Prolog$) and Logical English to Prolog ($LE\rightarrow Prolog$), and introduces a new reasoning-guided translation framework called Structured Four-Stage Legal Translation ($S4L\rightarrow Prolog$). The proposed S4L framework performs semantic role extraction, scene completion, logical mapping, and Prolog rule generation within a single guided prompt, enabling direct translation of raw traffic rules into executable logic without human intervention. A benchmark consisting of twenty real-world traffic rules was used to evaluate each approach in terms of syntactic validity, semantic correctness, and logical completeness. $S4L\rightarrow Prolog$ achieves the highest accuracy, correctly formalizing 75 percent of the rules, while $NL\rightarrow Prolog$ reaches 60 percent and $LE\rightarrow Prolog$ reaches 55 percent. Qualitative analysis further shows that S4L captures implicit causal relations, deontic modality, and exception structure more reliably than the baselines. These results demonstrate that structured reasoning prompts can substantially improve the reliability of natural-language-to-logic translation for legal and safety-critical applications.
research.abstractZh: 交通法规是为人类理解而编写的，因此依赖于共享的背景知识和灵活的措辞，这固有地引入了歧义、上下文依赖性和语义欠明确性。这些语言特征与诸如Prolog等计算推理引擎所要求的精确性相冲突，后者要求明确的逻辑结构。本研究评估了两种基线翻译方法，即自然语言到Prolog（$NL\rightarrow Prolog$）和逻辑英语到Prolog（$LE\rightarrow Prolog$），并引入了一种新的推理引导翻译框架，称为结构化四阶段法律翻译（$S4L\rightarrow Prolog$）。所提出的S4L框架在单个引导提示中执行语义角色提取、场景补全、逻辑映射和Prolog规则生成，使得原始交通规则无需人工干预即可直接翻译为可执行逻辑。使用包含二十条真实世界交通规则的基准测试集，从语法有效性、语义正确性和逻辑完整性方面评估每种方法。$S4L\rightarrow Prolog$达到了最高的准确率，正确形式化了75%的规则，而$NL\rightarrow Prolog$达到60%，$LE\rightarrow Prolog$达到55%。定性分析进一步表明，S4L比基线方法更可靠地捕获了隐含的因果关系、道义模态和例外结构。这些结果表明，结构化推理提示可以显著提高法律和安全关键应用中自然语言到逻辑翻译的可靠性。

policy.titleEn: 守好网络法治防线 护航数字经济行稳致远 ——最高法发布典型案例聚焦网络法治
policy.titleZh: 守好网络法治防线 护航数字经济行稳致远 ——最高法发布典型案例聚焦网络法治
policy.summaryZh:
2026年9月14日至20日国家网络安全宣传周期间，最高人民法院于9月16日发布4件典型案例，聚焦网络法治，明确网络暴力人格权侵害禁令适用、带货主播侵害人格权责任认定、搜索引擎服务提供者侵权责任认定、为跨境赌博提供网络技术支持服务定罪量刑等问题。

案例一为李某申请人格权侵害禁令案。李某与张某、胡某均为短视频平台自媒体博主，张某、胡某账号合计超2000万粉丝。2023年7月起，张某以李某“插足”其与男友情感为由发布侮辱、诽谤言论并联合胡某炒作，煽动粉丝实施网络暴力，致李某部分商业合作方解约；诉讼中二人仍继续实施。法院认定符合民法典第九百九十七条人格权侵害禁令适用条件，明确应综合考量侵权方式与信息传播速度范围判断紧迫性、人格权类型与救济手段是否充分判断损害是否难以弥补、相关因素裁定禁令措施防止超出必要限度。《最高人民法院关于依法审理涉人工智能纠纷案件的意见》亦对依法适用该禁令制度作出规范。案例二为李某瑾诉某文化公司网络侵权责任纠纷案。某文化公司委托带货主播制作发布短视频推广家庭育儿类图书，约定视频侵权由委托方担责；主播未经授权截取李某瑾演讲、授课视频片段，搭配音色、语调、发音风格高度近似的AI合成音频，制作发布带跳转购书链接的宣传视频，某文化公司未审核素材及授权材料。
policy.bodyText:
遭遇“网暴”如何快速拿起维权的法律武器？如何划分“技术创新”的权责边界？为网络犯罪提供“技术帮助”，究竟要承担怎样的法律责任？
2026年9月14日至20日是国家网络安全宣传周，主题为“网络安全为人民，网络安全靠人民——智能时代网安护航”。网络强国建设离不开司法审判工作的支撑与保障，宣传周期间，最高人民法院于9月16日发布4件典型案例，明确发生网络暴力时的人格权侵害禁令适用、带货主播侵害他人人格权的责任认定、搜索引擎服务提供者的侵权责任认定、为跨境赌博提供网络技术支持服务的定罪量刑等问题，用鲜活案例明晰网络行为法律边界，用裁判规范引领网络空间法治风尚。
用好人格权禁令，筑牢人格权益“防火墙”
网络暴力传播快、范围广、伤害深，有时一条谣言、一场直播“围攻”，就足以让受害者陷入精神伤害、名誉贬损、经济损失的困境。而且这种损害结果往往不可逆，即使事后通过司法程序赢得了赔偿，也很难完全抚平受害人的创伤。
民法典第九百九十七条设立人格权侵害禁令制度，目的是及时制止人格权侵权、防止损害发生和扩大，按下侵权“停止键”。不久前出台的《最高人民法院关于依法审理涉人工智能纠纷案件的意见》，亦对依法适用人格权侵害禁令制度作出相关规范。但在司法实践中，如何把握人格权侵害禁令条款“不及时制止将使其合法权益受到难以弥补的损害”这一适用条件，一直是实践中的难点问题。
在第一个典型案例“李某申请人格权侵害禁令案”中，李某与张某、胡某均为短视频平台自媒体博主，张某、胡某的网络账号共计有超2000万粉丝。2023年7月起，张某以李某“插足”其与男友情感为由，在网络平台公开发布针对李某的侮辱、诽谤言论，并联合胡某炒作相关话题，煽动粉丝对李某实施谩骂、攻击、举报等网络暴力行为。事件发生后，李某的部分商业合作方解除与李某的合作协议。
随后，李某提起名誉权侵权诉讼，但在案件审理过程中，张某、胡某仍煽动粉丝实施上述网络暴力行为，李某遂向法院申请人格权侵害禁令。
法院审理认为，张某、胡某对李某实施了群体性网络暴力违法行为，且在案件审理过程中仍继续实施上述网络暴力行为、扩大损害结果。张某、胡某通过直播等形式在网络上传播侵权信息，案涉信息传播速度快、波及范围广、负面影响大，已对李某造成精神损害和经济损失，不及时制止将导致李某合法权益受到难以弥补的损害，符合人格权侵害禁令适用条件。
对于网络暴力情形下适用人格权侵害禁令的审查，本案明确了三个应当综合考量的因素。一是综合考量侵权行为方式、信息传播速度和范围等因素，判断是否达到需要及时制止的紧迫性标准；二是综合考量被侵害人格权类型、侵害行为性质、事后赔偿等救济手段是否能够充分弥补申请人的损害等因素，审查损害是否难以弥补；三是综合考量被侵害人格权类型、侵权行为方式以及损害范围、程度等因素，裁定采取相应禁令措施，防止超出必要限度。
划清权责边界，回应数字时代新挑战
随着人工智能技术深度融入各类互联网场景，AI换脸拟声、大模型检索生成等新应用层出不穷。但技术在赋能产业的同时，新的侵权纠纷也随之衍生。
在电商平台，一些商家委托主播剪辑他人公开影像，配上高度仿真AI合成声音，假借名人影响力推销商品，殊不知已经违反了法律。
“李某瑾诉某文化公司网络侵权责任纠纷案”正是这样一起关于“AI仿名人带货”套路的典型案例。在本案中，某文化公司为推广销售家庭育儿类图书，委托某带货主播制作发布短视频进行网络宣传，并协议约定，视频侵犯第三方合法权益的，由委托方承担责任。某带货主播未经授权擅自截取李某瑾演讲、授课的视频片段，搭配音色、语调、发音风格与李某瑾高度近似的AI合成音频，制作并发布带有跳转购书链接的宣传视频。经查，案涉视频中的相关素材并未取得李某瑾的授权，某文化公司也未对案涉视频的相关素材及授权材料进行审核。
法院审理认为，案涉视频未经李某瑾同意，擅自使用李某瑾肖像并结合使用与其声纹特征高度吻合的AI合成声音，构成对李某瑾肖像权和声音权益的侵害。某文化公司未对视频素材的来源、视频素材是否获得李某瑾授权等事项进行审核，存在未尽合理审核义务的过失，构成共同侵权。遂判决某文化公司向李某瑾赔礼道歉、赔偿经济损失及维权合理支出。
本案判决提示广大电商经营者：带货主播受电子商务经营者委托，通过制作发布视频等方式进行商品推广时，故意使用侵害他人人格权等权益的素材的，构成侵权；委托人电子商务经营者对宣传推广内容未尽到法律规定或者合同约定的审核义务，对损害结果发生存在过失的，与带货主播成立共同侵权，应依法承担连带责任。
policy.relevanceReason: 最高人民法院发布的典型案例涉及网络暴力人格权侵害禁令、AI仿名人带货侵权责任、搜索引擎服务提供者侵权责任及为跨境赌博提供网络技术支持服务定罪量刑，直接关系网络空间司法审判与人工智能应用的法律边界，属于法院与AI、AI法律合规核心议题。

news.titleEn: RelativityOne Gets A New Name To Reflect Its Increasing Capabilities Around AI and Data
news.titleZh: RelativityOne更名以反映其在AI和数据方面不断增强的能力
news.summaryZh: 电子取证公司Relativity宣布，将其云平台RelativityOne更名为Relativity aiR，该名称此前用于Relativity的AI与代理能力套件。更名旨在将平台及其AI能力统一在一个名称下。AI是如同当年云一样具有变革性的转变，Relativity拥有值得信赖的平台和经验来负责任地引领这一转变。Relativity自2001年成立以来长期仅提供本地部署产品，2017年推出SaaS替代方案RelativityOne。尽管本地产品曾是电子取证领域的巨头，云平台最终取代了它，去年Saunders宣布2028年所有新案件必须迁移至RelativityOne。同时，Relativity推出了一系列生成式AI产品，始于2023年宣布的Relativity aiR for Review，用于帮助用户更快定位响应发现请求的数据。此后陆续推出aiR for Privilege用于特权审查、aiR for Case Strategy用于创建叙述和时间线、aiR Assist用于对话式AI辅助，以及最近的Relativity claiR，专为律师设计的对话式AI。从RelativityOne到Relativity aiR的转变强化了Relativity的焦点：AI原生嵌入整个平台、AI代理支持现有工作并开启新工作、围绕AI代理构建更简单体验，以及可扩展性赋能合作伙伴和从业者社区解决新的独特法律挑战。更名反映客户越来越多地将平台用于诉讼之外的一系列数据智能目的。实际上，客户在平台上创建的新事项中超过一半并非用于诉讼。Brown写道，行业已完全进入AI平台时代，法律数据与专门构建的代理能力相结合，以推动更好的结果并扩展法律团队的事项智能。Relativity aiR的AI能力包含在平台当前定价中，因此采用2026定价计划的客户将能访问所有代理工具。
news.bodyHtml:
Perhaps it is only fitting that a product launched in the cloud should be renamed for the atmosphere it occupies.

The e-discovery company Relativity announced today that it has renamed RelativityOne, its cloud-based platform, as Relativity aiR, giving it the name that had previously been assigned to Relativity’s suite of AI and agentic capabilities.

The purpose of the name change, the company said, is to unify the platform and its AI capabilities under one name.

“This name confirms what our community already knows: AI is as transformative a shift as the cloud was years ago, and Relativity has the trusted platform and the experience to lead through it responsibly,” Phil Saunders, the company’s CEO, said in an announcement.

Starting from its founding in 2001, Relativity had long offered only as an on-premises product. In 2017, it introduced RelativityOne as a SaaS alternative. Even though the on-premises product had long been the 800-pound gorilla of e-discovery technology, the cloud platform eventually came to supersede it, to the point where, last year, Saunders announced a 2028 deadline for all new cases to move to RelativityOne.

Meanwhile, Relativity has been introducing a series of generative AI products, starting with its 2023 announcement of Relativity aiR for Review, designed to help users more quickly locate data responsive to a discovery request.

It has since rolled out aiR for Privilege for privilege review, aiR for Case Strategy for creating narratives and timelines, aiR Assist for conversational AI assistance, and, most recently, Relativity claiR, a conversational AI designed specifically for lawyers.

“The shift from RelativityOne to Relativity aiR reinforces where Relativity is focused: AI embedded natively throughout the platform, AI agents supporting the work already performed and opening up new kinds of work, simpler experiences built around AI agents, and extensibility that empowers Relativity’s community of partners and practitioners to solve new and unique legal challenges,” the company said in its announcement.

In a companion blog post, Chris Brown, who was recently named Relativity president after having been its chief product officer since 2018, said that the name change reflects the fact that customers are increasingly using the platform for a range of data intelligence purposes that extend beyond litigation.

In fact, he said, more than half of new matters customers are creating on the platform are not for litigation at all.

“Our industry is now fully entrenched in the era of the AI platform, where legal data is paired with purpose-built agentic capabilities to drive stronger outcomes and expand legal teams’ matter
intelligence,” Brown writes.

“That’s what we’ve been building: a system of record that securely houses your most sensitive and complex data at extraordinary scale, and a system of action that reads deeply into the documents, pairing agents with human judgment to surface insights and turn them into impactful work product.”

Relativity aiR’s AI capabilities are included in the platform’s current pricing, so customers on the 2026 pricing plan will have access to every agentic tool as part of the  platform.

news.titleEn: Parker Poe Clients & Attorneys Build AI Assistants Together to Help Deliver Better Outcomes
news.titleZh: Parker Poe律师与客户携手共建AI助手，助力实现更优法律成果
news.summaryZh: 2026年9月10日，Parker Poe律师事务所在其夏洛特办公室举办了一场仅限受邀者参加的AI工作坊，总法律顾问、法务运营负责人、合规专业人士、企业高管及该所律师分组协作，共同构建并测试AI应用，以应对日常共同挑战。参与者以四至六人小组形式，利用Lega AI Builder Lab平台，探索AI模型、优化提示词并连接相关知识源。工作坊设公司研究、风险披露更新和高管法律简报三个方向，其中高管简报方向吸引了约90%的参与者，旨在将详细法律更新转化为企业领导者易于使用的信息，明确变化内容、对业务的重要性及所需决策或行动。工作坊注重实操，参与者从零开始设计可运行的AI助手，构建可重复、模板化的AI流程，这是将AI从使用推向运营化的桥梁。一位全球化学品公司高级IT主管开发了一款AI应用，通过询问行业、公司规模等数据为高管起草简报，并称该工作坊对构建提示词、比较不同AI模型响应及起草分级简报“超级有帮助”。该活动是Parker Poe“Moments That Matter™”客户体验项目的一部分，旨在强化信任、信心与长期客户关系。目标是将客户对业务的了解与该所法律判断及AI实际应用相结合，消除业务障碍。Lega创始人、现BARBRI创新主管Christian Lang主持活动并评选出三项优胜创新，Parker Poe将代表获胜团队向所选慈善机构捐赠奖金。Parker Poe是全美首批开展此类客户实验室的律所之一，此前与加拿大Fasken律所合作的类似项目案例在2026年SKILLS Law Showcase上荣获最具启发性展示观众奖。
news.bodyHtml:
Sept. 11, 2026 Charlotte, NC – General counsel, legal operations leaders, compliance professionals, business executives, and Parker Poe attorneys sat side by side on September 10 at the firm’s Charlotte office to build and test AI apps addressing challenges that company leaders and attorneys face together every day. Working in small teams, participants explored AI models, refined prompts, and connected relevant knowledge sources to develop practical tools designed to improve collaboration and legal outcomes.

Teams chose from three tracks: company research, risk disclosure updates, and executive legal briefings. The executive briefing track drew approximately 90% of the participants and focused on a common source of friction in the client relationship, translating detailed legal updates into information business leaders can readily use. Clients and attorneys worked together to build assistants that tailored updates on a commercial dispute to different executives, making clear what had changed, why it mattered to the business, and what decisions or actions were needed. The exercise reflected the workshop’s broader purpose, which was about creating a better client experience through the everyday interactions that may never appear on a legal bill but shape the attorney-client relationship, from clearer communication to anticipating what a client needs next.

“The workshop was hands-on and not just presentation slides,” said Zach Porfiris, who is head of legal at Symphonic Distribution, a global music distribution and technology company. “I teamed up with Parker Poe attorneys and other in-house counsel and business leaders to design working AI assistants from scratch. The practical skill goes beyond prompting. It’s building repeatable, templatized AI processes your team can run without you. That’s the bridge between using AI and operationalizing it.”

“I’m excited to bring ideas back to Symphonic as we expand AI-powered contract drafting and lifecycle management, operationalize legal workflows through AI, and develop frameworks considering AI-generated content across our global platform,” Zach added.

One senior IT leader of a global chemicals company who attended the event built an AI app that asks IT managers and directors what industry they belong to, the size of their company, and other relevant data in order to draft briefings for company executives. The workshop was a “super helpful” way to use AI to build the right prompts, compare how different AI models respond to those prompts, and then draft briefs for various levels of company executives so the information they would receive was relevant to them, the IT manager commented after the workshop.

The invitation-only workshop was part of the firm’s Moments That Matter™ client experience program. The program focuses on the interactions that most strongly shape trust, confidence, and long-term client relationships, and it helps create a more consistent and intentional client experience across the firm.

The event was intentionally created to make complex information easier to act on, surface risks sooner, and communicate more clearly, ultimately strengthening how clients and their lawyers work together, said Will Cannon, a Raleigh partner who leads Parker Poe’s Technology Industry Team and provided welcoming remarks for the event.

“Our clients know their businesses and the hurdles that slow their businesses down,” Will said. “Our goal is to combine that knowledge with our legal judgment and practical uses of AI to remove those obstacles. We’re working alongside our clients to build tools that make their work easier and help their businesses move faster.”

Using the Lega AI Builder Lab platform, participants collaborated in groups of four to six people. Christian Lang, the founder of Lega and now head of innovation at BARBRI (which recently acquired Lega), facilitated the event and selected three winning innovations.

“This is not a theoretical exercise,” Christian told the participants during the workshop. “Today we’re using these knowledge sources and data we created. Tomorrow we can be doing things that are directly plugging into your production and other systems. This is the kind of thing that I hope will start to inspire people about what’s possible and what we can do together.”

Parker Poe will donate the prize money for each winning team to a charity of their choice. The three winning teams presented their work informally during a cocktail reception that followed, with guests circulating between them.

Parker Poe is among the first firms in the country to run a client lab of this kind. A similar client AI lab with Fasken in Canada brought lawyers and clients together to build practical AI solutions, and the case study of Lega’s Client AI Lab with Fasken earned the Most Inspiring Showcase Audience Award at the 2026 SKILLS Law Showcase.

“This new technology and the ability to collaborate using AI is exciting because it allows us to provide a better work product for our clients,” said Russell Killen, a partner in the firm’s Raleigh office who leads the Technology Committee. “As lawyers, that’s our goal.”

“When used properly, AI provides lawyers and clients with a better basis for decision-making,” Russell added. “You can take the judgment and experience of a lawyer and the business needs of a client and now you’re able to use this tool to get to better decisions faster. That’s the real benefit of building AI tools together. You’re able to think through complicated problems in a more effective way. That’s good for the clients and the law firms.”

The most important thing to the client is not the technology, said Kristen Bateman Leis, Parker Poe’s chief marketing and business development officer. What they want is predictability, clearer communication, fewer surprises, and a team that knows their business well enough to see what is coming. The technology can help attorneys get to that better client experience and business outcome.

“The relationships that matter are not built at the closing table,” Kristen said. “They are built in the ordinary moments in between, and this was one of them. A client and their lawyer at the same table, building the same thing, deciding together what ‘better’ looks like. That is what the relationship is all about.”

About Parker Poe Adams & Bernstein LLP
Businesses and local governments turn to Parker Poe to structure transactions, navigate regulations, and resolve disputes. Founded in 1884, the Southeast business law firm today has approximately 300 attorneys across offices in North Carolina, South Carolina, Georgia, and Washington, DC.

Parker Poe is a member of two leading international legal networks: TerraLex and the Employment Law Alliance. TerraLex and the ELA have chosen Parker Poe to help guide clients through the challenges of global business.

news.titleEn: 31% of Law Firms Say AI Improves Profitability
news.titleZh: 31%的律所表示AI提升了盈利能力
news.summaryZh:
BigHand的一项新定价调查显示，31%的律所在仔细审查数据后发现，AI“提高了每项业务的盈利能力”。这大概是因为AI有助于减少非计费工作的时间，从而让每个客户项目实现更多利润。此外，在固定收费的业务中，AI加速带来了可观的“技术红利”。同时，30%的律所发现AI有助于推动业务处理量增加，对于能够从更快完成的项目中获益的律所而言，这同样是显著提振。一些律所可能未给出肯定答复，仅仅是因为它们没有追踪回答这些问题所需的数据。

然而，还有其他几个因素为一些律所描绘了更复杂的财务图景：某些任务的可计费工时减少了27%，对人工任务的依赖降低了31%。对于完全固守传统计费小时模式的律所来说，这些数字并不受欢迎。对于能够驾驭AI影响下新定价环境的律所而言，上述情况也是好消息。另一个问题是，即便现在，35%的合伙人仍对与客户讨论AI使用感到“不自在”。但可以理解，当客户可能因律所在其业务中部署AI而要求折扣时——而如今在大多数大型律所使用此类技术已是标准做法。人们也会猜测，采用固定收费并拥抱快速处理量的律所更愿意进行此类讨论。总体而言，这些数据对正在适应变化的律所是好消息，也表明AI如今已真正以有意义的方式嵌入大部分市场。
news.bodyHtml:
A new pricing survey by BigHand shows that 31% of law firms – which had scrutinised their data – found that AI had ‘improved profitability per matter’.

This is presumably because AI is helping to reduce time spent on non-billable work, allowing more profits to be realised for each client project. Plus, where a matter is on a fixed fee AI acceleration provides a healthy ‘tech dividend’.

Also, 30% of firms saw that AI is helping to drive increased matter throughput – again a notable boost to firms that are able to benefit from more rapidly completed projects.

However, there are several other factors here that paint a more complex financial scenario for some law firms:

  • There was also a reduction in billable hours for certain tasks – 27%
  • And a reduced reliance on manual tasks – 31%

For firms that are wholly wedded to the traditional billable hour model, then such figures are not that welcome. For those that can navigate the new AI-influenced pricing environment, then the above is also good news.

As AL has said before, the key to law firm success with AI is primarily around getting the business model right for a world where efficiency is now a core element of the end product for the client. You can either work with this new reality and reap the rewards, or stick to the former, primarily time-based approach and struggle to make AI as profitable as it could be.

— Advertisement —

—

One other wrinkle is that even now, 35% of partners were ‘uncomfortable’ discussing AI use with clients. But, one can understand that when clients might be asking for discounts because of AI deployment on their matters – at a time when using such technology across most large firms is now standard. One would also guess that firms using fixed fees and embracing rapid throughput are more open to such discussions.

Overall, the data is good news for law firms that are adapting and also shows that AI is now truly embedded in a meaningful way across much of the market.

You can find the report here.

—

news.titleEn: Clio Hires Bridget Mary McCormack
news.titleZh: Clio聘请布里奇特·玛丽·麦科马克
news.summaryZh: Clio已聘请前密歇根州最高法院首席大法官布里奇特·玛丽·麦科马克。她最近担任美国仲裁协会首席执行官，期间推动法律AI的应用。她将以总经理（司法）身份加入Clio，据称此举将加强Clio向法院扩张背后的领导团队。此前不久，Clio刚聘请帕布罗·阿雷东多担任高级副总裁（司法），他是Casetext的前联合创始人，该公司已被汤森路透收购。这两项任命都是Clio更加关注“在法院、司法官员和争议解决组织合作伙伴中实现增长”的一部分。其以显著的规模和广泛的法律基础进入法院；收购vLex为平台增加了权威研究、判例法、案卷和法院记录，该平台被130多个国家的40多万法律专业人士使用。司法机构是加强法律体系运作的最大机会之一，他们正以长期雄心为此建设；布里奇特对这个市场的理解达到了极少数人才能达到的水平，她领导过法院，在司法系统中工作过，知道如何赢得他们想要服务的机构的信任。数百万人在利害关系最大的时刻依赖法院，却往往没有有意义的法律支持；现在的机会是给这些机构更好的工具来履行这一责任。
news.bodyHtml:
Clio has hired Bridget Mary McCormack, a former Michigan Supreme Court Chief Justice, and most recently CEO of the American Arbitration Association (AAA), where she spearheaded a drive toward legal AI adoption.

She will join the legal tech company as General Manager, Judiciary, strengthening the leadership team behind Clio’s expansion into the courts, they said.

The move follows swiftly on from the hire of Pablo Arredondo as Senior Vice President, Judiciary, who is the former co-founder of Casetext, which was bought by Thomson Reuters.

Both moves are part of an increased focus on ‘growth across courts, judicial officers, and dispute resolution organizational partners’. To which end they noted that ‘Clio enters the courts with significant scale and a broad legal foundation. Its acquisition of vLex added authoritative research, case law, dockets, and court records to a platform used by more than 400,000 legal professionals in over 130 countries.’

Jack Newton, CEO and Founder of Clio, commented: ‘The judiciary represents one of the largest opportunities to strengthen how the legal system works, and we are building for it with long term ambition.

‘Bridget understands this market at a level very few people do. She has led courts, worked across the justice system, and knows what it takes to earn the confidence of the institutions we want to serve. This is part of a much bigger vision for Clio to help shape the infrastructure of modern legal work, across the profession and the institutions that support it.’

McCormack concluded: ‘Millions of people rely on courts at moments when the stakes are highest, often without meaningful legal support. The opportunity now is to give those institutions better tools to meet that responsibility. If we do this well, the impact won’t be about efficiency. It will be the strengthening of the public justice system’s service to the people who depend on it, and the corresponding growth in public trust.’

Is this a big deal?

Well, it’s not every day you hire a former judge – or the head of the AAA, so this is indeed a big move. And as noted above, Clio is set on expanding into the judiciary field, so the new hire and that of Arredondo are significant steps towards accomplishing this goal.

news.titleEn: Salesforce Rolls Out Legora For Legal Function
news.titleZh: Salesforce为其法务部门部署Legora
news.summaryZh: Legora已被Salesforce选中，为其遍布美国、欧洲和亚太地区的法务团队提供服务。此举值得关注，因为Salesforce一直公开表示其内部自行开发了许多法律科技应用，并曾在Legal Innovators California上谈及此事。AI正在重塑法律团队的运作方式，借助Slack和Agentforce，Salesforce正在构建一个AI原生、信任优先的法务部门，使团队能够更高效地工作，将时间集中在影响最大的地方。将Legora加入其转型组合，为团队提供了额外的法律工具，以支持研究、起草和其他工作流程，从而让他们能花更多时间在需要专业知识和判断力的工作上。Salesforce决定采用Legora反映了内部法律团队拥抱代理式AI的更广泛转变，这是他们运行全面法律工作流程所依赖的关键基础设施的一部分。对于一家一直以利用自身技术和AI能力为法务团队进行建设而自豪的公司来说，在全球范围内部署Legora——后者必然提供了许多他们已经设计的相同‘技能’——对这家总部位于斯德哥尔摩的公司来说是一次成功。此外，Salesforce规模庞大，与数千家其他公司有联系，因此这对Legora来说是一个坚实的胜利。
news.bodyHtml:
AL doesn’t usually do client wins, but this one is worth a mention. Legora has been picked by Salesforce for its legal teams across the US, Europe and APAC. It’s noteworthy as Salesforce has been vocal about building many of its own legal tech applications for internal use. In fact, they talked about this at Legal Innovators California.

Erica Swainson, VP, Legal Innovation & Strategic Initiatives, Salesforce, commented: ‘AI is reshaping how legal teams operate, and with Slack and Agentforce we’re building an AI-native, trust-first legal function that empowers our team to work more efficiently and focus their time where it can have the greatest impact.

‘Adding Legora to our transformation portfolio gives our team additional legal tools to support research, drafting, and other workflows, so they can spend more time on the work that requires their expertise and judgment.’

And, Max Junestrand, CEO and Co-Founder of Legora, added: ‘Salesforce’s decision to adopt Legora reflects a broader shift in how in-house legal teams are embracing agentic AI. It’s part of the critical infrastructure they depend on to run comprehensive legal workflows.’

Is this a big deal?

Well, as mentioned, for a company that has taken great pride in leveraging its own tech and AI capabilities to build for its legal team, the fact they’re doing a global roll out of Legora – which must be offering many of the same ‘skills’ they’ve already designed for – is a coup for the Stockholm-based company. Plus, Salesforce is huge – and connects to 1,000s of other companies. So, a solid win for them here.

—

Legal Innovators Conferences London and New York this November

Come and join us in London this November 4th + 5th at Legal Innovators. The conference at the intersection of legal AI and the business of law. Day One: law firms, Day Two: inhouse.

Legal Innovators UK – London, Nov 4 and 5

And,

Legal Innovators New York – Nov 17 and 18

See you at Legal Innovators New York – Nov 17 and 18 – join us at the intersection of legal AI and the business of law in New York for the most important legal innovation event of the year! Day One: law firms, Day Two: inhouse. Top speakers from across the legal AI world, leading law firms, and major companies. All for one purpose: to describe and explore the frontier of legal technology. See you there!

  • Legal Innovators UK – London, Nov 4 and 5
  • Legal Innovators New York – Nov 17 and 18

news.titleEn: One Plus One Equals More Than Two: Clio Lands McCormack to Join Arredondo in Judiciary Expansion
news.titleZh: 一加一大于二：Clio 聘请 McCormack 与 Arredondo 共同推进司法领域扩张
news.summaryZh: Bridget M. McCormack 的去向已确定。她现任美国仲裁协会总裁兼首席执行官，曾任密歇根州最高法院首席大法官。她此前表示新机会“无法拒绝”，并暗示涉及“专注于法官的构建机会”。两周前，Clio 宣布开发面向法官的技术，并聘请 Casetext 联合创始人 Pablo Arredondo 担任司法业务高级副总裁。今日 Clio 正式宣布聘请 McCormack 担任司法业务总经理，帮助构建法院技术的未来。Clio 通过这两项招聘推动法院业务扩张。McCormack 在司法系统创新方面的经历可追溯至其担任密歇根州首席大法官期间，并在美国仲裁协会推动 AI 采用及开发 AI Arbitrator 等产品。Arredondo 曾领导 Casetext 开发包括首个 GPT-4 AI 法律助手 CoCounsel 在内的产品，Thomson Reuters 于 2023 年以 6.5 亿美元收购 Casetext。司法领域是加强法律体系运作的最大机会之一，Clio 正以长期雄心为此构建，McCormack 对该市场的理解很少有人能及，她领导过法院、在司法系统中工作过，知道如何赢得目标机构的信任。McCormack 将于 10 月开始在 Clio 工作，负责领导司法业务的市场与商业战略，直接向 Newton 汇报。Arredondo 将领导司法部门的产品开发与战略方向，向 Clio 首席产品官 John Foreman 汇报。Clio 进军法院技术开发正值司法领域的关键时刻。
news.bodyHtml:
The mystery of Bridget M. McCormack’s destination has been solved.

Last week, I reported that McCormack, current president and CEO of the American Arbitration Association and former chief justice of the Michigan Supreme Court, was leaving her job for an undisclosed opportunity that, as she said at the time, “I could not turn down,” teasing only that it involved “the chance to build something focused specifically on judges.”

The timing seemed telling, as I noted then. Just two weeks earlier, Clio had announced its move into developing technology for judges and its hiring of Casetext cofounder Pablo Arredondo as senior vice president, judiciary, to lead that effort. Could her announcement, so soon after, be mere coincidence?

Turns out, it was not. Today, Clio made it official, announcing that it has recruited McCormack to join the company as general manager, judiciary, “to help build the future of court technology.”

Clio’s dual hirings of McCormack and Arredondo to drive its expansion into the courts is one of those situations where one plus one adds up to a whole lot more than two.

McCormack’s track record on justice-system innovation traces back to her time as chief justice in Michigan and carries through to her tenure at the AAA, where she spearheaded its adoption of AI and its development of products such as the AI Arbitrator. (Listen: An AI Arbitrator? The Latest Innovations from the American Arbitration Association, with CEO Bridget McCormack and CTO Diana Didia.)

Arredondo, who led Casetext’s development of a strong of innovative products, including CoCounsel, the first GPT-4 AI legal assistant, first turned his attention to the challenges facing the judiciary while at Thomson Reuters, which acquired Casetext for $650 million in 2023. (Listen: Why Legal AI Pioneer Pablo Arredondo Is Joining Clio to Build Technology for the Courts.)

“The judiciary represents one of the largest opportunities to strengthen how the legal system works, and we are building for it with long term ambition,” said Jack Newton, Clio’s CEO and founder.

“Bridget understands this market at a level very few people do. She has led courts, worked across the justice system, and knows what it takes to earn the confidence of the institutions we want to serve.”

Leading Market Strategy

When McCormack begins working at Clio in October, her role will be to lead the market and commercial strategy for Clio’s judiciary business. She will report directly to Newton.

Arredondo will lead product development and strategic direction for the judicial division. He will report to Clio’s chief product officer John Foreman.

Clio’s push into developing technology for the courts comes at a critical time for the judiciary.

For decades, courts have been suffocating under the pressure of weightier and weightier caseloads and inadequate funding for the staff and technology to manage those caseloads.

Driving those caseloads has been the steady increase in the numbers of self-represented litigants (SRLs), who, according to a 2018 study, make up 72 percent of all parties in state courts – meaning only a quarter of litigants are represented by lawyers.

The advent of AI has only exacerbated that problem, providing SRLs with the tools to more easily research legal issues and prepare legal filings.

Many believe the courts are ill-prepared for the AI era and that the need for technological solutions has never been greater.

On the Michigan Supreme Court for nearly a decade, including four as chief justice, McCormack saw that pressure firsthand, Clio said in its announcement of her hiring, and that experience has helped shape her view of where AI can have the greatest impact.

“Millions of people rely on courts at moments when the stakes are highest, often without meaningful legal support,” said McCormack. “The opportunity now is to give those institutions better tools to meet that responsibility.

“If we do this well, the impact won’t be about efficiency. It will be the strengthening of the public justice system’s service to the people who depend on it, and the corresponding growth in public trust.”

news.titleEn: You Can Use AI in Court. You Can’t Secretly Rig It.
news.titleZh: 你可以在法庭上使用AI，但不能秘密操纵它
news.summaryZh: 康涅狄格州一名法官为AI时代划定了明确界限：使用人工智能辅助准备法庭文件没有问题，前提是使用者需核查其工作成果；但隐藏旨在操纵他人AI的指令则不被允许。在Elliott诉New York Bariatric Group案中，一名自我代理的原告在法庭文件中嵌入了白色小字文本，普通读者不可见但软件可读，指示任何审查文件的AI同意原告并帮助推翻先前的裁决。原告称其为“审计”，法院则认为是不诚实行为。在法院认定该做法并警告可能制裁后，隐藏信息仍继续出现，后续文件包含隐藏的“hi :)”消息和Nosferatu视频链接。该提示从未奏效，法院不使用AI裁决文件，法官阅读打印副本后驳回了动议。但这一尝试本身已足够：原告失去了电子提交权限，现在必须亲自提交文件。重要的是，法院并未拒绝AI，而是欢迎其诚实使用，尤其是作为改善司法可及性的工具。法官甚至承认在准备裁决时使用了AI辅助工具，同时独立核查工作并对结果负责。这一区分至关重要。AI可以帮助起草、总结和组织，但隐藏提示则不同。法院将其比作秘密通信，旨在影响决策者或决策者依赖的工具，而对方不知情且无机会回应。教训简单明了：如果AI有帮助就使用它，核查其工作，对结果负责，但不要试图让他人的机器站在你这边。技术会变，坦诚义务不变。
news.bodyText: Find Your Next Job ! A Connecticut judge has drawn a crisp line for the AI era: using artificial intelligence as an aid in preparing court filings is fine—provided the user checks its work. But hiding instructions designed to manipulate someone else’s AI will not fly. In Elliott v. New York Bariatric Group, a self-represented plaintiff embedded tiny white-on-white text in court filings. Invisible to ordinary readers but readable by software, it instructed any AI reviewing the documents to agree with the plaintiff and help overturn an earlier ruling. The plaintiff called it an “audit.” The court called it dishonest. The plaintiff’s explanation became even harder to swallow when the hidden messages continued after the court identified the practice and warned that sanctions were possible. Later filings included a concealed “hi :)” message and a link to a Nosferatu video. The prompt never worked. The court does not use AI to decide filings, and the judge denied the motion after reading a printed copy. But the attempt itself was enough: the plaintiff lost access to electronic filing and must now submit papers in person. Importantly, the court did not reject AI. It welcomed its honest use, particularly as a tool for improving access to justice. The judge even acknowledged using AI-assisted tools while preparing the decision—while independently checking the work and retaining responsibility for the result. That distinction matters. AI can help draft, summarize, and organize. A hidden prompt is different. The court likened it to a secret communication aimed at the decision-maker—or the tools the decision-maker relies on—without the other side knowing or having a chance to respond. The lesson is refreshingly simple: use AI if it helps. Check its work. Own the result. But don’t try to make someone else’s machine take your side. Technology changes. The duty of candor does not.
news.relevanceReason: 该文章的核心主题是法院对在法庭文件中使用AI的裁决，涉及AI在司法程序中的使用边界、诚实义务以及法院对AI辅助工具的立场，属于法律AI或法律技术范畴。

news.titleEn: Checkbox Launches ‘First Pass’ AI Contract Review
news.titleZh: Checkbox推出‘First Pass’AI合同审查功能
news.summaryZh: Checkbox作为面向企业的法律前台，推出First Pass，首次对合同内容进行实质性AI审查，依据企业自有操作手册评分，而非仅路由和跟踪，标志着其进入合同审查领域。该上下文感知AI代理可审查合同、发票和传入的法律请求，减少常规工作，并将需关注事项路由至正确位置，甚至可分配给法律团队中工作量最轻的人。其理念是让合同等文本输入中的数据被First Pass利用，将智能向上游移动。Checkbox不试图取代CLM，First Pass是“第一遍阅读”，当合同到达现有工具时，常规工作已完成，真正问题已被标记。此举因法律团队被大量合同、发票和请求淹没，而CLM和电子账单平台仅在事项进入系统后管理，不提前过滤或分流。今年1月，Checkbox完成2300万美元A轮融资，联合创始人兼首席产品官James Han表示，融资将推动为法律工作构建智能系统，把日常请求转化为机构专业知识，助团队更快行动、更一致并减少对外部律师依赖。
news.bodyText: Checkbox, a legal front door for corporates, has launched First Pass, marking a move into contract review – and which builds upon its platform for inhouse teams. (See AL interview with Evan Wong, CEO, below.) The company said that this new capability will entail a ‘context-aware AI agent that reviews contracts, invoices, and incoming legal requests, to reduce routine work and route what needs attention to the right place’. They added that the idea is that all the data embedded in contracts and other text-based inputs into a legal team can be harnessed by First Pass, which moves that intelligence ‘upstream’. One nifty feature that AL noted is that as requests are analysed by the AI, matters can be sent to ‘whoever has the lightest workload’ on the legal team. In terms of the details of how it will operate, they explained: It’s worth adding that in January this year they raised a Series A round of $23m. At that time, James Han, Co-Founder and Chief Product Officer at Checkbox, commented: ‘The Series A funding will fuel Checkbox’s vision to build a system of intelligence for legal work, turning everyday requests into institutional expertise. This institutional expertise can then be leveraged by AI to help teams move faster, deliver more consistent work, and reduce dependency on outside counsel.’ — And now the AL interview with CEO, Evan Wong. Contract review for Checkbox is totally new? Yes, First Pass is the first time Checkbox is doing substantive AI review of contract content – scoring it against your own playbook – rather than just routing and tracking it.We’re not trying to replace anyone’s CLM. First Pass is exactly what it sounds like – the first read. By the time a contract reaches the tools legal teams already run, the routine work is done and the real questions are flagged. Why now? Legal teams are buried in contract, invoice, and request volume. CLM and e-billing platforms manage work once it’s already in the system – they don’t filter or deflect it before it reaches a lawyer. Nobody was working on the moment it arrived – partly because it’s unglamorous, partly because until recently you couldn’t automate a first read without creating more work than it saved. Both of those changed. First Pass moves that intelligence upstream.
news.relevanceReason: 该文章主要介绍Checkbox推出的AI合同审查功能First Pass，属于法律AI产品发布，核心主题是AI在法律工作流程中的应用。

news.titleEn: Law Firm Workflow Automation: From Court Docket to Case Task
news.titleZh: 律所工作流自动化：从法院案卷到案件任务
news.summaryZh:
法院和案卷数据应转化为人身伤害律所的工作流，因为截止日期不是需要留意的信息，而是由指定人员在指定日期完成的工作。当案卷条目在案件档案内转化为任务、事件和通知时，工作得以完成；否则只会被报告。人身伤害诉讼不是任务清单，而是一连串依赖关系，法院截止日期是其中一环，而非日历上的一条线。律所工作流自动化并非取代判断，而是确保下一步行动存在、被分配且可见。法律技术市场已开始反映这一点，近期发展将法院和案卷信息更直接地连接到诉讼工作流。

工作流自动化是定义案件中发生某事时应采取的行动，然后由案件管理软件按规则执行，而非依赖人员记忆。截止日期输入后，准备任务出现并带有负责人和日期；阶段变化时，下一组行动被分配；文件到达时，正确人员收到通知。这不是AI对案件做决定，而是律所一次性定义流程，软件每次以相同方式运行，判断权留给律师，记忆移至系统。案卷数据应直线连接法院与执行工作的人员，无系统间遗漏。步骤包括：监控案卷并捕获条目，将其日期和要求归档至事项而非收件箱；计算截止日期并输入案件日历，包括从法院日期倒推的内部截止日期；按规则为每项工作创建任务，各有负责人和到期日；日历事件发送给相关人员；团队在事项中查看状态。
news.bodyHtml:
Court and docket data should become workflow in a personal injury firm because a deadline is not information to be noted. It is work to be done, by named people, by a date. When a docket entry becomes a task, an event, and a notification inside the case file, the work gets done. Elsewhere, it gets reported on. 

Key takeaways 

  • PI litigation is not a task list. It is a chain of dependencies, and a court deadline is a link in that chain, not a line on a calendar. 
  • A deadline recorded somewhere other than where the work happens is a deadline someone has to remember to look for. 
  • Law firm workflow automation is not about replacing judgment. It is about making sure the next action exists, is assigned, and is visible. 
  • The test of any calendaring approach is simple: when a filing lands, does something happen, or does someone have to notice? 

Why should court and docket data become workflow in a personal injury firm? 

Because every docket entry implies work. A scheduling order sets deadlines that each need a task, an owner, and a date. An opposing filing needs a response, and a response needs research, drafting, review, and filing, each with its own deadline counted back from the court’s. Recording the docket entry is not the job. Turning it into the work it implies, inside the case where that work will be done, is the job. 

The legal technology market has started to reflect this. Recent developments have connected court and docket information more directly to litigation workflows, on the premise that a deadline and the work it triggers belong together. That premise is right, and personal injury firms, with long cases and unforgiving statutes, have more riding on it than most. 

PI litigation is not a task list. It is a chain where the demand depends on the chronology, the chronology depends on the records, and the motion depends on the deadline the court set. When the software tracking that work and the people doing it sit apart, you get status reporting instead of execution. Docket data becoming workflow is the plainest example of the alternative. 

What is law firm workflow automation? 

Law firm workflow automation is the practice of defining what should happen when something occurs in a case, then having the case management software carry it out by rule rather than relying on someone to remember. A deadline is entered, and the preparatory tasks appear with owners and dates. A stage changes, and the next set of actions is assigned. A document arrives, and the right person is notified. 

It is worth being precise about what this is and is not. It is not AI making decisions about a case. It is the firm deciding, once, how its process should run, and the software running it the same way every time. The judgment stays with the attorney. The remembering moves to the system. 

How should docket data connect to case workflow? 

In a straight line from the court to the person doing the work, with nothing falling into a gap between systems. The sequence that holds up in practice: 

  • The docket is monitored and the entry is captured, with its date and what it requires, and filed to the matter rather than to an inbox. 
  • The deadline is calculated and entered on the case calendar, including the internal deadlines counted back from the court date. 
  • Tasks are created by rule for each piece of work the deadline implies, each with an owner and a due date. 
  • Calendar events go to the people involved, so the hearing, the deposition, or the filing date is on their schedule as well as the case’s. 
  • The team sees the status in the matter: what is due, who owns it, what is done. Nobody has to ask, and nobody has to remember to check. 

Every step in that sequence happens inside the case. That is the point. The docket entry starts as court data and ends as a completed task in the matter, and it never had to cross into a separate system where it could be overlooked.

policy.titleEn: 最高人民法院发布人民法院网络法治典型案例
policy.titleZh: 最高人民法院发布人民法院网络法治典型案例
policy.summaryZh: 2026年9月14日至20日国家网络安全宣传周期间，最高人民法院于9月16日发布人民法院网络法治典型案例，共4件。案例涉及网络暴力情形下人格权侵害禁令适用、带货主播侵害他人人格权责任认定、搜索引擎服务提供者侵权责任认定、为跨境赌博提供网络技术支持服务的定罪量刑。案例一明确适用人格权侵害禁令应综合考量侵权行为方式、信息传播速度和范围、损害是否难以弥补及禁令措施限度等因素，长春新区人民法院裁定侵权人停止侵害，禁令有效期6个月。案例二明确带货主播受电子商务经营者委托推广商品时故意使用侵害他人人格权素材构成侵权，委托人未尽审核义务存在过失的构成共同侵权，北京互联网法院判决某文化公司赔礼道歉并赔偿12万元。案例三明确使用检索增强生成技术的搜索引擎服务提供者应承担与算法、数据优势相匹配的注意义务，对算法合规负更重证明责任，未主动上传、编辑、推荐信息且知悉侵权后及时处理的，不构成侵权，上海知识产权法院二审维持驳回全部诉讼请求。案例四明确明知跨境赌博集团仍提供软件开发、技术支持等服务的构成开设赌场共同犯罪，重庆市第五中级人民法院二审维持原判。
policy.bodyText:
网络生态治理是网络强国建设的重要任务，事关国家发展和安全，事关人民群众切身利益。习近平总书记多次强调，要健全网络生态治理长效机制，持续营造风清气正的网络空间。网络法治是网络强国建设的重要保障，司法审判是网络法治实施体系的重要方面。近年来，人民法院深入学习贯彻习近平法治思想和习近平总书记关于网络强国的重要思想，坚持为大局服务、为人民司法，依法惩治电信网络诈骗、网络暴力等违法犯罪，依法审理涉人工智能、数据权益、网络虚拟财产等新类型案件，有力保障网络空间各类主体合法权益，积极融入和促推网络空间安全综合治理，携手有关部门做实“抓前端、治未病”，提升网络领域矛盾纠纷预防化解能力，依法惩治网络违法犯罪，助力提升网络空间法治化水平。
2026年9月14日至20日是国家网络安全宣传周，本届宣传周主题为“网络安全为人民，网络安全靠人民——智能时代 网安护航”。为认真贯彻落实党中央部署要求，进一步发挥司法裁判的示范引领作用，配合做好网络安全法治宣传，9月16日，最高人民法院发布人民法院网络法治典型案例。此次发布的4件典型案例，涉及发生网络暴力时的人格权侵害禁令适用、带货主播侵害他人人格权的责任认定、搜索引擎服务提供者的侵权责任认定、为跨境赌博提供网络技术支持服务的定罪量刑等内容，彰显了人民法院依法惩治网络违法犯罪、处理涉网矛盾纠纷，维护人民群众合法权益、维护网络空间秩序、促进数字经济健康有序发展的坚定立场和工作成效。
下一步，人民法院将深入贯彻习近平法治思想和习近平总书记关于网络强国的重要思想，进一步提升涉网案件审判工作质效，结合审判实践强化网络法治调研，以严格公正司法护航网络生态治理，为网络强国、数字中国建设提供高质量司法服务和保障。

【案例一】明确适用人格权侵害禁令的考量因素，及时有效遏制网络暴力——李某申请人格权侵害禁令案
【基本案情】
李某与张某、胡某均为短视频平台自媒体博主，张某、胡某的网络账号共计有超2000万粉丝。2023年7月起，张某以李某“插足”其与男友情感为由，在网络平台公开发布针对李某的侮辱、诽谤言论，并联合胡某炒作相关话题，煽动粉丝对李某实施谩骂、攻击、举报等网络暴力行为。事件发生后，李某的部分商业合作方解除与李某的合作协议。2023年10月，李某提起名誉权侵权诉讼。案件审理过程中，张某、胡某仍煽动粉丝实施上述网络暴力行为。2024年3月，李某向人民法院申请人格权侵害禁令，请求责令张某、胡某立即停止在全平台社交媒体发布、传播侵害其名誉权的内容。
【裁判结果】
吉林省长春新区人民法院经审查认为，张某、胡某对李某实施了群体性网络暴力违法行为，且在案件审理过程中仍继续实施上述网络暴力行为、扩大损害结果。张某、胡某通过直播等形式在网络上传播侵权信息，案涉信息传播速度快、波及范围广、负面影响大，已对李某造成精神损害和经济损失，不及时制止将导致李某合法权益受到难以弥补的损害，符合人格权侵害禁令的适用条件。吉林省长春新区人民法院依法裁定张某、胡某立即停止侵权行为，禁令有效期限为6个月；如违反禁令，法院将依法视情节轻重予以罚款、拘留；构成犯罪的，依法追究刑事责任。
【典型意义】
网络文明是新形势下社会文明的重要内容，是建设网络强国的重要领域。网络暴力行为传播速度快、影响范围广、损害不可逆甚至造成难以弥补的后果，严重影响社会公众安全感。民法典第九百九十七条规定了人格权侵害禁令条款，目的是及时制止人格权侵权、防止损害发生和扩大。《最高人民法院关于依法审理涉人工智能纠纷案件的意见》亦对依法适用人格权侵害禁令制度作出规范。司法实践反映，人格权侵害禁令条款的适用条件，特别是“不及时制止将使其合法权益受到难以弥补的损害”不好把握，有必要进一步细化明确适用的考量因素。本案例明确，对于网络暴力情形下适用人格权侵害禁令的审查，应当综合考量侵权行为方式、信息传播速度和范围等因素，判断是否达到需要及时制止的紧迫性标准；综合考量被侵害人格权类型、侵害行为性质、事后赔偿等救济手段是否能够充分弥补申请人的损害等因素，审查损害是否难以弥补；综合考量被侵害人格权类型、侵权行为方式以及损害范围、程度等因素，裁定采取相应禁令措施，防止超出必要限度。本案中，网络自媒体博主在社交平台、直播间侮辱诽谤他人，煽动粉丝实施网暴行为。该侵权行为具有持续性，且张某、胡某二人粉丝量超2000万，案涉侵权信息传播速度快、波及范围广，已导致李某社会评价降低、商业利益受损，制止该侵权行为具有紧迫性，如不及时制止，受害人将面临难以弥补的损害，故人民法院认为本案符合人格权侵害禁令适用条件，依法予以支持。本案的处理，有利于及时制止人格权侵害行为，防止损害后果扩大蔓延，有效遏制恶意炒作、煽动网络暴力等乱象，对规范网络言行、净化网络空间、维护网络秩序具有规范引领意义。
【案例二】明确带货主播侵害他人人格权的责任认定规则，强化网络空间人格权益保护——李某瑾诉某文化公司网络侵权责任纠纷案
【基本案情】
2024年，某文化公司为推广销售家庭育儿类图书，与某带货主播订立协议，委托带货主播制作并发布短视频为其店铺进行网络宣传。该协议约定，带货主播发布的视频侵犯第三方合法权益的，委托方某文化公司应当承担责任。随后，前述带货主播在某网络平台的个人账号发布了多个宣传视频，使用了李某瑾公开演讲、授课的视频片段，并配以与李某瑾声音在音色、语调、发音风格上高度近似的AI合成音频。用户点击宣传视频一侧的按钮，可以直接跳转至某文化公司网络店铺购买相关图书。经查，案涉视频中的相关素材并未取得李某瑾的授权，某文化公司对案涉视频的素材来源、授权材料等未进行审核。李某瑾向法院提起诉讼，请求判令某文化公司赔礼道歉、赔偿经济损失及合理开支25万元。
【裁判结果】
北京互联网法院经审理认为，案涉视频未经李某瑾同意，擅自使用李某瑾肖像并结合使用与其声纹特征高度吻合的AI合成声音，案涉行为构成对李某瑾肖像权和声音权益的侵害。某文化公司未对视频素材的来源、视频素材是否获得李某瑾授权等事项进行审核，存在未尽合理审核义务的过失，构成共同侵权。2025年7月18日，北京互联网法院判决某文化公司向李某瑾赔礼道歉、赔偿经济损失及维权合理支出12万元。宣判后，双方当事人均未提起上诉，判决已发生法律效力。
【典型意义】
强化网络空间人格权益保护，是加强网络生态治理、营造清朗网络空间的重要内容。当前，带货主播擅自使用他人肖像、AI合成声音等实施“仿冒名人带货”的商业推广行为时有发生，破坏网络生态环境，侵害他人人格权益，应当依法予以规制。本案例明确，带货主播受电子商务经营者委托，通过制作发布视频等方式进行商品推广时，故意使用侵害他人人格权等权益的素材的，构成侵权；委托人电子商务经营者对宣传推广内容未尽到法律规定或者合同约定的审核义务，对损害结果发生存在过失的，与带货主播成立共同侵权，应依法承担连带责任。本案中，某文化公司与带货主播形成委托关系，案涉协议明确了某文化公司对推广内容的审核责任和管理权限。在案涉视频明显、大量使用知名人士李某瑾肖像和高度仿真的AI合成声音，侵权风险显而易见的情况下，某文化公司未对视频素材来源、视频素材是否获得李某瑾授权等事项进行审核，存在未尽合理审核义务的过失。该过失与带货主播的侵权故意相结合，共同造成了损害后果，应当认定构成共同侵权。本案的处理，有效规制“仿冒名人带货”违法行为，依法保护网络空间人格权益，促推电子商务经营者对宣传推广内容切实履行审核义务，进一步推进网络生态治理法治化。
【案例三】厘清搜索引擎服务提供者的侵权责任边界，平衡技术创新与权利保护——某文化公司诉某网络科技公司侵害作品信息网络传播权纠纷案
【基本案情】
某网络科技公司基于某大语言模型（已通过国家网信办的生成合成类算法备案），使用检索增强生成技术（使用外部知识源对搜索结果进行补充完善，以提供精准搜索服务）开发并运营某AI搜索引擎平台。某文化公司享有《某兵》《某花》两部电视剧的信息网络传播权。2024年11月28日，某文化公司在案涉搜索引擎平台分别搜索上述两部电视剧，首位搜索结果是第三方网盘分享链接，链接提供的视频内容与两部电视剧内容一致。2024年12月5日，某文化公司向某网络科技公司提出下架搜索结果等要求，某网络科技公司当日即删除了案涉搜索结果。某文化公司向法院起诉，请求判令某网络科技公司赔偿经济损失。
【裁判结果】
上海市徐汇区人民法院经审理认为，案涉网盘分享链接侵害了某文化公司对《某兵》《某花》两部电视剧的信息网络传播权，但某网络科技公司作为某AI搜索引擎平台的网络服务提供者，未主动上传案涉侵权视频的网盘分享链接，不构成直接侵权。由于某AI搜索引擎平台展示的是源自公共互联网网页的内容，在现阶段现有技术无法自动识别侵权信息，且某网络科技公司已履行模型算法的备案义务，在获悉侵权信息后及时作出有效处理，尽到了注意义务，亦不构成帮助侵权。2025年7月1日，上海市徐汇区人民法院判决驳回某文化公司全部诉讼请求。宣判后，某文化公司不服，提起上诉。2025年12月25日，上海知识产权法院作出二审判决，驳回上诉，维持原判。
【典型意义】
人工智能、大数据等新技术新应用不断涌现，给网络生态治理带来新挑战。人民法院依法办理涉新技术应用案件，既依法规范技术应用，也尊重技术发展规律，依法支持技术迭代发展，为数智化转型提供司法保障。本案是一起厘清使用检索增强生成技术的搜索引擎服务提供者侵权责任边界的典型案例。民法典第一千一百九十七条规定：“网络服务提供者知道或者应当知道网络用户利用其网络服务侵害他人民事权益，未采取必要措施的，与该网络用户承担连带责任。”《最高人民法院关于审理侵害信息网络传播权民事纠纷案件适用法律若干问题的规定》细化了认定网络服务提供者对网络用户侵害信息网络传播权的情形是否“明知或者应知”的考量因素。与一般搜索引擎的网络服务不同，使用检索增强生成技术的搜索引擎服务的检索结果精准性、个性化更强，人民法院在适用上述法律规定认定网络服务提供者侵权责任时应当考虑技术特点、服务模式、检索结果生成过程等因素。本案例明确，搜索引擎服务提供者应当依法承担与其算法、数据优势程度相匹配的注意义务，对检索增强生成技术的算法合规负有更重的证明责任；检索信息来源于互联网，搜索引擎服务提供者未主动上传、编辑、推荐该信息，不符合明知或者应知的主观状态，且在知悉侵权信息后及时作出有效处理的，不具有侵权过错，不构成侵权。本案的处理，有利于实现著作权人、技术创新者、社会公共利益三者之间的利益平衡，推动形成支持和规范网络领域科技创新的法治环境。
【案例四】依法惩处为跨境赌博提供技术支持服务的犯罪，维护网络空间安全——黄某等人开设赌场案
【基本案情】
菲律宾某跨境赌博集团开发、运营了14个赌博网站、6个第四方支付平台，组织、招揽我国公民参与网络赌博。2016年至2020年，被告人黄某等人根据菲律宾某跨境赌博集团安排，在中国成立某软件科技公司，为该赌博集团提供技术支持服务，包括网络赌博软件开发、编写服务器代码、对服务器和域名进行管理、维护赌博平台等。经查，黄某等人违法所得共计1216万余元。
【裁判结果】
重庆市綦江区人民法院经审理认为，被告人黄某等人根据赌博犯罪集团安排，为赌博犯罪活动提供软件开发等技术支持服务，构成开设赌场罪，判处黄某等人有期徒刑五年六个月至六个月不等，并处罚金。宣判后，部分被告人提出上诉，2023年12月6日，重庆市第五中级人民法院作出二审裁定，驳回上诉，维持原判。
【典型意义】
党中央高度重视打击治理跨境赌博犯罪。当前，技术供应链降低了赌博网站开发和运营成本，跨境赌博犯罪存在网络化趋势，人民群众对此深恶痛绝。本案即为人民法院依法严惩为跨境赌博提供技术支持犯罪的典型案例。本案中，被告人黄某等人根据赌博犯罪集团安排，组建网络赌博技术供应链团队，开发架构复杂、功能齐全的软件，为跨境赌博集团运营的赌博网站、支付平台提供技术支持服务，与跨境赌博集团事先通谋并形成了较为稳定的配合关系，人民法院依法认定被告人黄某等人构成开设赌场罪。本案例明确，行为人明知是跨境赌博集团，仍根据其安排提供软件开发、技术支持等服务的，构成开设赌场的共同犯罪，彰显了人民法院全方位全链条打击跨境赌博犯罪的鲜明立场，以严格公正司法助力营造清朗网络空间。

news.titleEn: Ex-Simmons Solutions chief joins Purple to help law firms monetise AI – Exclusive interview
news.titleZh: 前Simmons Solutions负责人加入Purple，助律所将AI变现——独家专访
news.summaryZh:
Simmons & Simmons Solutions前董事总经理Ben McGuire已加入法律科技构建工作室Purple，担任风险合伙人。Purple由ThoughtRiver前创始人Tim Pullan与前Gowling WLG律师Dom Conte创立，专注于设计并构建定制化AI法律技术解决方案以帮助创收。McGuire曾任Simmons合伙人，协助该所客户开发能力、技能和技术以打造差异化服务。

Pullan和Conte所建公司可能缺乏在律所内部运营的经验，他作为风险合伙人将帮助律所把与其共同构建的产品和服务落地到自身场景中。他将协助解答合伙人为何应关注、资金从何而来、如何支付、前景与运营模式等问题，并指出这与他近十年在Solutions所做的工作基本一致。他还会帮助律所处理如何利用节省的时间并再投资于更盈利事项等问题。当前律所日益重视利用自身知识和知识产权构建专有解决方案，但许多律所仍受困于遗留基础设施项目。可以直接利用AI等技术创收，为变革提供资金，而不必让合伙人苦等五年。他补充，当前技术的一大优势是可策展提供给生成式AI的上下文质量，无需彻底重构文档管理系统，初期可能仅限小型垂直领域，但仍能通过工程化数据提供上下文，在该垂直领域产生高质量成果，从而帮助支付其他事项。这并非全部答案，因为仍有大型基础设施项目需要完成，但应提前布局，而非被数据问题拖累两三年。
news.bodyHtml:
Ben McGuire, the former managing director of Simmons & Simmons Solutions, has joined legal tech build studio Purple as a venture partner. Purple was founded by Tim Pullan (former founder of ThoughtRiver) and Dom Conte (ex Gowling WLG lawyer), who have built a company that designs and builds custom AI-powered legal technology solutions that help generate income.

McGuire, who was also a partner at Simmons, helped the firm’s clients to develop the capabilities, skillsets and technology to build differentiated offerings.

Advertisement

Speaking to Legal IT Insider, McGuire praised the company that Pullan and Conte have built, observing: “Maybe the gap is that they haven’t run it inside a law firm. The gap I’m filling really is to be a venture partner, which essentially means helping law firms actually make products and services that they’ve built with us inside their context.”

Questions that he will help to address include “why should partners be interested in this? Where’s the money going to come from? How are you going to pay for it? What does the outlook look like? What does the operating model look like?” And he points out, “Because that’s basically what I did with Solutions for nearly a decade.” He will also be helping law firms to process questions including how to leverage time saved and reinvest it, “doing more profitable things than they were before.”

Advertisement

There has been a strong emphasis recently among law firms on leveraging their own knowledge and IP to build proprietary solutions. While many firms are still battling with legacy infrastructure projects, McGuire observes: “I think you can do more than just worry and think to yourself, ‘right, we need partners to suck it up for five years while we sort this out before we get any benefit.’ Because you can do quite a lot to generate revenue directly using AI and other technologies and approaches, which will help to significantly pay for that change.”

He adds: “One of the great things about the technology we’re using now is you can curate the quality of the context that you’re giving to generative AI. And you can make sure that it has high-quality context without completely re-engineering your document management system or making sure that everything’s in place. And it might only be in small verticals initially, but you can still engineer data and give context to generative AI, which will produce a very high quality outcome in that small vertical, which will start to help you pay for other things. It’s not the whole answer, right? Because there are some big infrastructure projects that people need to do. But why not get ahead of the loop instead of thinking ‘I’ve got this ball and chain holding me back for the next two or three years while I make sure all my data is in the right place.’”

news.titleEn: Descrybe Announces Susan E. Guthrie as Strategic Advisor
news.titleZh: Descrybe宣布Susan E. Guthrie出任战略顾问
news.summaryZh: 2026年9月15日，位于波士顿的法律研究与智能平台Descrybe宣布，Susan E. Guthrie以战略顾问身份加入公司。Guthrie拥有超过35年作为律师、调解员、教育者和法律创新者的经验，职业生涯专注于帮助法律与争议解决专业人士应对变革。她曾任美国律师协会争议解决分会主席，培训超过25000名专业人士，是四届亚马逊畅销书作者。她创建并主持全球排名前1%的播客《Divorce & Beyond》，以及《The Practice Playbook Podcast》，其播客下载量超过300万次，近期还作为专家嘉宾做客《The Oprah Podcast》。Guthrie善于预见变革并帮助法律专业人士实际应对变革，AI正在改变法律工作的地点和方式，Descrybe正在为这一新环境构建法律智能层，Guthrie对技术转变和采用的人文层面均有理解。AI已经改变了法律实践，重要的是让法律专业人士获得可自信且负责任使用的可靠法律智能。Descrybe的技术将结构化美国初级法律与引证、后续处理、争点和来源智能相结合，帮助用户研究法律问题、分析权威、理解法律如何组合、验证来源并识别无依据主张。用户可通过Descrybe平台、集成于ChatGPT、Claude、Microsoft 365 Copilot Cowork和Perplexity等领先AI助手的Descrybe Legal Engine，或通过Descrybe Open Connector在自定义AI工具和工作流中使用。Descrybe成立于2023年，已从自力更生的初创公司成长为塑造品类的法律科技公司，服务数千用户。
news.bodyHtml:
Leading attorney, mediator, educator, and legal innovation thought leader joins Descrybe.

BOSTON, Sept. 15, 2026 — Descrybe, the legal research and intelligence platform for people and AI systems, today announced that Susan E. Guthrie has joined the company as a strategic advisor.

Guthrie brings more than 35 years of experience as an attorney, mediator, educator, and legal innovator, along with a career focused on helping legal and dispute resolution professionals navigate change. A past chair of the American Bar Association Section of Dispute Resolution, she has trained more than 25,000 professionals and is a four-time Amazon bestselling author. She is the creator and host of Divorce & Beyond, a top 1% podcast globally, and host of The Practice Playbook Podcast. Her podcasts have generated more than three million downloads, and she was recently featured as an expert guest on The Oprah Podcast.

“Susan has spent her career seeing change coming and then helping legal professionals actually navigate it,” said Kara Peterson, CEO and Co-Founder of Descrybe. “That matters enormously right now. AI is changing where and how legal work gets done, and Descrybe is building the legal intelligence layer for that new environment. Susan understands both the technology shift and the human side of adoption, and that combination is incredibly valuable to us.”

Guthrie joins Descrybe at a pivotal moment for the legal profession, as generative AI moves rapidly from experimentation into everyday professional workflows. Descrybe is building the legal intelligence layer for that shift, combining structured U.S. primary law with citation, subsequent treatment, issue, and source intelligence to help people and AI systems research legal questions, analyze authority, understand how the law fits together, verify sources, and identify unsupported claims.

“The question is no longer whether AI will change legal practice. It already has,” said Guthrie. “What matters now is giving legal professionals access to reliable legal intelligence they can use confidently and responsibly. Descrybe is doing something especially important by bringing that intelligence directly into the AI tools where professionals are increasingly working, while making sophisticated legal research accessible well beyond the largest firms and institutions. I’m delighted to join Kara, Rich, and the Descrybe team as they help shape what comes next.”

Descrybe can be used directly through the Descrybe Platform, through Descrybe Legal Engine in leading AI assistants including ChatGPT, Claude, Microsoft 365 Copilot Cowork, and Perplexity, or through the Descrybe Open Connector, which brings its legal research and intelligence capabilities into custom AI tools and workflows. news.titleZh: 从AI用户到构建者：Akerman聘请首位AI开发总监
news.summaryZh: 美国律所Akerman任命了首位AI开发总监，从德克萨斯州律所Munck Wilson Mandala聘请了Charles Zerner。Zerner最初是诉讼律师，后转向AI领域，在新职位上将负责构建定制AI应用。Akerman已是AI的重度用户，部署了Harvey、TR CoCounsel、Copilot、Claude和ChatGPT等工具，但Zerner的任务是识别现有工具无法满足或定制工具可能更有效满足需求的领域。现成产品能满足一定数量的需求，但它们是面向大量客户设计的，模型能力与利用这些模型加速法律工作的实施之间存在巨大潜力和差距。律所对AI采取“整体”方法，涵盖数据、技术和确保AI安全部署所需的治理。Zerner的任命是在Akerman于8月聘请Michael Adler担任AI治理与数据保护总监之后进行的。Akerman近年来在AI上投入巨大，这已成为律所“最重要的预算分配”之一，且相对于历史支出增长快于其他领域。他预计今年AI支出占总预算的比例将再次增加，但表示“关键不在于花多少钱，而在于怎么花”。Akerman的方法一直是先确定哪些工作流程可以应用AI，然后再确定工具，而不是先购买或构建工具再想办法应用到工作中。吸引他加入Akerman的是共同愿景，即预见律师需求并努力填补空白、解决问题。他说，自己既是诉讼律师又是AI工程师的经历意味着他从独特视角看待这一角色。Zerner于2000年联合创立了一家神经网络初创公司，自2012年以来在法律实践中部署机器学习。在上一家律所，他设计并构建了生产级法律实践AI系统，包括一个完全在律所控制下运行、基于开源模型的文档审查平台。
news.bodyHtml:
By Joanne Harris

US firm Akerman has appointed its first director of AI development, hiring Charles Zerner from Texas firm Munck Wilson Mandala.

Zerner, originally a litigator before moving into AI, takes on a new role in which he will be responsible for building custom AI applications.

Advertisement

Akerman is already a heavy user of AI, deploying tools including Harvey, TR CoCounsel, Copilot, Claude and ChatGPT, but Zerner is tasked with identifying areas where a tool does not currently exist, or where a bespoke tool may do the job more effectively.

“You have the ability to fulfil a certain number of needs with off the shelf products, but at the same time off the shelf products are designed for a large number of clients. There’s an enormous potential and an enormous gap between what models can do and the implementation of those models to accelerate legal work,” Zerner told Legal IT Insider.

Advertisement

“Part of my job is to look for those specific needs that we have that are not going to be met by existing commercial platforms, or that we can do better; part of it is the long term understanding that models are evolving fast. What do we need to build out so that we’re ready when the models are that capable?”

Akerman chief executive officer Scott Meyers said the firm’s approach to AI was “holistic”, encompassing data, technology, and the governance required to ensure AI could be deployed safely. Zerner’s appointment followed Akerman’s August hire of Michael Adler as director of AI governance & data protection.

Meyers said Akerman had been investing heavily in AI in recent years, and it was now one of the firm’s “most significant budget allocations” as well as increasing faster than other areas relative to historic spend. He added that Akerman anticipated it would continue to increase its spend on AI as a proportion of total budget again this year, although he said: “It’s less about how much you spend and more about how you spend it.”

Meyers added: “Our approach has always been rather than to buy or build a tool and then figure out how to apply it to our work, to figure out what workflows we can apply to AI and then figure out the tool.”

Zerner said he was attracted to joining Akerman by the shared vision of anticipating lawyers’ requirements and working to fill gaps and solve problems. He said his experience both as a litigator and an AI engineer meant he was approaching the role from a unique perspective.

Zerner co-founded a neural-network startup in 2000 and has deployed machine learning in legal practice since 2012. At his previous firm he designed and built production-scale AI systems for legal practice, including a document review platform built on open-source models running entirely within the firm’s control.

“You can put a lot of investment into building things that don’t serve the lawyers’ needs because they don’t match the way that they work,” Zerner added. “That’s why having someone with a foot in both worlds is so important, and that’s where you can create value.”

Zerner will be part of Akerman’s information technology team under chief information officer Azfar Shamsi.

An increasing number of major international law firms are investing in building their own solutions in addition to buying from technology companies. Among the most significant announcements, in May this year, Kirkland said it would spend $500m over the next three to four years developing custom AI tools and services.

New white paper equips litigation professionals with practical guidance for responsibly integrating AI into their practice

Chicago, IL — 14 September 2026 — The International Legal Technology Association (ILTA), in partnership with Thomson Reuters, today announced the release of AI Guide for Litigators , the second installment in its ongoing white paper series exploring artificial intelligence's impact across the legal profession. The publication follows ILTA's inaugural AI Foundational Guide, released in late June 2026, and continues the organization's commitment to equipping legal professionals with practical, sector-specific AI guidance.

AI Guide for Litigators addresses the unique considerations litigators face when adopting AI tools, from discovery and case strategy to ethical obligations and risk management. The guide draws on the expertise of a cross-section of practitioners, technologists, and thought leaders from across the legal industry.

"As a former litigator now working in legal innovation and technology, I've watched AI conversations stall the moment jargon enters the room. The real work of change management lives or dies on translation between practitioners and technologists. I'm proud to have helped create this guide that breaks AI use in litigation into practical and familiar concepts legal practitioners can use to foster understanding in their work," said Brendan W. Miller, J.D. , Legal Innovation & Practice Transformation Advisor, Former AmLaw 100 Partner.

research.titleEn: Lexplorer: Navigating the Complexity of Legal Document Landscapes
research.titleZh: Lexplorer： navigating法律文档景观的复杂性
research.abstractEn: As technological and social innovations create novel regulatory challenges, legal systems grow in complexity - increasing the need for interfaces that enable effective interactions with legal document collections. Through interviews with legal scholars (n=15), we find that supporting legal work requires going beyond retrieval-centered legal-information-system paradigms. Hence, we propose Lexplorer, a flexible interface for exploring, navigating, and analyzing legal documents, based on a taxonomy capturing user intents. Distinguishing text and data views for one, few, and many documents, Lexplorer enables context-sensitive interactions with evolving collections of interconnected legal texts, facilitating Adaptive Meaning Construction in law. We evaluate Lexplorer with legal scholars (n=20) in the context of European Union law, validating our elicited requirements, intent taxonomy, and prototype design. Resulting from a close collaboration between visual-analytics researchers and legal scholars, our work also provides nuanced insights into the process required to design interactive systems for expert domains driven by implicit methodological knowledge.
research.abstractZh: 随着技术和社会的创新带来新的监管挑战，法律系统的复杂性不断增加——这增加了对能够有效交互法律文档集合的界面的需求。通过对法律学者的访谈（n=15），我们发现支持法律工作需要的不仅仅是基于检索的法律信息系统范式。因此，我们提出了Lexplorer，一个灵活的界面，用于探索、导航和分析法律文档，基于一个捕捉用户意图的分类法。区分文本视图和数据视图，分别针对单篇、少量和大量文档，Lexplorer支持对不断演变的相互关联的法律文本集合进行上下文敏感交互，促进法律中的适应性意义构建。我们在欧盟法律的背景下，与法律学者（n=20）一起评估了Lexplorer，验证了我们所引出的需求、意图分类法和原型设计。由于视觉分析研究人员和法律学者之间的紧密合作，我们的工作也为设计面向专家领域的交互式系统提供了细致的见解，这些领域由隐性的方法论知识驱动。

news.titleEn: Consilio formalises Legora partnership – CEO Andy Macdonald explains why
news.titleZh: Consilio正式与Legora建立合作伙伴关系——CEO Andy Macdonald解释原因
news.summaryZh: 9月9日，Consilio宣布与Legora正式建立合作伙伴关系，协助内部法律团队和律师事务所进行实施、治理、工作流、培训与采用。Consilio以电子取证服务闻名，同时提供文件审阅、灵活法律人才和转型咨询服务，年收入达10亿美元。在正式宣布前，该公司已与Legora合作超过一年。公司将帮助内部团队和律所将Legora整合到现有事务和工作流中，并提供工作流设计以及整合、治理和培训方面的协助，以帮助团队更快、更有效地采用。公司正在组建法律和技术人才团队以满足该领域需求。18个月前还能找到同时具备法律和技术技能的人，现在很难找到，因此正在组建两者兼备的团队。Consilio使用Legora交付客户工作已超过一年，熟悉其在研究、起草和文件审阅方面的全套能力。该关系并非独家：Consilio旗下的LOD与法律AI公司Wordsmith有正式合作。能够与客户就其使用的工具开展合作很重要，若走独家路线，约三分之二的客户会不满意。他估计此类整合工作占Consilio收入不到10%，但属于增长中的业务。谈及个人AI使用，Macdonald承认，如今使用AI工具的频率可能至少是1月份的50倍，但不确定自己是否更高效。这正是Consilio寻求在组织层面为客户解决的挑战，即确保工具得到恰当嵌入。
news.bodyHtml:
By Tom Saunders

Last week (9 September) Consilio announced a formal partnership with Legora, assisting in-house legal teams and law firms with implementation, governance, workflow, training and adoption.

Advertisement

Consilio, which is best known as an eDiscovery provider, also offers services including document review, flexible legal talent, and transformation consulting services. The company, which reports annual revenues of $1bn has been working with Legora for over a year prior to the formal announcement.

Andy Macdonald, CEO of Consilio, told Legal IT Insider that Consilio will help in-house teams and law firms integrate Legora into existing matters and workflows. The company will also provide workflow design and assist with integration, governance and training to help teams adopt faster and more effectively. The company is building teams of legal and technical talent to meet demand in this space, with Macdonald commenting, “Eighteen months ago, I could get someone who had the legal and tech skills in a single body but they’re hard to find now, so we’re building teams that have a little bit of both.”

Advertisement

Consilio has also been delivering client work using Legora for over a year, so is familiar with the full suite of its capabilities across research, drafting and document review. The relationship is not exclusive: LOD, which is owned by Consilio, has a formal partnership with legal AI company Wordsmith. For Macdonald, it is important to be able to work with clients on the tools they are using, and he says: “If I were to go exclusive, I would then have probably have two-thirds of my clients who would be unhappy with me.”

Macdonald estimates that this sort of integration work accounts for less than 10% of Consilio’s revenues, but it is a part of the business that is growing. Speaking about his personal AI use, Macdonald admits: “The amount of times I use AI tools today versus January, is probably at least 50 times more, but I don’t know that I’m any more efficient.” This is exactly the challenge Consilio is looking to solve for clients at an organisational level by making sure tools are embedded properly.
