news.titleEn: Ex-Eigen Team Raises $20m Seed For Twin1
news.titleZh: 前Eigen团队为Twin1筹集2000万美元种子轮
news.summaryZh: Twin1结束隐身模式，获得由Bessemer Venture Partners等联合领投的2000万美元种子轮融资，用于为律师开发数字孪生。公司由Eigen前CEO Lewis Liu领导，Eigen已被Sirion收购。创始团队还包括前Eigen员工Tom Cahn和Huiting Liu。公司总部位于加州圣马特奥，并在伦敦设有另一个办公室。Linklaters、Orrick和Dechert等律所已在使用该产品，AL了解到其他律所和公司中还有大量概念验证。其开发的数字孪生是“你自己的AI延伸”，Twin1是一个完全加密的平台内代理，知道你所知道的一切，代表你回应，并在你决定的范围内充当你的AI版本，帮助你跳过瓶颈、定位关键信息，并与其他Twin建立联系以快速获得正确答案。数字孪生基于用户的工作上下文，包括电子邮件、会议、文档和工作场所系统，并在Slack、Microsoft Teams、Outlook、Gmail、Google Drive和SharePoint等工具中运行，以更深入的上下文和专业知识增强专业人员的AI代理。Twin学习你私人知识库中的语言、语气和沟通模式，并用该上下文以你的风格起草回复，包括适应你与不同人的沟通方式。你保持控制权，可以在消息共享前审查、编辑或拒绝。此外还有大量隐私保护措施。Twin方法还提供“主权AI”，通过将数据、专有知识和治理政策保持在企业控制之下，支持灵活的SaaS、单租户和私有云部署模型，减少对任何单一模型或基础设施提供商的依赖。
news.bodyText: Twin1 has come out of stealth with a $20m Seed round co-led by Bessemer Venture Partners, among others, to develop digital twins for lawyers. It’s captained by Lewis Liu, the former CEO of Eigen – which was sold to Sirion, (see AL interview with Liu in following article). The founding team also includes Tom Cahn and Huiting Liu, both ex-Eigen staffers. It’s based in San Mateo, California, with another office in London. Law firms such as Linklaters, Orrick, and Dechert have already been using it, and AL is aware of a ton of POCs among other law firms and also corporates. The digital twins that it develops are ‘an AI extension’ of yourself. Or, as they say: ‘Twin1 is a fully-encrypted in-platform agent that knows everything you know, responds on your behalf, and acts as an AI version of you to the extent you decide. Helping you skip bottlenecks, locate key information, and network with other Twins so you get the right answers fast.’ ‘The digital twins are grounded in the user’s work context, including emails, meetings, documents, and workplace systems. ‘These digital twins operate where professionals work across tools such as Slack, Microsoft Teams, Outlook, Gmail, Google Drive, and SharePoint and supercharge professionals’ AI agents with deeper context and know-how.’ Also, your Twin ‘learns the language, tone and communication patterns in your own private knowledge base and uses that context to draft responses in my style, including adapting how I communicate with different people. You remain in control and can review, edit or reject messages before they are shared.’ They continued that: There is also a ton of privacy safeguards – as you’d expect. — (Advertisement) — Legal Innovators New York – Nov 17 and 18 – the landmark legal innovation conference: Day One: law firms, Day Two: inhouse. — One other aspect they highlighted is that the Twin approach provides ‘Sovereign AI: it gives enterprises control over their AI destiny by keeping their data, proprietary knowledge and governance policies under their control, while supporting flexible SaaS, single-tenant, and private-cloud deployment models and reducing dependence on any single model or infrastructure provider.’

research.titleEn: InsufficiencyBench: Evaluating LLM legal advice on underspecified user queries
research.titleZh: 不足基准：评估大语言模型在信息不充分的用户查询上的法律建议
research.abstractEn: Legal AI systems are increasingly used to answer legal questions, yet existing benchmarks assume queries arrive fully specified. In practice, users omit facts that materially determine the legal outcome. We introduce InsufficiencyBench, the first legal benchmark targeting query-side insufficiency: whether a model recognizes when a query lacks legally material information, identifies what is missing, and refrains from premature conclusions. We formalize a taxonomy of eight canonical missing-element categories across three structural failure modes---switch, gating, and fatal prerequisite--- and construct 202 benchmark items (58 base queries, 144 deficient variants) spanning six legal domains and 24 US jurisdictions and annotated by practising attorneys. Evaluating ten frontier models, we find that no model exceeds F2 = 0.46 on missing-element identification and that the median recall is 0.44. Models either hedge indiscriminately or answer silently under fabricated presumptions. No model both identifies and qualifies responses to deficient queries while directly addressing complete ones.
research.abstractZh: 法律人工智能系统越来越多地被用于回答法律问题，然而现有的基准假设查询在提出时信息完整。在实践中，用户会遗漏对法律结果具有实质性决定作用的事实。我们引入了不足基准，这是第一个针对查询侧信息不足的法律基准：测试模型是否能识别查询中是否缺乏法律上重要的信息，识别缺失的内容，并避免过早得出结论。我们形式化了一个包含八个典型缺失元素类别的分类法，涵盖三种结构性失败模式——切换、门控和致命前提——并构建了202个基准项目（58个基础查询，144个缺陷变体），涵盖六个法律领域和24个美国司法管辖区，并由执业律师进行标注。评估十个前沿模型，我们发现没有模型在缺失元素识别上超过F2 = 0.46，中位召回率为0.44。模型要么不加区分地回避，要么在虚构的假设下默默回答。没有模型既能识别并限定对缺陷查询的回答，又能直接处理完整查询。

research.titleEn: ContractScrub: A benchmark for final review of legal contracts
research.titleZh: ContractScrub：法律合同最终审查的基准
research.abstractEn: Legal work, with its heavy reliance on processing large amounts of text, is often considered one of the domains most exposed to the use of LLMs. Contract ``scrubbing,'' the final review of transactional agreements for errors and inconsistencies, is a particularly suitable task for automation, because it is routine, painstaking work requiring detailed attention to long documents. Scrubbing also seems to align naturally with the general capabilities expected of frontier LLMs around long-context reasoning, consistency checking, and named entity recognition (NER). Despite the economic value and potential for automation, no formal evaluations of LLMs performing contract scrubbing have been conducted. We introduce ContractScrub, the first benchmark designed to evaluate contract scrubbing capabilities, comprising contracts hand-crafted by experienced lawyers over diverse error categories such as misuse of defined terms, incorrect references, and inconsistent language. Frontier models perform surprisingly poorly with only one model reaching 0.75 macro average recall despite strong performance on seemingly related general benchmarks, demonstrating the practical limits of current models and the importance of narrowly targeted, domain-specific benchmarks for measuring real-world impact.
research.abstractZh: 法律工作因其大量依赖处理文本，通常被认为是最容易受到LLM影响的领域之一。合同“清洗”，即对交易协议进行最终审查以发现错误和不一致之处，是一项特别适合自动化的任务，因为它是一项常规、费力的工作，需要对长文档进行细致关注。清洗似乎也与前沿LLM在长上下文推理、一致性检查和命名实体识别（NER）方面的通用能力自然契合。尽管具有经济价值和自动化潜力，但尚未对执行合同清洗的LLM进行正式评估。我们引入了ContractScrub，这是第一个旨在评估合同清洗能力的基准，包含由经验丰富的律师手工制作的合同，涵盖多种错误类别，如定义术语的误用、不正确的引用和不一致的语言。前沿模型的表现出人意料地差，只有一个模型达到了0.75的宏平均召回率，尽管在看似相关的通用基准上表现强劲，这证明了当前模型的实际局限性以及针对特定领域的窄范围基准对于衡量现实世界影响的重要性。

news.titleEn: Candle AI Introduces Candle Work: Run Your Law Firm from Your Inbox
news.titleZh: Candle AI 推出 Candle Work：在收件箱中运营你的律所
news.summaryZh:
Candle 今日推出 Candle Work。Candle 已将律所收件箱与案件及事项管理系统、文档、客户信息及工作负责人等数据打通，此前集成能把正确的文档、状态和上下文带入邮件，但 Candle 只能帮助用户看到工作，执行仍需人工。客户索要文档和状态更新、对方律师发来修订协议、客户告知需更新案件管理系统的事项，每封邮件都始于几行非结构化文本，却会转化为检索案件管理系统、核对其他系统、更新事项信息、寻找负责人、起草回复等实际工作，每天发生数十次，且大多不可计费。

用户只需对 Agent 说“处理这件事”，它便能理解请求、收集信息、跨系统操作并返回可供审核的结果：为客户邮件查找文档、核对未完成事项、确定负责人并起草含附件的回复；识别客户邮件中的变更、对照案件管理系统并准备更新，经批准后由 Candle 写回；针对修订协议找到旧版本、标记实质性变更并起草回复，按指示接受或反驳后完成；对触发多项后续事项的邮件，判断其对案件的影响，准备更新、文档和跟进事项并提交审批。Candle 并非取代律所现有技术，而是位于邮件中非结构化信息与律所已依赖的结构化系统之间，案件管理系统保持不变，律所还可通过 MCP 连接更多系统和工具。用户始终掌控流程，Agent 收集信息、准备工作并提出行动建议，任何重要操作均须经用户审核、调整和批准。Candle Work 今日面向有限数量的律所开放早期访问，可通过邮件联系联合创始人 sujith@trycandle.ai 或 carl@trycandle.ai 申请。
news.bodyHtml:
Today, Candle is introducing Candle Work.

The inbox is where the work shows up. But it hasn’t been where the work gets done.

Candle has connected your firm’s inbox to the firm’s data: the case and matter management system, documents, client information, and the people who own the work. Those integrations have already saved time by bringing the right documents, the right status, and the right context directly into email.

But until now, Candle could only help you see the work. You still had to do it.

An email comes in. A client asks for documents and a status update. Opposing counsel sends a revised agreement. A client tells you something’s changed that needs to be updated in the case management system. Each starts as a few lines of unstructured text, and each turns into real work: searching the CMS, checking another system, updating matter information, tracking down an owner, drafting a response. This happens dozens of times a day, and much of it isn’t billable.

Candle Work closes that gap.

Tell your Agent, “Take care of this,” and it understands the request, gathers the relevant information, works across your firm’s systems, and comes back with a result to review.

What that means day-to-day:

A client emails asking for documents and a status update? Your Agent finds the relevant documents, checks what’s outstanding, identifies who’s handling it, and drafts the response, attachments included.

A client emails with information that changes the matter? Your Agent identifies what changed, checks it against your case management system, and prepares the updates. Approve them, and Candle writes the changes back.

Opposing counsel sends a revised agreement? Your Agent finds the previous version, flags the substantive changes, and drafts your response. Tell it what to accept and push back on, and it finishes the job.

An email triggers several things that need to happen next? Your Agent figures out what it means for the matter, prepares the resulting updates, documents, and follow-ups, and lays it out for your approval.

One email can create work across multiple systems. Candle orchestrates what happens next, right from the inbox.

This isn’t about replacing your firm’s technology. Candle sits between the unstructured information flowing through email and the structured systems your firm already relies on. Your case management system remains your case management system. Firms can also connect additional systems and tools through MCP, extending Agents beyond Candle’s built-in integrations. Candle just makes the inbox the place where the work across those systems gets done.

You stay in control. Agents gather information, prepare work, and propose actions. You review, adjust, and approve before anything consequential happens.

Today, too much time is spent turning emails into separate tasks, moving between systems, and copying information from one place to another. Candle Work gives that time back.

Lawyers already work in their inbox. Now their Agents can work there too.

Candle Work is available today to a limited number of firms in early access.

Request early access by emailing our co-founders directly: sujith@trycandle.ai or carl@trycandle.ai

news.titleEn: LegalFab: The vertically integrated answer to the governance gap
news.titleZh: LegalFab：针对治理缺口的垂直整合解决方案
news.summaryZh: Legal IT Insider首席分析师Neil Cameron对LegalFab进行了两小时演示审查，并阅读了其架构文档。LegalFab是面向律所的新型代理操作系统，采用垂直整合方案，拥有知识编织层、代理工作室和预建工具，其中合规与冲突模块最成熟。其架构核心是“连接而非复制”，仅在解析层持久化数据，原始记录保留在律所边界内。公司称LegalFab可能逐步吸纳现有法律技术提供商的解决方案，但律所无需先替换这些方案即可采用LegalFab。合规序列演示中，系统对商业地产交易中的可疑方进行洗钱风险评分，触发红旗规则，执行静默背景调查，识别出 probable shell，并自动生成可疑活动报告。系统还能检测监管变化，通过无代码规则编辑器编码，实时生效。公司成立于2026年1月，伦敦总部，约40名员工，自筹和天使投资，报告一个英国全服务律所生产试点和一个德国IP精品所合同，均保密。当前部署中证明的11个系统连接包括iManage、NetDocuments、Aderant、HighQ、Salesforce、SharePoint、微软技术栈、STP和Genese。公司承认直通处理和85%假阳性减少来自先前金融服务工作，而非法律部署验证。独立评估缺失，架构文档虽好但为公司自述。
news.bodyHtml:
“It is the most impressive thing I’ve been shown in this particular space in the market.” Neil Cameron, lead analyst for Legal IT Insider, examines LegalFab, a new agentic operating system for law firms. 

In Gen AI 3 I argued that the governance of AI agents is cross-system by nature. An agent traverses the document management system, practice management, finance and email in a single task, and no content vendor owns all of those. I set the enforcement layer out as a spine between the applications a firm buys and the data they consume, and observed that nobody owned it.

Advertisement

I have now seen LegalFab demonstrated for two hours by its chief executive, put a two-page question set to the company, and read the architecture document it has since published. I told them at the time that I would summarise what I had seen under the word ‘astonishing’. I do not withdraw it, and I want it at the top rather than buried, because most of what follows is the harder question of what has been evidenced.

LegalFab is the vertically integrated answer to that gap. Rather than build an enforcement layer between other people’s systems and other people’s agents, it proposes to own the resolution layer, the governance layer and the agents together. Three layers: a Knowledge Fabric that resolves entities across the estate, an Agentic Studio for composing teams of agents, and pre-built utilities of which compliance and conflicts is the most developed. The architectural claim carrying all the weight is “connect, don’t copy” – active metadata over live sources, with only the resolved layer persisted and raw records left behind the firm’s boundary.

Advertisement

Disclosure. I have known Simon Thompson professionally for several decades. I also told LegalFab during the demonstration that I am working with an alternative vendor on a pricing engine for a law firm pilot, and declined to be shown their pricing module. This review is unpaid and unsponsored.

The declaration

I asked the company where it sits relative to everyone else, and which layers a firm would continue to buy elsewhere. The written answer declines the framing entirely – LegalFab, it says, is a change in a firm’s operating model, not another product in the stack – and then answers anyway. The firm keeps its systems of record, infrastructure, identity, security and any specialist applications it chooses to retain. Everything above that is contested, explicitly and over time: some applications may remain, some become narrower systems of record, some capabilities get rebuilt on LegalFab.

Then this: Intapp is the clearest and most immediate example of the model LegalFab is built to succeed. The company says that LegalFab may progressively subsume solutions from incumbent legal technology providers, but the point is that firm’s do not have to replace these solutions before adopting LegalFab. It is once data, identity, governance, intelligence and execution are unified across the enterprise, that many functions currently requiring separate applications can increasingly be performed within the common LegalFab architecture. This transition will happen progressively.

I have not previously had a vendor name its displacement targeting so directly, in writing and for publication. It is the clearest statement of the vertical-integration thesis anyone in legal has made, and a considerable risk: a product that replaces conflicts, displaces the CRM and obviates the warehouse has no single budget holder and invites every incumbent it threatens to defend at once.

What the demonstration showed

The compliance sequence is the most immediate evidence of where the product is strongest. A commercial real estate matter days from completion; an email from a client director asking that funds go to a party nobody has heard of. The system scores it for money laundering risk, states which of the firm’s red-flag rules have triggered and why, separates known client and counterparty from unknown third party, and proposes a silent background check – silent because tipping off is an offence. The check returns no adverse media but characterises the new party as a probable shell: no trading history, registered at a formations agent, in a high-value transaction. The analyst accepts, and the system drafts a suspicious activity report onto the regulator’s template, populated and routed for approval.

The most important moment received the least airtime. A regulatory change – the FCA treating crypto asset exposure as high risk – was detected, matched against the client base, and then encoded: a no-code rules editor, a new condition, a weighting, saved, live across the firm. The gap between a compliance team learning of a change and the firm’s systems reflecting it is measured in weeks and is structural, because one team understands the rule and another encodes it. Collapsing that into one screen is a serious operational claim.

It is also the point at which an authorised user can make a rule change with firm-wide consequences. Firms should test the permissions, dual-control requirements, approval path, version history, rollback and audit trail there first. The same applies to the SAR: deciding whether and how to report engages criminal-law obligations, including tipping-off risk, and a system that assembles the document in thirty seconds changes the character of that judgment whether or not a human signs.

Permissions, and whose graph wins

Two answers arrived in two versions, and both reconciled properly when pressed.

On ethical walls, the demonstration suggested inheritance; the written answers describe enforcement at a derived layer, via a consolidated permission model that exists because the source systems’ models do not align. The company’s position is that these are halves of one mechanism. Where the current evidence stops

Against that, the evidence base currently appears narrower than the proposition, largely by reason of novelty.

The company was founded in January 2026, is London headquartered with around forty staff, self-funded and angel-funded, and reports one production pilot with a UK full-service firm and one contract with a German IP boutique. Both are confidential and no reference is available. Conflicts is the most conservative purchase a law firm makes, and no architecture solves that.

Connectivity needs care. The software was demonstrated live in a populated environment and it completed the opening query – active matters unbilled for thirty days with average work in progress older than sixty days, by client. The interface showed the question decomposed into sub-queries, agents reaching the displayed operational sources, and an actionable table returned with matter-level financials behind it. Proclaim, Visualfiles and SOS Connect and such are absent because no customer has yet required them, which is consistent with the company’s stated model of treating connectivity as a commodity built per engagement – and the two deployments it describes required systems most vendors have never heard of, which supports its account that it builds what each engagement needs. For mid-market and defendant-insurance firms this is a delivery question rather than a capability one, but it is still a delivery question. The figure of over a thousand in the deck needs qualification: it describes the broader addressable connectivity surface, not a thousand production-proven legal connectors. The demonstration referred to 200-plus; the set evidenced in current deployments is eleven. The eleven are the more impressive number.

Asked to attribute two performance claims, the company confirmed that the straight-through-processing figure and the 85 per cent reduction in false positives comes from prior financial services work. Its benchmarking method is better than most, and it volunteers that its mature figures come from a financial-services production setting rather than a live legal deployment, with legal replication to be labelled model output until validated. That is a creditable admission. It also means that neither of the two headline figures put to me was supported by validated results from a live legal deployment. The wider gap is independent assessment. No independent product-level evaluation was made available to me establishing that the implementation matches the architecture document. That document is unusually good, and much of the architectural assessment in this review rests on it, but it is a description of intent written by the company whose intent it describes. A firm’s own security function will want more, and should ask early and properly: an accredited certificate verified through the accreditation body rather than the issuer or the vendor, and the underlying audit and penetration-test reports rather than summaries or certificates. That is a reasonable standard for anyone claiming to hold the record by which their own conduct is proved.

Assessment

I have not seen anything like this for law firms, and I have looked. Products exist that do parts of it: intake and conflicts, client intelligence, document understanding, agent orchestration. I have not seen another product resolve the estate, reason across it, act on it and encode the firm’s own rules in the same motion, nor take the compliance sequence end to end from an inbound email to a populated report on the regulator’s template. The architecture documentation is the best I have seen in this sector, and the candour on the mosaic effect – that inference from legitimately visible material cannot be claimed away, only bounded and logged – is rarer still.

The proposition does concentrate authority – over resolution, over permissions, over action, and over the record by which all three are proved. Every vendor produces its own audit trail, so that on its own is unremarkable. What is not unremarkable is that in a multi-vendor estate the records can disagree, and the disagreement provides an accidental check. Centralise resolution, permissions, action and their audit record in one platform and that check diminishes. This is less a criticism of LegalFab than the trade its model asks a firm to make: consistency and coherent control in exchange for some of the independence multiple systems supply by accident. Firms should make it knowingly, and should want independent assessment of the architecture in proportion to how much they hand over.

None of which is a reason not to look at it, indeed, it is a reason for looking at it sooner rather than later. Waiting for a fuller reference list reduces adoption risk; it also gives the incumbents whose territory LegalFab contests time to respond. The company chose the standard itself – proof, not assurance. I will report on progress.

news.titleEn: Intapp Compliance with Celeste: Accept more business, faster — without increasing risk
news.titleZh: Intapp Compliance 携手 Celeste：更快接受更多业务，同时不增加风险
news.summaryZh: 随着律所通过横向招聘、私募资本投资、并购及地域扩张实现增长，新业务量上升，接受业务所需的合规工作也随之增加。每项新业务都需在计费前完成受理、冲突和客户义务清理，而专家判断前的重复性准备工作限制了律所可接受的业务量。7月，Intapp宣布面向专业服务机构的代理式AI平台Intapp Celeste正式可用，该平台基于律所自身知识和政策。如今Celeste已直接嵌入Intapp Intake、Conflicts和Terms，专业人员可在日常产品中协作，将常规设置交给代理式剧本，并用自然语言询问合规数据。Celeste支持客户生命周期各阶段：业务受理中，可在Outlook内打开新受理请求，从邮件提取细节自动填充表单、实时验证答案并在提交前提供增强建议；冲突清理中，构建搜索策略、匹配公司树、自动运行搜索、分类结果供专家审查并自动起草清理摘要；条款管理中，读取外部律师指南、匹配客户记录、填充属性并分类，自动从共享收件箱摄取新指南并在数秒内分类，配置条款可自动接受并流入下游应用；合规智能方面，嵌入面板提供自然语言查询，答案来自律所记录、链接回源并基于访问政策。与通用AI工具不同，Celeste为专业服务工作流构建，处理决策前重复任务，让专家保持对决策的控制，每一步均有记录，律所可更快接受更多业务。
news.bodyHtml:
As firms grow through lateral hiring, private capital investment, and M&A and geographic expansion, the volume of new business rises — and so does the compliance work required to accept it.

Every new engagement requires teams to clear intake, conflicts, and client obligations before it can be billed. The repetitive steps that stand between experts and their judgment limit how much a firm can accept.

In July, we announced the general availability of Intapp Celeste, our agentic AI platform for professional firms that’s grounded in your firm’s knowledge and policies. Now, Celeste is embedded directly inside Intapp Intake, Conflicts, and Terms. Your professionals can work with Celeste in the products they use every day, handing routine setup work to agentic playbooks and asking questions about their compliance data in plain language.

Preparation, not decision-making, is the real bottleneck

Compliance work depends on expert judgment. But before an analyst can weigh a conflict or clear a request, the search must be built, the details gathered and validated, the corporate structures mapped, and the context assembled.

Most of that preparation is repetitive, high-volume work that consumes hours and rarely calls for the analyst’s expertise. The burden doesn’t fall on compliance teams alone. The professionals who win the work must also conduct the same preparation work — completing intake forms manually, responding to follow-up questions, and waiting for clearance — before they can begin billing.

The effect compounds across the firm: Time-to-bill slows, new business stalls, and skilled professionals are pulled away from the higher-risk questions that need their attention.

Traditionally, firms have met growing compliance demands by adding headcount. But today’s growth is outpacing that model. Every lateral team, acquisition, and new office adds volume faster than a firm can recruit and train analysts to clear it.

Celeste offers a different approach by handling the preparatory tasks, allowing experts to remain in control of and provide judgment on every decision.

Celeste lifts the ceiling for compliance

Business acceptance workflows represent some of a firm’s most repetitive, high-volume compliance work. Celeste follows the same workflows your teams do, supporting every stage of the client lifecycle — from intake and conflicts clearance to ongoing client obligations.

  • Business intake: The moment an email arrives, professionals can ask Intapp Celeste to open a new intake request — without leaving Outlook. Celeste extracts details from the email to auto-populate the form, then validates each answer in real time as the requestor reviews, edits, and completes the request. It also offers recommended enhancements before submission, so compliance teams can begin their assessment with complete, accurate requests — accelerating time-to-bill.
  • Conflicts clearance: The moment a request arrives, Celeste builds the search strategy, matches corporate trees for each party, and runs the search automatically. It then triages the results for expert review, surfacing likely conflicts and helping to clear low-risk items faster. Celeste can also automatically draft the clearance summary, pulling together resolved hits and the details that matter, with a clear record of how each was resolved.
  • Terms and client obligations management: When outside counsel guidelines arrive — through Outlook or the Intapp Celeste panel — Celeste reads them, matches them to the right client records, populates the key attributes, and categorizes the terms. It automatically ingests new guidelines from a shared inbox and categorizes them in Terms within seconds, eliminating manual cataloging.

    Firms can also enforce configured terms — like block billing or restricted words — to auto-accept during AI categorization. The terms will flow straight into downstream applications like Time the moment Celeste ingests the new guidelines document — no handoff required.

  • Compliance intelligence: An embedded Celeste panel sits directly in Intapp Intake, Conflicts, and Terms — giving professionals one place to ask questions about their compliance data in plain language and run routine playbooks. Answers are drawn from the firm’s own records, link back to the source for verification, and are grounded in the firm’s access policies. Risk and firm leaders get immediate answers during compliance procedures, strategic planning, and regulatory responses.

Celeste reflects how professional firms actually work

Unlike generic AI tools and point solutions — which require firms to adjust their workflows — Celeste is built for the professional services workflows your teams rely on today. It handles the repetitive tasks that precede every decision while allowing the expert to remain in control of the decision itself.

That balance is what governed AI looks like in a regulated firm. Celeste handles the preparatory work. Experts remain in control of every decision. And every step — the analysis and rationale behind each request, workflow, and decision — is documented. Firms accept more business faster, and every decision carries a clear account of how it was reached.

What’s next?

This is just the beginning. We’ll continue to introduce new ways for Celeste to support your teams and to put your compliance data to work across every workflow. The future is continuous compliance, where risks are identified, surfaced, and addressed before they become problems.

Learn more about how Intapp Compliance with Celeste works across the client lifecycle, or talk with your Intapp account team.

news.summaryZh: 加利福尼亚北区联邦地区法院近期受理的一起诉讼指控，用于在裁员中对员工进行评分、排名和筛选的AI工具，对休受保护假期的员工和残障员工构成歧视。部分原因在于AI系统的输入项（如生产力指标和“AI原生”评级）无法由缺勤或需要合理便利的员工积累。诉状进一步主张，雇主未针对受保护假期调整这些输入项，未将休受保护假期者或寻求便利者排除出筛选群体，也未暂停系统以进行法律所要求的个性化、对假期和便利保持中立的审查。该诉讼提醒考虑或已在裁员、绩效管理或其他高风险雇佣决策中部署AI工具的雇主，注意开发技术固有的法律风险。两个领域需立即关注：公司如何构建AI相关审查以保护特权与保密性，以及在员工点击AI平台“回车”前已建立哪些内部治理框架。使用AI进行雇佣决策时最重大且常被忽视的风险之一，是决策背后分析的可发现性。雇主通常进行偏见审计、不利影响分析和AI工具供应商评估，但若结构不当，这些分析可能成为原告的“证据A”。特权保护分析，但不是合规策略。雇主需在任何AI工具触及雇佣决策前建立实质性治理框架。AI辅助雇佣决策已成定局，随之而来的诉讼和监管审查亦然。现在投资于受特权保护的评估和健全内部治理的雇主，在决策受挑战时将处于更有利地位；不这样做的雇主可能会以艰难方式认识到，速度和效率不能替代法律合规。
news.bodyText: Find Your Next Job ! A recent lawsuit filed in the Northern District of California alleges that AI-based tools used to score, rank, and select employees for a reduction in force discriminated against workers on protected leave and those with disabilities. The lawsuit alleges this occurred, in part, because the AI-system’s inputs, such as productivity metrics and “AI-native” ratings, could not be accumulated by employees who were absent or working under various accommodations. The complaint further asserts that, based on information and belief, the employer did not neutralize those inputs for protected leave; did not exclude protected-leave-takers or accommodation-seekers from the selection cohort; and did not pause the system for the individualized, leave- and accommodation-neutral review that the law requires. This lawsuit serves as a timely reminder for employers considering, or already deploying, AI tools in layoffs, performance management, or other high-stakes employment decisions—specifically, underscoring the inherent legal risks of developing technology. As we have explored in our prior publications addressing AI, privilege, confidentiality, and the issues every business must address in its first AI policy, two specific areas demand immediate attention: (1) how companies structure AI-related reviews to protect privilege and confidentiality, and (2) what internal governance frameworks are in place before an employee hits “enter” on the AI platform. One of the most significant and frequently overlooked risks of using AI in employment decisions is the discoverability of the analysis behind those decisions. Employers routinely conduct bias audits, adverse impact analyses, and vendor assessments of AI tools, but if those analyses are not structured properly, they can become plaintiff’s “Exhibit A.” (For a deeper treatment of the privilege landscape as it applies to AI, see our recent article on AI, Privilege, and the Future of Confidentiality in the Workplace and Beyond.) Here is how to get it right: Privilege protects the analysis, but it is not a compliance strategy. Employers need substantive governance frameworks in place before any AI tool touches an employment decision. (For organizations building these frameworks from the ground up, our article on Your First AI Policy: Six Burning Issues for Every Growing Business to Consider offers a practical starting point.) AI-assisted employment decisions are here to stay, and so is the litigation and regulatory scrutiny that follows them. Employers who invest now in privilege-protected assessments and robust internal governance will be far better positioned to defend their decisions if challenged. Those who do not may find themselves learning the hard way that speed and efficiency are no substitute for legal compliance. More Upcoming Events Sign Up for any (or all) of our 25+ Newsletters
news.relevanceReason: 该文章的核心主题是AI在劳动力决策（如裁员、绩效管理）中的应用及其法律风险，包括特权保护、合规治理和歧视诉讼，属于法律AI或法律科技范畴。

news.titleEn: AI Is Rewiring M&A Practice — But Judgment Still Sets the Deal’s Direction
news.titleZh: AI正在重塑并购实践——但判断力仍决定交易方向
news.summaryZh: AI在并购中正从离散的生产力工具转变为交易架构的核心组成部分，使信息以更结构化的方式在交易团队中流动，从尽职调查到起草再到谈判。这可能压缩时间线并改变对人员配置和定价的预期，但也使验证、判断和问责更加重要。问题不再是AI是否会出现在交易中，而是它能在何处提高工作质量和经济效益，同时保持结论得出方式的透明度。运用得当，AI处理可重复的分析任务，让律师有更多自由处理依赖背景、风险偏好和战略的问题。实践中，AI被部署在交易的多个层面，作为审阅、比较和综合的共享基础设施，而非交易团队的替代品。初级律师可用AI识别需第三方同意或控制权变更即可终止的合同并注明对方、触发语言和剩余期限，将数天或数周的初步审阅压缩至几分钟，但律师仍须评估问题重要性并纳入尽职调查叙述。高级律师可用AI Word插件将赔偿和盈利支付条款与先例比较并标记有利于卖方的偏差，但先例是基准而非交易特定判断的替代品。合伙人可用AI综合尽职调查发现为风险摘要并压力测试谈判立场，但综合不决定风险分配，只使权衡更可见。每个层面都须准确性检查，AI可加快工作但不能保证自身可靠性。在适当验证协议下，这些用途可促成对交易的整合理解，加速问题升级并更审慎分配律师时间，但也引发培训、审阅协议、数据处理和最终结论问责的问题。
news.bodyText: Find Your Next Job ! AI in M&A is moving from a discrete productivity tool to a core component of the deal architecture itself. The shift goes beyond faster document review; it means information can now move through the deal team in a more structured way—from diligence to drafting to negotiation. That may compress timelines and change expectations around staffing and pricing, but it also makes verification, judgment and accountability more important than ever. That is the emerging commercial reality for firms and clients. The relevant question is no longer whether AI will appear in a transaction, but where it can improve the quality and economics of the work while preserving transparency in how conclusions are reached. Used well, AI handles repeatable analytical tasks and gives lawyers more freedom to engage with questions that hinge on context, risk appetite and strategy. In practice, AI is being deployed at multiple levels of a transaction—not as a replacement for the deal team, but as a shared infrastructure for review, comparison and synthesis. The same matter can generate different uses depending on the lawyer’s role: A junior associate conducting diligence may ask the AI platform to “identify every contract that requires third-party consent or is terminable on a change of control, and note the counterparty, the triggering language and the remaining term.” Across hundreds of commercial contracts, that query can produce a streamlined, source-linked output and identify agreements that may affect deal structure or timing. The effect is compelling: an initial review that once consumed days or weeks can be completed in minutes, allowing the team to focus sooner on red flags, context and escalation. But identification is only part of the task; a lawyer must still assess each issue’s significance and incorporate it into a coherent diligence narrative that can shape negotiation strategy and informed client counseling. A senior associate refining a purchase agreement may use an AI Word add-in to ask it to “compare the indemnification and earnout provisions in this draft against our firm precedent and flag every deviation that favors the seller.” The result can expose gaps and off-market terms for further analysis and contribute to a markup more closely aligned with precedent. But precedent is a benchmark, not a substitute for transaction-specific drafting and judgment; a deviation may be deliberate, and a tool cannot supply the commercial reason for keeping or changing it. At the partner level, the AI platform may be asked to “synthesize the diligence findings into a concise risk summary and pressure test our key negotiating positions for the weaknesses that opposing counsel is most likely to exploit.” That synthesis can translate scattered findings into negotiation strategy, which is particularly effective when the issues list is long and the time before signing is short. However, such a synthesis does not determine the risk allocation. Rather, it makes the potential tradeoffs more visible for a lawyer to assess. At each of these levels, accuracy checking is imperative. The junior associate must confirm that flagged provisions actually say what the tool indicates; the senior associate must confirm that no material drafting nuances were missed; the partner must ensure that strategic synthesis rests on accurate premises rather than illusory or mischaracterized facts. AI can expedite the work, but it cannot guarantee its own reliability. With appropriate verification protocols in place, these examples point to a change in operating model. The junior associate’s structured diligence, the senior associate’s precedent-driven contract refinements and the partner’s risk synthesis can contribute to an integrated, comprehensive understanding of the deal. That may accelerate issue escalation and allow lawyer time to be allocated more deliberately, but it also raises practical questions about training, review protocols, data handling and who is accountable for the final conclusion. AI is most useful where the task is clearly delineated and the output can be verified against source material. It is less reliable when the answer depends on incomplete facts, ambiguous language, business context or a client’s tolerance for risk. A model may identify a change-of-control provision; it cannot decide whether that provision should lead to a purchase-price adjustment, a closing condition or a negotiating concession. AI therefore informs but does not replace independent professional judgment. Every AI-enabled output still requires review, verification and refinement by counsel who understands the transaction and can explain the basis for the advice. ABA Formal Opinion 512 reflects the same principle: generative AI tools can enhance the efficiency and quality of legal services, but they cannot substitute for the independent professional judgment of counsel.

news.titleEn: Elevate Buys Lupl in Software Business Expansion
news.titleZh: Elevate收购Lupl，扩展软件业务
news.summaryZh: Elevate已收购法律项目管理平台Lupl，该平台此前获得CMS、Cooley和Rajah & Tann Asia的支持。这是这家现已多元化的法律公司一系列收购中的最新一笔，Elevate自身也提供软件产品。Elevate已拥有自己的ELM（企业法律管理）系统，以及为法律团队提供代理自动化的ELMA。Lupl于2020年推出，并随时代发展。如今，该平台“将代理AI与任务管理、协作和工作流自动化相结合，最近通过一套专门围绕Claude构建的能力实现”。简言之，此次收购将强化Elevate的软件战略。此次收购是Elevate软件业务的重要下一步。”“Lupl打造了一个定义品类的平台、一支才华横溢的团队以及包括一些全球领先律师事务所在内的强大客户群。与ELM和ELMA一起，Lupl推进了我们通过连接跨事项和工作流的团队与数据来自动化法律工作的愿景。”目前，Lupl主要帮助“管理复杂的法律事项，从跨境并购交易和多司法管辖区监管项目到高风险争议”。该平台支持事项的全生命周期，包括“受理和范围界定、规划和预算、任务和截止日期跟踪、客户协作以及进度报告”——这将与Elevate同样于2020年推出的ELM系统良好连接。Elevate现在将开发该平台，并将其覆盖范围扩展至Elevate的全球法律部门和律师事务所客户群。法律正在改变，法律工作的管理方式也随之改变。用电子表格和便利贴管理法律项目的时代即将结束。加入Elevate为我们提供了规模、资源和覆盖范围，以定义下一步发展，并将其带给更多法律团队。
news.bodyText: Elevate has bought Lupl, the legal project management platform backed by CMS, Cooley, and Rajah & Tann Asia. It’s the latest in a series of acquisitions from the now multifaceted law company, which also has its own software offering. (See AL interview below). Elevate already has its own ELM (enterprise legal management) system, as well as ELMA, which provides agentic automation for legal teams. Meanwhile, Lupl launched back in 2020 and has evolved with the times. Today, the platform ‘integrates agentic AI with task management, collaboration, and workflow automation, most recently through a set of capabilities built specifically around Claude’. In short, you can see how the acquisition will bolster Elevate’s software strategy. Liam Brown, Chairman and CEO, Elevate, commented: ‘This acquisition is an important next step for Elevate’s software business.’ ‘Lupl has built a category-defining platform, a talented team, and a strong customer base that includes some of the world’s leading law firms. Together with ELM and ELMA, Lupl advances our vision for automating legal work by connecting teams and data across matters and workflows.’ At present, Lupl primarily helps ‘to manage complex legal matters, from cross-border M&A transactions and multi-jurisdictional regulatory projects to high-stakes disputes’ they said. The platform supports the full life of a matter, including ‘intake and scoping, planning and budgeting, task and deadline tracking, client collaboration, and progress reporting’ – and that will connect well with Elevate’s ELM system, which was also launched in 2020. Elevate will now develop the platform and extend its reach across Elevate’s global customer base of law departments and law firms. Jeff Green, CEO of Lupl, commented: ‘Law is changing, and the way legal work gets managed is changing with it. The days of running legal projects on spreadsheets and post-it notes are ending. Joining Elevate gives us the scale, resources, and reach to define what comes next, and to bring it to many more legal teams.’ AL Interview with Elevate Why do this and why now? AI is being bolted onto legal processes, but the way those processes are managed hasn’t changed much in 20 years. It is often still email threads, Excel trackers and Post-it notes. As AI accelerates the throughput and velocity of legal work, these legacy processes are no longer fit for purpose, and the need for a system to organise and orchestrate legal work for human + agent teams has become more urgent.

news.titleEn: Why General AI Alone Is Not Enough for Legal Work
news.titleZh: 为何通用AI不足以胜任法律工作
news.summaryZh: 法律科技领域“AI驱动”一词已被过度使用和炒作。如今几乎所有法律科技供应商都声称拥有能处理复杂法律工作的AI方案，通用AI提供商也宣扬其法律能力，导致市场拥挤、买家难以区分专用AI方案与披着法律外衣的聊天机器人。这种混乱的根源在于对AI能为法律顾问做什么、不能做什么普遍缺乏了解。通用AI无疑改变了法律格局，为法律团队和律所带来显著效率提升，能总结分析合同库、修订文件并加速研究。但仅有能力还不够。通用AI模型被训练为广泛适用于大量任务，可谓“博而不精”，其基于公开信息训练，优化生成看似合理、上下文相关的回答。例如律师审查供应商合同时要求AI识别异常条款，通用模型虽能对照训练数据中的模式，却无法理解该供应商关系如何契合公司采购战略、某些偏差能否获批、或哪些合同风险在特定情境下商业上可接受。除非提供指导，AI做出判断的能力有限，如同极其聪明却有些过度热心的实习生。为充分发挥通用AI能力，需认识其局限，合同相关工作的一些主要局限包括：可在几个简单用例中考虑这些局限。
news.bodyText: By Senne Mennes, LawVu. Few terms in legal technology have become as overused as ‘AI-powered.’ Not to mention over-hyped. Today, virtually every legal tech vendor claims that they have AI solutions capable of handling complex legal work, while general-purpose AI providers themselves also tout legal capabilities. This creates confusion and a crowded market where buyers struggle to distinguish between a fit-for-purpose AI solution and a chatbot dressed up in legal clothing. Underpinning this confusion is a general lack of knowledge about what AI can do for counsel, and what it can’t. We thought it was time to change that. General-purpose AI has unquestionably changed the legal landscape by creating serious efficiency gains for both legal teams and law firms. AI can summarize and analyze repositories of contracts, redline documents, and accelerate research in ways that would have seemed impossible just a few years ago. There’s no denying that general AI is incredibly capable, but it’s important to recognize that capability alone is not enough. General-purpose AI vs purpose-built tools General AI models are trained to be broadly useful across an enormous range of tasks; think of it as a jack-of-all-trades and master of none. They are trained on vast collections of publicly available information and are optimized to generate plausible, contextually relevant responses. A lawyer reviewing a supplier contract might ask an AI system to identify unusual provisions. While a general model can compare the document against patterns it has observed in training data, it cannot inherently understand how that supplier relationship fits within the company’s procurement strategy, if certain deviations can be approved, or which contractual risks are commercially acceptable in that specific context. In other words: AI is limited in its capacity to make judgment calls unless guidance is provided – not unlike an extremely intelligent, somewhat overzealous intern. news.titleEn: Intapp announces re-architected Compliance and Time solutions, with Intapp Celeste at the core
news.titleZh: Intapp宣布重新架构合规与时间解决方案，以Intapp Celeste为核心
news.summaryZh:
Intapp（纳斯达克代码：INTA）于2026年8月19日宣布推出Compliance with Celeste和Time with Celeste，即其合规与时间解决方案以Intapp Celeste和代理式工作流为核心重新架构。这些解决方案通过新的授权提供给律所，将Celeste的代理能力引入客户接纳、风险与收入流程，覆盖Intapp Intake、Conflicts、Terms和Time。它们处理重复性工作，让人员专注于需要人类判断的任务。

在风险方面，并购、整合和横向招聘带来的增长使新业务引入和风险管理日益复杂，表格、检索和义务检查量可能超出专家团队能力。在收入方面，AI提高工作效率，使计费小时承压，客户期望定价反映效率，律所需要实验新收费结构，这需要数据洞察支持。Compliance with Celeste和Time with Celeste利用各律所自身数据和规则应对这两方面压力。在Intake、Conflicts和Terms中，Celeste填写请求表单、标记缺失数据、构建检索策略、映射公司树、运行检索并分类结果、读取外部律师指南并提取关键条款，用户可在Intake、Conflicts、Terms或Outlook中提问或启动剧本。在Time中，Celeste起草完整时间条目、撰写叙述、标记块计费并帮助拆分或重写，并整合工作活动、计费规则和财务数据展示实现率、事项经济性、利用率和AI工具表现。这些解决方案标志着Intapp转向代理优先平台，采用Firm AI方法。现有客户可升级，激活授权后新功能在现有环境中可用。
news.bodyHtml:
New, agent-first solutions – Compliance with Celeste and Time with Celeste – bring agentic AI that knows how the firm works to the workflows behind profitable, compliant growth, from business acceptance and client risk management to timekeeping and revenue governance

PALO ALTO, Calif. — August 19, 2026 — Intapp (NASDAQ: INTA), the governed AI platform for professional firms in highly regulated industries, today announced the availability of Compliance with Celeste and Time with Celeste – its Compliance and Time solutions re-architected with Intapp Celeste and agentic workflows at their core. Available to firms through a new entitlement, these solutions bring the agentic capabilities of Celeste into the client acceptance, risk, and revenue processes law firms and other professional firms run in Intapp Intake, Conflicts, Terms, and Time. They handle the repetitive parts of that work so people can focus their time on work that requires human judgment.

AI is changing the economics of law firms and other professional firms by squeezing them in two directions at once.

On the risk side, growth through M&A, consolidation, and lateral moves makes onboarding new business and managing risk increasingly complex. The volume of forms, searches, and obligation checks required to support that growth can quickly outpace the capacity of expert teams, whose expertise is scarce and takes years to develop. When highly skilled professionals spend too much time on repetitive tasks instead of judgment, firms face a difficult trade-off between moving intake forward quickly and maintaining rigorous risk management.

Revenue is the other side of the equation. As AI helps people work faster, the billable hour — the backbone of most firm revenue — comes under pressure. Clients increasingly expect pricing that reflects those efficiencies, and firms will need room to experiment with new fee structures to deliver it. This experimentation will only work with the right data and insights behind it. Without visibility into how AI-assisted work and other hours add up at the matter level, firms lack the insight needed to make critical decisions about what to scope, what to charge, who to staff, and where to invest in AI.

Compliance with Celeste and Time with Celeste meet both pressures head-on, bringing agentic AI directly into these workflows using each firm’s own data and rules.

How Celeste helps Compliance

Inside Intake, Conflicts, and Terms, Celeste takes on the repetitive parts of intake and risk work so experts can get to the analysis and judgment.

  • Faster, cleaner intake. Celeste fills in request forms using information from the emails people already share, then flags missing or incomplete data before anything gets submitted.
  • The busywork behind each decision, handled. Celeste builds the search strategy, maps corporate trees, runs the searches, and triages what comes back for expert review.
  • Client obligations that don’t slip. Celeste reads outside counsel guidelines, matches them to the right client, pulls out key terms, and files the attributes that matter.
  • Answers right where you work. Ask Celeste a question or kick off a playbook from a prompt inside Intake, Conflicts, Terms, or directly in Outlook.

How Celeste helps Time

Inside Time, Celeste captures hours that would otherwise be lost, helps prevent revenue leakage, and gives firms a clearer view of what each matter is actually worth.

  • Time entries ready to bill. Celeste drafts complete entries from the work it already sees and fills in the gaps.
  • Revenue governance without the manual work. With agentic time entry, Celeste writes each narrative for you and can rewrite the ones you enter yourself. Both stay compliant with outside counsel guidelines and firm style.
  • Block-billing, caught early. When an entry breaks the rules, Celeste flags it and helps you either split it or rewrite the narrative.
  • Analytics that connect the dots. Celeste pulls together work activity, billing rules, and financial data to show what’s driving realization, matter economics, utilization, and AI tool performance.

These solutions mark Intapp’s shift to an agent-first platform. Intake, Conflicts, Terms, and Time no longer just support human-led work; Celeste now carries that work forward with people stepping in where judgment matters most. Each solution runs on the same foundation of structured data, agentic workflows, systems of record, context, and guardrails, which is what lets Celeste do real work inside regulated processes. Intapp calls this approach Firm AI – agentic AI applied to the business of the firm itself, not just to individual tasks or work products.

Availability

Firms already running their business acceptance, time, and billing with Intapp can upgrade to the new agentic AI offerings. Once the new entitlement is activated, the new capabilities will be available in their existing environments. To see them in action, firms can book a demo or talk to their Intapp account team at intapp.com.

Supporting quotes

Thad Jampol, Co-Founder and Chief Product Officer, Intapp

“Intapp is now agent-first. We’ve re-architected our Compliance and Time solutions with Celeste and agentic workflows at their core, so the agents, the data they run on, and the compliance guardrails all come from one place. Pulling that together is the hard part, and it’s the part no one else has done. That’s what makes Compliance with Celeste and Time with Celeste real for firms – the agents do meaningful work inside regulated processes, on each firm’s own data and under its own rules.”

Katherine Lowry, Chief Information Officer and Head of IncuBaker, BakerHostetler

“There is really no true beginning or end to a workday in a law firm. Knowing that Celeste is there all the time is key. We believe that Celeste can have a very positive impact on our intake and conflicts process. Celeste’s cutting-edge AI capabilities will help us responsibly take on matters and evaluate conflicts faster than ever before. At BakerHostetler, we have experienced tremendous lateral growth in recent years and as a result, have onboarded a significant number of important new clients and complex engagements. We believe that Celeste will help us operate more efficiently as we continue to grow.”

news.bodyText:
New, agent-first solutions – Compliance with Celeste and Time with Celeste – bring agentic AI that knows how the firm works to the workflows behind profitable, compliant growth, from business acceptance and client risk management to timekeeping and revenue governance

PALO ALTO, Calif. — August 19, 2026 — Intapp (NASDAQ: INTA), the governed AI platform for professional firms in highly regulated industries, today announced the availability of Compliance with Celeste and Time with Celeste – its Compliance and Time solutions re-architected with Intapp Celeste and agentic workflows at their core. Available to firms through a new entitlement, these solutions bring the agentic capabilities of Celeste into the client acceptance, risk, and revenue processes law firms and other professional firms run in Intapp Intake, Conflicts, Terms, and Time. They handle the repetitive parts of that work so people can focus their time on work that requires human judgment.

AI is changing the economics of law firms and other professional firms by squeezing them in two directions at once.

On the risk side, growth through M&A, consolidation, and lateral moves makes onboarding new business and managing risk increasingly complex. The volume of forms, searches, and obligation checks required to support that growth can quickly outpace the capacity of expert teams, whose expertise is scarce and takes years to develop. When highly skilled professionals spend too much time on repetitive tasks instead of judgment, firms face a difficult trade-off between moving intake forward quickly and maintaining rigorous risk management.

Revenue is the other side of the equation. As AI helps people work faster, the billable hour — the backbone of most firm revenue — comes under pressure. Clients increasingly expect pricing that reflects those efficiencies, and firms will need room to experiment with new fee structures to deliver it. This experimentation will only work with the right data and insights behind it. Without visibility into how AI-assisted work and other hours add up at the matter level, firms lack the insight needed to make critical decisions about what to scope, what to charge, who to staff, and where to invest in AI.

Compliance with Celeste and Time with Celeste meet both pressures head-on, bringing agentic AI directly into these workflows using each firm’s own data and rules.

Inside Intake, Conflicts, and Terms, Celeste takes on the repetitive parts of intake and risk work so experts can get to the analysis and judgment.

Faster, cleaner intake. Celeste fills in request forms using information from the emails people already share, then flags missing or incomplete data before anything gets submitted.

The busywork behind each decision, handled. Celeste builds the search strategy, maps corporate trees, runs the searches, and triages what comes back for expert review.

Client obligations that don’t slip. Celeste reads outside counsel guidelines, matches them to the right client, pulls out key terms, and files the attributes that matter.

Answers right where you work. Ask Celeste a question or kick off a playbook from a prompt inside Intake, Conflicts, Terms, or directly in Outlook.

Inside Time, Celeste captures hours that would otherwise be lost, helps prevent revenue leakage, and gives firms a clearer view of what each matter is actually worth.

Time entries ready to bill. Celeste drafts complete entries from the work it already sees and fills in the gaps.

Revenue governance without the manual work. With agentic time entry, Celeste writes each narrative for you and can rewrite the ones you enter yourself. Both stay compliant with outside counsel guidelines and firm style.

Block-billing, caught early. When an entry breaks the rules, Celeste flags it and helps you either split it or rewrite the narrative.

Analytics that connect the dots. Celeste pulls together work activity, billing rules, and financial data to show what’s driving realization, matter economics, utilization, and AI tool performance.

These solutions mark Intapp’s shift to an agent-first platform. Intake, Conflicts, Terms, and Time no longer just support human-led work; Celeste now carries that work forward with people stepping in where judgment matters most. Each solution runs on the same foundation of structured data, agentic workflows, systems of record, context, and guardrails, which is what lets Celeste do real work inside regulated processes. Intapp calls this approach Firm AI – agentic AI applied to the business of the firm itself, not just to individual tasks or work products.

Firms already running their business acceptance, time, and billing with Intapp can upgrade to the new agentic AI offerings. Once the new entitlement is activated, the new capabilities will be available in their existing environments. To see them in action, firms can book a demo or talk to their Intapp account team at intapp.com .

Thad Jampol, Co-Founder and Chief Product Officer, Intapp

“Intapp is now agent-first. We’ve re-architected our Compliance and Time solutions with Celeste and agentic workflows at their core, so the agents, the data they run on, and the compliance guardrails all come from one place. Pulling that together is the hard part, and it’s the part no one else has done. That’s what makes Compliance with Celeste and Time with Celeste real for firms – the agents do meaningful work inside regulated processes, on each firm’s own data and under its own rules.”

Katherine Lowry, Chief Information Officer and Head of IncuBaker, BakerHostetler

“There is really no true beginning or end to a workday in a law firm. Knowing that Celeste is there all the time is key. We believe that Celeste can have a very positive impact on our intake and conflicts process. Celeste’s cutting-edge AI capabilities will help us responsibly take on matters and evaluate conflicts faster than ever before. At BakerHostetler, we have experienced tremendous lateral growth in recent years and as a result, have onboarded a significant number of important new clients and complex engagements. We believe that Celeste will help us operate more efficiently as we continue to grow.”

news.bodyHtml:
Practice the future of law today

With Clio Work, you go beyond generic chatbots and use AI that understands the context of your matters and delivers precise, cited legal research, analysis, and drafting that moves your cases forward.

Discover Clio Work
news.bodyText: From court activity to legal work 1. Never miss a court development Search for a public court case by party, case number, keyword, or court, then connect it to the corresponding matter in Clio. From there, Clio Docket monitors the case for new filings, court orders, and scheduling changes. When the court moves, your firm receives an alert tied to the relevant matter, so the team can see what changed and determine what needs attention next. I ve been asking Clio to build this for years. I wake up to an alert that something was filed overnight, and right away I know what matters and what to act on, said Dmitriy Stadlin, a solo litigator practicing criminal defense and civil rights. 2. Find the filing without the extra work When a court document is available online, you can retrieve it through Clio Docket and save it directly to the relevant client matter. Traditionally, lawyers retrieve those same documents through PACER or another court system, where filings are generally purchased on a per-page basis. It s also common to ask around the firm to see whether someone has already paid for the document before purchasing it again. Clio Docket works differently. Once a court document has been purchased and added to Clio Docket s collection, it can be accessed by other Clio Docket customers without requiring each firm to purchase the same filing again. That means you re searching more than 1 billion U.S. court filings through a continually growing collection that expands as new documents become available. Instead of repeatedly paying for the same filings, you can spend less time tracking them down and more time putting them to work. When you find the filing you need, you can save it directly to the client matter and immediately use it in Clio Work to inform your research, strategy, and drafting. 3. See what changed in the case and decide what to do next A new filing is only one part of what the docket tells you. The docket also shows how the case has developed, which deadlines or scheduled events may be affected, and what the team may need to address next. Whether you open the docket proactively or arrive through an alert, you can review the latest development alongside the history of the case and the broader context of the matter. From there, the work continues in Clio Work. Research the legal issues raised by the development, compare relevant motions, briefs, pleadings, and orders from other proceedings, and use those materials to shape your strategy and drafting. Instead of treating the alert, the filing, and the resulting legal work as separate steps, the firm can move from seeing what changed to deciding what to do next. Clio Docket has saved me three times already. I ll get an alert that something needs to be filed today, when I only had vague knowledge it even needed to be filed. As a solo, that s the difference between catching it and not, said Amanda Simmons, a solo litigator specializing in special education and civil litigation. 4. Keep the matter moving in Clio Manage Legal work doesn t end when the research or drafting is complete. Clio Work connects with Clio Manage, so the work remains tied to the operational life of the matter. Retrieved filings, court activity, deadlines, tasks, communications, documents, time, and billing stay connected to the same client record. For litigation teams, Clio Manage becomes the operational hub for the matter. New court activity can trigger updated deadlines, follow-up tasks, and next steps without relying on disconnected emails, spreadsheets, or manual updates. The more everything integrates, the more it becomes a clean hub of all your relevant facts, matters, billables. You see everything in one place. That just streamlines the time the attorney has to spend on the matter, said Adam Grant, a solo litigator practicing in LA County probate. 5. Built as a connected legal AI platform This workflow reflects how Clio is intentionally designed as a legal AI platform. Rather than separating the systems used to manage matters from the tools used to perform legal work, Clio brings them together around a shared understanding of the client matter. Court activity discovered through Clio Docket flows naturally into research, strategy, and drafting in Clio Work, while the resulting deadlines, documents, tasks, communications, time, and billing continue in Clio Manage. The result is continuity. Instead of repeatedly moving information between disconnected tools, your firm s context moves with the matter, helping you understand what changed, determine what to do next, and carry that work through to resolution. Built on Docket Alarm Clio Docket was introduced at ClioCon 2025 as the evolution of Docket Alarm. The latest release brings its court search, document retrieval, and docket monitoring capabilities directly into Clio Work and Clio Manage for eligible solo, small, and midsized firms. Together with Clio Work and Clio Manage, Clio Docket extends Clio s connected legal AI platform from managing matters to understanding and acting on what s happening in court. Start your free trial of Clio Work today Clio Docket is one more example of how Clio is expanding what s possible with a connected legal AI platform. While Clio Docket helps bring court activity into your workflow, Clio Work helps you turn that information into action through AI-powered research, strategy, and drafting, all grounded in the context of your matters. Start your free trial to explore how Clio Work helps legal professionals move work forward. Start your free Clio Work trial . news.bodyHtml:
At ILTACON, Litera will preview how deterministic redlines, firm-approved precedent, and agentic change management work together

 

CHICAGO – Aug. 18, 2026 – Litera, the Legal AI platform provider that best unifies the practice and business of law, announced new capabilities that connect contract drafting and negotiation in one trusted Legal AI workflow. From sourcing firm-approved precedent and building the first draft to comparing versions, understanding risk and proposing response language, Litera keeps the work connected instead of forcing lawyers across separate tools. The announcement includes new Lito workflows, Litera’s award-winning Legal AI agent, in Microsoft Word and Litera for Windows, a modern desktop experience that brings Litera’s Legal AI platform directly to a user’s computer.

Litera is the only Legal AI provider that combines deterministic accuracy for high-stakes work with modern LLM intelligence, delivered through one agent and built on 30 years of legal-specific expertise. Most Legal AI platforms rely primarily on probabilistic foundation models. Even when fine-tuned for legal work, outputs can vary and require extensive verification. That creates the Trust Gap: AI promises speed, but the value disappears when lawyers must recheck every result. Litera closes that gap by applying the right AI to each task. Its proprietary deterministic engines provide repeatable, verifiable results where precision matters. LLM-powered intelligence builds on that foundation to surface insights, accelerate workflows, and handle complexity that rules alone cannot reach. 

 

“Negotiation is where a matter is won or lost, and where a single missed change carries the most risk,” said Adam Ryan, Chief Product Officer, Litera. “Yet most Legal AI stops at the first draft, leaving lawyers to read redlines line by line under deadline. If a lawyer still has to recheck everything, the value of AI was never really created. Litera closes that gap with intelligent connected workflows built on 30 years of legal expertise and each firm’s approved knowledge, so our lawyers can focus on the strategy behind the deal, not the mechanics of tracking changes.”

 

Litera’s connected contract drafting and negotiation workflow follows the way legal work actually moves:start from firm knowledge, see exactly what changed, and then act with confidence.

  • Start from firm-approved precedent: Available now, Precedent within Litera Create Content lets lawyers search the firm’s curated content library and document management system for gold-standard clauses, definitions, and precedent documents. Lawyers build first drafts from language the firm has already approved and negotiated successfully. 
  • See exactly what changed: When the opposing side returns a new version, Litera’sdeterministic comparison engine shows every change in a redesigned unified viewer across browser and desktop. Litera for Windows adds right-click comparison from Windows Explorer and direct redline sharing through Outlook. Comparison also sits within Lito, keeping the redlinein the same Legal AI experience where the negotiation continues.
  • Act on what matters: Beginning in late September, Lito’s Manage Changes workflow in Word will build AI-powered change management on top of Litera Compare’s deterministic redline. It will surface changes that carry risk, explain the impact of each one, and suggest rewrites, so lawyers spend time on consequences rather than spotting edits. Grounding those suggested rewrites in the firm’s own approved precedent is planned for Q4.

The result is one connected negotiation loop that answers what changed, what it means, and what to send back. For firms, that is how the Practice of Law creates legal value: trusted work, stronger outcomes, less rework, and time returned to lawyers. It also advances the full Return on AI (RoAI), because reclaimed capacity creates more value when it strengthens client trust and makes room for the next matter.

 

“Lito helped me review and compare over 40 leases,” said Brian Corbett, Partner, Poyner Spruill. “What would have taken five hours took 30 to 45 minutes.”

Litera for Windows

Litera for Windows combines the Litera for Web experience, embedded Lito capabilities, and the deterministic comparison engine used across the legal industry in a modern, native Windows application. Lito is embedded in Litera for Windows, offering all the power of Litera’s AI skills and workflows directly from a user’s home screen. Users can compare multiple document sets, launch right-click comparisons from Windows Explorer, and send redlines directly through Outlook. 

This is the first step in bringing Litera’s unified platform experience from the web to the desktop, with Litera for Mac coming soon. Litera for Windows reaches General Availability on Aug. 24.

At ILTACON: Extending the Connected Matter into Agentic Due Diligence

At ILTACON, Litera will demonstrate the Due Diligence Agent, an integration of Lito and AI-powered contract intelligence platform Kira that takes an M&A deal team from data room to client-ready draft report in a single guided workflow. Kira handles document classification and extraction; Lito orchestrates the workflow and drafts the report section by section, structured to the firm’s own precedent reports. Every finding is traceable back to the underlying extraction and source document, and the agent pauses for lawyer review at each phase rather than substituting for legal judgment. It is the latest example of how Litera is building Earned Intelligence across the matter lifecycle: a firm’s precedents and prior work shape each new draft instead of every deal starting from scratch. The integration is expected to be available in Q4.

Visit Litera at ILTACON, Aug. 24–27, Booth #301. To see the drafting and negotiation workflow or the Lito and Kira demonstration, or to arrange a briefing with Litera executives, visit info.litera.com/iltacon.html. For more information, visit litera.com/iltacon.

About Litera
Litera is the Legal AI platform provider that best unifies the practice and business of law, built on 30 years of legal expertise that no AI startup can shortcut, and engineered for the decades ahead. The company combines purpose-built legal technology with Lito, its award-winning Legal AI agent, to Raise The Bar™ for the legal profession worldwide. With AI solutions spanning legal drafting, document comparison, contract review, knowledge management, business development, and more, Litera serves over 15,000 global customers and more than 1 million daily users, including 99% of the Am Law 100. Integrated directly into Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace across devices, Litera delivers the right data, in the right place, at the right time – reducing context-switching so lawyers can practice law, not manage tools, while winning more business, driving efficiency and the deeper client relationships that fuel sustainable growth. For more information, visit litera.com or follow us on LinkedIn.

 

Press Contacts

Jared Albert

PR and Communications, Litera

jared.albert@litera.com

 

Tracy Wemett

BroadPR, Inc. for Litera

twemett@broadpr.com

+1 617-939-3631

news.titleEn: Clio Docket Is Now In Clio Work, Combining An AI Workspace with Access to More Than 1 Billion Court Filings
news.titleZh: Clio Docket 现已集成至 Clio Work，将 AI 工作空间与超过 10 亿份法院文件访问权限相结合
news.summaryZh: Clio 于 2025 年收购 vLex 时获得了 Docket Alarm，该数据库收录了来自联邦和州法院的超过 10 亿份文件。在去年的 ClioCon 用户大会上，Clio 将其重新推出为 Clio Docket。现在，Clio 将 Clio Docket 集成到其 AI 驱动的法律工作环境 Clio Work 中，使用户能够将公开法院案卷与对应客户事项关联、监控案卷新动态、检索相关文件，并立即开始后续实质性法律工作。该集成带来三项功能：监控公开案卷、搜索联邦和州法院文件以及检索底层文档。律师可按当事人、案号、关键词或法院搜索，以检索自己案件中的文件，或查找其他诉讼中的相关动议、简报、诉状和命令。一旦律师将案件案卷与对应客户事项关联，Clio Docket 便会监控该案卷，并就新文件、命令和日程变更向律师发出提醒。随后，律师可使用 Clio Work 研究新动态引发的问题，比较其他诉讼中的类似动议、简报、诉状和命令，并开始起草回应。据我 4 月报道，solo、small and mid-sized law firms 现在可以购买 Clio Work 作为独立产品，但 Clio 表示它与 Clio Manage 配合使用效果更佳。Clio Docket 还通过共享文档集合帮助律师节省案卷下载费用：一旦任何 Clio Work 客户通过 Clio Docket 购买或添加文档，该文档便可供事务所内任何人在无需额外付费的情况下使用，从而避免向 PACER 等来源支付下载费用。Clio Docket 是 Docket Alarm 的演进，后者由 Michael Sander 创立，于 2018 年被 Fastcase 收购，2023 年 vLex 与 Fastcase 合并，2025 年 6 月 Clio 以 10 亿美元收购 vLex。
news.bodyHtml:
When Clio acquired vLex in 2025, a key asset it gained was Docket Alarm, one of the world’s largest litigation databases containing more than 1 billion filings from federal and state courts. At the ClioCon user conference last year, Clio relaunched it as Clio Docket.

Now, Clio is making Clio Docket available from within Clio Work, its AI-driven legal work environment, enabling users to connect public court dockets to the corresponding client matters, monitor those dockets for new activity, retrieve relevant filings, and immediately begin any substantive legal work that follows.

The addition brings three capabilities to Clio Work: monitoring of public dockets, search across federal and state court filings, and retrieval of the underlying documents. Lawyers can search by party, case number, keyword or court to retrieve documents from their own cases or to find relevant motions, briefs, pleadings and orders from other proceedings.

Once a lawyer connects a case docket to the corresponding client matter, Clio Docket watches that docket and alerts the lawyer to new filings, orders and scheduling changes.

Using Clio Work, the lawyer can then research the issues raised by a new development; compare similar motions, briefs, pleadings and orders from other proceedings; and begin drafting a response.

As I reported in April, solo, small and mid-sized law firms can now purchase Clio Work as a standalone product. But Clio says it is better together with Clio Manage, its flagship practice management platform.

“Clio Work and Clio Manage work in tandem to give legal professionals one complete picture of the matter,” the company said in a press release. “As substantive legal work is completed in Clio Work, it carries into the matter in Clio Manage, alongside the deadlines, tasks, communications, time, billing, and other activity tied to that client and matter.”

Clio Docket can also help lawyers save money on docket downloads by providing access to a shared document collection. Once any Clio Work customer purchases or adds a document via Clio Docket, the document is available to anyone within the firm at no extra charge.

That avoids the need to pay a source such as PACER to download a document someone else has already purchased.

(Note that some other products have a similar feature, including CourtListener and PacerPro.)

From Docket Alarm to Clio, via vLex

Clio Docket is the evolution of Docket Alarm, the litigation analytics and docket-research platform founded by Michael Sander.

In 2018, Docket Alarm was acquired by Fastcase, the U.S. legal research company. In 2023, vLex merged with Fastcase, bringing Docket Alarm’s court-data collection into the vLex fold alongside its Vincent AI research technology.

Then, in June 2025, Clio acquired vLex for $1 billion, folding all of that legal research and docket data into Clio’s practice management platform.

Clio introduced Clio Docket at ClioCon 2025 as Docket Alarm’s next chapter, and today’s release delivers on that by bringing court search, document retrieval, and docket monitoring directly into Clio Work’s AI suite.
