news.bodyHtml:
Intapp, the publicly traded company whose software manages intake, conflicts, and deal workflows for law firms and other professional services firms, yesterday announced the general availability of Celeste, an agentic AI product it describes as an “expert AI coworker” designed to run the business operations of a firm — from deal screening and conflicts clearance to business development and lateral hiring.

The launch, announced during a global broadcast event, comes roughly five months after Intapp first previewed Celeste at its annual product event in New York in February, where the company described it as a purpose-built agentic AI platform for professional firms in regulated industries.

Since then, Celeste has been in limited release with early-adopter firms, including the law firm BakerHostetler and the private equity firm Hg.

For the Business, Not the Practice, of Law

With Celeste, Intapp is targeting what it sees as a gap in legal AI. While most firms now have AI assistants on every desk, drafting and reviewing faster than ever, that AI is built for the individual practitioner. It speeds up the practice of law without speeding up the business behind it.

Intapp’s answer to that gap is what it is branding “Firm AI,” a category it distinguishes from horizontal assistants (general-purpose tools for everyday tasks) and practice AI (tools that help produce the legal work product itself). Firm AI is aimed at the operational side of the firm, functions such as origination, intake, conflicts, pricing and hiring.

“Firms will run several kinds of AI: horizontal assistants for everyday work, practice AI for the work product, and Firm AI for the business of the firm itself,” said Thad Jampol, Intapp’s co-founder and chief product officer, in a statement. “That last category is the hard one, and it’s the one almost nobody is building.”

“When a conflicts team can clear 10 times the matters and a fund can screen 10 times the deals, that’s not saved time — that’s a new business model,” he said.

(Jampol lays out more of his thinking on this in A Blueprint for Firm AI, co-authored with Intapp’s chairman and CEO John Hall.)

Executing Multi-Step Workflows

According to Intapp, Celeste operates autonomously rather than waiting to be prompted, executing multi-step workflows designed as playbooks. It ships with a library of playbooks covering origination, business development, intake, conflicts, pricing, fundraising and lateral hiring, along with a no-code builder that lets firms create their own.

“Celeste encodes the firm’s own methods as playbooks — multi-step workflows that automate the firm’s best practices,” the company says.

The product is natively integrated with a firm’s systems of record — which makes sense given that Intapp’s applications already sit atop the intake, conflicts and relationship data of many large firms — andit  can ingest the firm’s documents and connect to outside data partners through open connectors.

On the governance front, Intapp says the same ethical walls, need-to-know restrictions, and audit requirements that apply to a firm’s people apply equally to Celeste. Restricted information stays restricted regardless of who asks, and firms can produce a full record of every action the AI takes for clients and regulators.

Intapp had previously announced a partnership with Harvey, allowing Celeste to invoke Harvey’s practice-of-law workflows while enforcing compliance and ethical wall standards. It similarly announced a partnership with Anthropic to bring its Claude models into Intapp’s governed environment.

Feedback from Early Adopters

For law firms specifically, Intapp says Celeste can surface relevant matters, partner experience, and prior pitch materials in response to an urgent client request in minutes rather than hours, and can run an end-to-end lateral hiring lifecycle, from candidate research and conflicts pre-screening through clearance preparation and onboarding.

At BakerHostetler, the focus so far has been on intake and conflicts. according to Katherine Lowry, the firm’s chief information officer and head of its IncuBaker innovation team.

“We believe that Celeste can have a very positive impact on our intake and conflicts process,” she said in a statement provided by Intapp, adding that the firm’s substantial lateral growth in recent years has brought a significant volume of new clients and complex engagements. “We believe that Celeste will help us operate more efficiently as we continue to grow.”

At Hg, the appeal is that the AI works from the firm’s own accumulated knowledge. “The intelligence is ours, not something generic applied to our firm,” said Shirin Veeran, who leads data and platform strategy at Hg, in a statement. “Celeste screens against our actual mandate, drawing on knowledge we have built across the firm over two decades.”

My Take

Intapp is not alone in seeking to stake a claim on the business side of legal AI — territory that Harvey, CoCounsel, and the rest of the practice-focused AI products are not directly contesting.

And it is, unquestionably, an area where the potential impact of AI could be significant. Large-firm workflows such as conflicts clearance, intake, lateral hiring, and others often remain highly inefficient, with process improvement hindered by the proprietary nature of firm data.

This is an area in which Intapp has the advantage of incumbency. It has spent two decades embedding itself in the systems of record where that data lives, and that makes it a natural home for AI that acts on that data.

Intapp had previously announced a partnership with Harvey , allowing Celeste to invoke Harvey’s practice-of-law workflows while enforcing compliance and ethical wall standards. It similarly announced a partnership with Anthropic to bring its Claude models into Intapp’s governed environment.

Feedback from Early Adopters

For law firms specifically, Intapp says Celeste can surface relevant matters, partner experience, and prior pitch materials in response to an urgent client request in minutes rather than hours, and can run an end-to-end lateral hiring lifecycle, from candidate research and conflicts pre-screening through clearance preparation and onboarding.

At BakerHostetler, the focus so far has been on intake and conflicts. according to Katherine Lowry , the firm’s chief information officer and head of its IncuBaker innovation team.

“We believe that Celeste can have a very positive impact on our intake and conflicts process,” she said in a statement provided by Intapp, adding that the firm’s substantial lateral growth in recent years has brought a significant volume of new clients and complex engagements. “We believe that Celeste will help us operate more efficiently as we continue to grow.”

At Hg, the appeal is that the AI works from the firm’s own accumulated knowledge. “The intelligence is ours, not something generic applied to our firm,” said Shirin Veeran , who leads data and platform strategy at Hg, in a statement. “Celeste screens against our actual mandate, drawing on knowledge we have built across the firm over two decades.”

My Take

Intapp is not alone in seeking to stake a claim on the business side of legal AI — territory that Harvey, CoCounsel, and the rest of the practice-focused AI products are not directly contesting.

And it is, unquestionably, an area where the potential impact of AI could be significant. Large-firm workflows such as conflicts clearance, intake, lateral hiring, and others often remain highly inefficient, with process improvement hindered by the proprietary nature of firm data.

This is an area in which Intapp has the advantage of incumbency. It has spent two decades embedding itself in the systems of record where that data lives, and that makes it a natural home for AI that acts on that data.

Bob Ambrogi

Bob is a lawyer, veteran legal journalist, and award-winning blogger and podcaster. In 2011, he was named to the inaugural Fastcase 50, honoring “the law’s smartest, most courageous innovators, techies, visionaries and leaders.” Earlier in his career, he was editor-in-chief of several legal publications, including The National Law Journal, and editorial director of ALM’s Litigation Services Division.

news.summaryZh: Relativity上周宣布，自2018年起担任首席产品官的Chris Brown被任命为公司总裁，任命于7月13日生效。在新职位上，Brown继续领导产品组织，同时将市场营销和技术合作纳入其职责范围。这一变动恰逢首席营销官Cristina Rossman在任职六年多后离职。此次任命之际，这家法律数据智能公司正进行一系列重要举措，包括6月收购由Dorna Moini创立的文档自动化公司Gavel，以及推出受治理的MCP集成，使Claude等AI助手能够在RelativityOne中编排事务和工作流程。周二，在Brown正式上任一天后，作者与他进行了对话，讨论将产品和营销合并于一位领导者之下的考量、收购Gavel的理由、Relativity向通用AI助手开放的原因、其aiR产品的采用轨迹，以及他在Orbitz构建消费旅游产品十年间积累的经验。对话记录经编辑，省略号表示省略内容，括号表示为清晰起见添加或替换的词语。
news.bodyHtml:
Last week, Relativity announced that Chris Brown, its chief product officer since 2018, had been named the company’s president, effective July 13. In the new role, Brown continues to lead Relativity’s product organization while adding marketing and technology partnerships to his scope — a change that coincides with the departure of Chief Marketing Officer Cristina Rossman after more than six years with the company.

The appointment comes amid a series of notable moves for the legal data intelligence company, including its June acquisition of Gavel, the document automation company founded by Dorna Moini, and its rollout of governed MCP integrations that allow AI assistants such as Claude to orchestrate matters and workflows within RelativityOne.

On Tuesday, a day after Brown officially stepped into the role, I sat down with him to talk about all of this — the thinking behind combining product and marketing under one leader, the rationale for the Gavel acquisition, why Relativity is opening itself up to general-purpose AI assistants, the adoption trajectory of its aiR products, and the lessons he carried over from a decade spent building consumer travel products at Orbitz.

Below is a transcript of that conversation, which I have edited for length, style and consistency. Ellipses indicate omitted text, and brackets indicate words added or substituted for clarity.

news.titleEn: Vanilla, Meatballs + Cooley’s Flat Fees – with David Wang

news.summaryZh: Cooley的基金设立平台Vanilla现将其业务中的关键环节——转让——以495美元的固定费用提供。Artificial Lawyer与Cooley创新主管David Wang探讨了定价应基于产出而非投入、法律市场动态的变化，以及宜家肉丸的类比。Vanilla是Cooley专为基金设立提供法律帮助和产品化服务而打造的平台，基金设立是这家加州律所的重要业务领域。但并非该工作的每个环节都需要全律师团队或按小时计费模式。事实上，部分法律工作可以低至495美元的固定费用出售给客户，对于这样一家律所而言这并不算多，因为初级律师一小时工作就可能收费如此。定价变化会在任何市场释放强大力量。更低的产出价格不一定意味着更差的律师。价格变动可以改变需求和购买量，从而推高利润。如果生产成本（即投入）也更低，更低的产出价格可以维持高利润率。新价格改变客户行为和忠诚度，并可激励购买更高价值的产品。总之，固定费用和产品化服务并不意味着大律所律师的PEP降低，只是比每年在小时费率上加5%并为手工工作填写时间表更复杂的模式。而且两者可以协同运作。法律经济学——Artificial Lawyer对法律科技和AI兴趣的基础——正日益成为对话的核心。讽刺的是，法律科技既不全是关于法律本身，也不只是技术。
news.bodyText: Cooley’s fund formation platform, Vanilla, is now offering a key element of its work – transfers – for a $495 flat fee. AL talked to Head of Innovation, David Wang, about how pricing should be all about outputs rather than inputs, the changing legal market dynamic, and the analogy of Ikea’s meatballs. In the short interview we unpack a lot, but the key points are as follows. Vanilla is a dedicated platform built by Cooley to provide legal help and productized services for fund formation – an important area for the California-based firm. But, it’s also where not every element of that work needs a full team of their lawyers, nor a billable hour model. In fact, as noted above, some components of this legal work can be sold to clients on a fixed fee for as little as $495. And that’s not a lot for a firm like this, given a junior associate might bill that for one hour of work. AL and Wang explore some of the key aspects here, which include: Overall, changes to pricing unleash incredibly powerful forces within any market. Moreover, lower output prices don’t necessarily mean poorer lawyers. Price shifts can change demand and the volume of purchases – and that can drive up profits. Lower output prices can sustain high profit margins if production costs – i.e. inputs – are also lower. New prices change customer behaviour and loyalty, and as noted above can incentivise purchases of higher value goods. In short, fixed fees and productised services do not mean Big Law lawyers with less PEP. It’s just a more complex model than adding 5% to the billable hour every year and filling in time sheets for the manual work performed. Moreover, also as explored, the two can operate in unison. Any road, legal economics – the foundation of Artificial Lawyer’s interest in legal tech and AI – is an area that is becoming more and more central to the conversation. Ironically, legal tech is neither all about the law itself, or just technology. Hey everybody, Richard Tromans here again, Artificial Lawyer TV doing a special interview today with David Wang from Cooley, ⁓ a legal innovator who you know well. ⁓ Today we’re gonna talk about Vanilla You may have seen some press on that already. We’re gonna dig into this. ⁓ David, good to have you with us. Tell us, what is Vanilla? David (00:00:33)

How is AI used in family law?

AI in family law streamlines high-volume tasks like document drafting, document analysis, client intake, scheduling calendar events, client communication, and billing. This helps attorneys reduce administrative workload and improve consistency, freeing lawyers to focus on strategy, negotiation, and client counseling, where judgment and empathy are essential.
news.bodyText: What is family law AI? Family law AI refers to artificial intelligence tools designed to help attorneys and legal staff automate, accelerate, and enhance work across divorce, custody, support, and related matters. These tools support solo practitioners and small to mid-sized firms alike by reducing administrative overhead, boosting workflow productivity, and strengthening case outcomes. Common applications of AI tools for family lawyers include document drafting, client communication, billing, and intake. In practice, this may involve generating drafts of pleadings or agreements, summarizing case files, organizing financial disclosures, drafting client updates, streamlining intake questionnaires, and automating client onboarding. By alleviating the burden of repetitive and administrative tasks, AI enables family lawyers to focus on strategy, negotiation, and client counseling, areas where legal judgment and human understanding are essential. How is AI used in family law? AI in family law streamlines high-volume tasks like document drafting, document analysis, client intake, scheduling calendar events, client communication, and billing. This helps attorneys reduce administrative workload and improve consistency, freeing lawyers to focus on strategy, negotiation, and client counseling, where judgment and empathy are essential. Key use cases for AI in family law practice AI tools for family law attorneys can be especially impactful in the day-to-day tasks that consume significant lawyer time and shape the client experience. Document drafting According to recent survey data , lawyers spend roughly 40% to 60% of their time drafting documents. Family lawyers in particular draft divorce petitions, custody agreements, parenting plans, and settlement letters, often under tight deadlines. Much of this work is repetitive and involves high document volume, making efficiency gains especially valuable in family law practice. Built into broader practice management workflows, Clio Draft helps firms automate document creation and generate routine family law documents more efficiently, without constant switching between disconnected tools. Legal research AI can help family lawyers analyze case law, interpret legislation, identify relevant precedents, and quickly get up to speed on unfamiliar issues. Tools grounded in authoritative legal sources generally provide greater accuracy and jurisdictional relevance than general-purpose AI systems. Built specifically for legal work, Clio Work combines legal research , analysis, and drafting in a single workspace. It helps lawyers uncover relevant authority, assess how it applies to the facts of a matter, and produce work product they can stand behind. Client communication Family law clients benefit from frequent communication. Because family law matters are highly personal and emotionally sensitive, tone and messaging are crucial, and lawyers must remain thoughtful, empathetic, and appropriate. AI can support the client-lawyer relationship by assisting with drafting routine updates, intake confirmations, and responses to common questions, improving both speed and consistency. To learn how AI-assisted client communication can help you gain a competitive advantage, see Clio’s guide to AI for client communication . Billing and time tracking Family law matters generate significant administrative work, making accurate billing and time capture a persistent challenge. AI-assisted billing can help reduce write-offs, record more billable time, and streamline administrative tasks. Integrated tools like Manage AI create reliable timekeeping and billing workflows. Client intake AI-powered intake forms and screenings can shorten the time between your first contact with a prospective client and the engagement process. This is especially valuable in family law, where firms handle high volumes of inquiries from individuals navigating urgent, emotionally charged situations. Across these use cases, AI helps reduce administrative friction and support more consistent, responsive client service. This allows firms to deliver higher quality legal services and achieve stronger outcomes for their clients. Be the first to see where legal is headed Sign up now to get the Legal Trends Report in your inbox the moment it drops, and you’ll be automatically entered to win a one-hour strategy session. Join the waitlist How to choose the right AI tool for your family law firm The job of evaluating AI tools for family law firms might fall to lawyers, paralegals , or support staff. It requires balancing speed and efficiency with confidentiality, accuracy, and workflow fit. Key criteria to consider include: Practice area coverage and jurisdictional accuracy Look for tools trained on legal data, ideally with family law use cases and jurisdiction-specific awareness. Note that general-purpose AI tools often lack reliable case law grounding and can produce inaccurate outputs. Data security and client confidentiality standards Client data in family law is highly sensitive. Prioritize tools with strong security certifications ( such as SOC 2 Type II ), clear data retention policies, and explicit commitments not to use client data for model training. Integration with existing practice management software AI for family lawyers delivers the most value when it fits into existing workflows rather than operating in isolation. Integration with your practice management system reduces the risk of duplicated work and constant context switching, and keeps client data centralized and organized. Ease of adoption across the team AI tools should be intuitive enough for lawyers and support staff to adopt quickly. Complex interfaces or fragmented workflows can slow adoption and reduce ROI . This matters especially in legal environments, where professionals are often time-constrained and resistant to tools that disrupt established billing and matter management routines. Platform integration vs. standalone tools Standalone AI tools can offer flexibility but often require more manual work. By contrast, AI that’s built into a broader platform provides stronger continuity across intake, matter management, billing, and communication. It’s worth emphasizing that general-purpose AI tools like ChatGPT and Gemini are not designed for legal work. They typically lack case law training, jurisdictional specificity, and the privacy protections required for handling sensitive client information. These limitations are especially important in family law practice. According to Clio’s latest Legal Trends Report for Solo and Small Firms , 57% of solo firms and 55% of small firms have no formal AI policy in place. Without clear guidelines, staff can easily default to public tools and paste sensitive client information directly into them, creating real risks around confidentiality and malpractice. When evaluating purpose-built legal AI platforms, look for SOC 2 Type II compliance, a commitment to never training on client data, and direct integration into your existing practice management workflow. Clio’s AI tools meet all of these criteria and are directly integrated into the broader practice management platform already in use. The result is stronger security, consistency, and overall workflow efficiency. Explore Clio’s family law software to learn how it enables secure and efficient management of family law matters. AI ethics and professional responsibility in family law Ethics and professional responsibility are central to family law practice. First and foremost, attorneys must meet their duty of competence under ABA Model Rule 1.1 , which includes understanding and supervising any AI tools they use. AI systems can support drafting and research, but their outputs should always be reviewed and verified by a lawyer . This is required by ABA Model Rules 5.1 and 5.3 . Another concern is the risk of hallucinations , including inaccurate or entirely fabricated citations and legal propositions. This reinforces the need to check all AI-assisted research against primary sources before relying on it in legal advice or court filings. Legal-specific tools such as Clio Work ￼ help reduce this concern by grounding outputs in verified legal data sources. Confidentiality is also a core ethical obligation in family law, where matters often involve highly sensitive personal information. Attorneys should avoid entering confidential client details into general-purpose AI tools that may not offer sufficient data privacy protections or clear limits on how data is stored or used for model training. Amid the rapid expansion of AI tools, bar associations, including the ABA, along with various state regulators, are actively issuing guidance on AI use . Lawyers have an ongoing obligation to stay current as professional responsibility standards continue to evolve alongside the technology. Will AI replace family lawyers? No. While AI automates parts of legal work, family law practice still relies heavily on legal judgment, negotiation, and client counseling, all of which require human expertise and complex decision-making. What are the best AI tools for family law? Adoption of AI is already widespread, especially across small firms. Clio’s 2026 Legal Trends for Solo and Small Law Firms shows that 71% of solo practitioners and 75% of small firms now use AI, with lawyers reporting higher quality work, less time spent on tedious tasks, faster client response times, and lower stress levels. Those gains are most pronounced when AI is embedded within platform-based systems that connect intake, document drafting, research, and billing in a single workflow. Clio’s integrated AI suite includes multiple functions across practice management: Manage AI for communication, billing and task management; Clio Work for legal research and drafting strategy; and Clio Draft for automating document creation and standardizing frequently used forms and agreements. Some firms supplement their practice management platform with standalone tools for specific tasks like legal research, drafting support, or brainstorming. These tools can add value, but their impact tends to be limited to individual tasks. To truly transform how your practice operates, AI needs to be woven into the workflows you already use, rather than scattered across separate tools. For a broader overview of how AI tools fit into legal workflows, see Clio’s AI tools for lawyers resource page. What is the best AI for family law? There is no single “best” AI for family law firms, but the most effective approach is to combine a legal practice management platform with integrated AI tools designed specifically for legal workflows, rather than relying on standalone general-purpose systems. AI is already changing family law. Here’s your next step. The field of family law is far from static. From “grey divorce” to the rise of self-represented litigants (now reportedly accounting for 72% of family law cases ), family law continues to evolve with the times. AI is further reshaping practice by streamlining intake, improving drafting and research workflows, and reducing the administrative burden that often consumes attorneys’ time. Despite the pace of change, the attorney remains in the driver’s seat, with AI serving as an assistive tool rather than a replacement. Family law depends on judgment, empathy, and trust. These elements cannot be automated and remain integral to the attorney-client relationship. Firms that adopt AI tools early are already delivering a faster, more consistent experience while improving operational performance. Family law will always be a fundamentally human area of practice. Now, with the aid of AI technology, lawyers can redirect their attention toward what matters most: the people they serve. Discover how family law firms use Clio to streamline intake, drafting, billing, and day-to-day practice management. Ready to take the next step? news.titleEn: Litera Relaunches to Unite the Practice and Business of Law on a Single AI Agent
news.titleZh: Litera 重新出发，以单一 AI 智能体统一法律业务与律所运营
news.summaryZh: 2026年7月15日，Litera 在芝加哥宣布公司重新出发并推出统一平台愿景，定位为能够在单一智能体和单一数据集上运行法律业务与律所运营的法律 AI 提供商。此次重新出发建立在 Lito 上市第一年的基础上，为8月的 ILTACON 大会铺路，届时公司将展示其获奖法律 AI 智能体在 Foundation、GrowthTech 及更广泛产品组合中的下一代版本。此次重新出发恰逢 Litera Foundation 365 在全球十大律所中的五家扩大部署。30年来，Litera 每月处理1000万次文档比对，每日用户超过100万，全球客户超过15000家，客户留存率达99%，在 Am Law 100 中渗透率达99%。过去18个月的变化在于，律所现在期望 AI 贯穿每个工作流程，而不仅仅是起草。重新出发突出三大平台差异化领域：一是全所单一智能体，Lito 原生嵌入 Microsoft 365 和 Google Workspace，覆盖起草、比对、合同审查、机构知识和客户开发，无需学习单独工具、单独登录或单独数据集，目前70%的活跃 Litera One 账户使用 Lito；二是高风险工作的确定性准确性，Litera 的红线算法经过30年、每月1000万次比对的打磨，基于规则且具有确定性，不会像概率模型那样猜测或产生幻觉；三是法律业务的基础，Litera Foundation 和 Foundation 365 作为法律业务的机构知识和客户关系管理平台，现已被全球十大律所中的五家使用，原生支持 Microsoft Dynamics 365，并被 Microsoft AI Inner Circle 认可为顶级 Microsoft AI 合作伙伴之一。此次重新出发还推出新品牌活动、更新 litera.com 和 lito.app 网站，并将在2026年8月23日至27日于纳什维尔举行的 ILTACON 上展示统一 Lito 平台愿景。
news.bodyHtml:
After 30 years serving 99% of the Am Law 100, Litera relaunches around one platform, one agent, and one dataset spanning every corner of the firm

CHICAGO – July 15, 2026 – Litera, the Legal AI platform provider that best unifies the practice and business of law, unveiled a company relaunch and unified platform vision, positioning itself as the Legal AI provider best built to run across the practice and business of law on one agent and one dataset. Building on Lito’s first year in market, the relaunch sets the stage for ILTACON in August, where the company will showcase the next version of its award-winning Legal AI agent across Foundation, GrowthTech, and the broader Litera product portfolio. The relaunch also coincides with the expanded deployment of Litera Foundation 365 across five of the 10 largest law firms in the world.

For 30 years, Litera has been the connective tissue of the profession’s most demanding work: 10 million document comparisons a month, over a million daily users across more than 15,000 global customers, 99% logo retention, and 99% penetration of the Am Law 100. What changed over the last 18 months is that firms now expect AI to run through every workflow – not just drafting. The relaunch reflects that shift, and the fact that Litera has already built for it.

“Every AI startup in legal is selling a feature,” said Avaneesh Marwaha, Chief Executive Officer, Litera. “We’re selling the platform those features run on. The practice of law and the business of law have run on separate systems for as long as firms have existed. That ends here: one agent, one dataset, every partner, associate, and business development lead working from the same intelligence.”

Adam Ryan, Chief Product Officer, Litera, added: “AI is table stakes. Trust is the moat. You can’t retrofit years of deterministic accuracy, and you can’t pilot your way into the Am Law 100.” 

The relaunch highlights three areas of platform differentiation:

  • One Agent across the Firm: Lito, embedded natively in Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace, spans drafting, comparison, contract review, institutional knowledge, and client development – no separate tool to learn, no separate login, no separate dataset. Already, 70% of active Litera One accounts use Lito.

  • Deterministic Accuracy on High-Stakes Work: Litera’s redline algorithm, refined over three decades and 10 million comparisons a month, is rules-based and deterministic. It doesn’t guess, and it doesn’t hallucinate the way probabilistic models can. For high-stakes work, firms confirm in every major benchmarking exercise that large language models do not match it.

  • Foundation for the Business of Law: Litera Foundation and Foundation 365, the institutional knowledge and client relationship management (CRM) platform for the business of law, are now used by five of the 10 largest law firms in the world. news.bodyHtml:
Celeste runs the business of the firm — from deal screening and conflicts clearance to business development and lateral hiring — on each firm’s own data, under its own rules

PALO ALTO, Calif. — July 15, 2026 — Intapp (NASDAQ: INTA), the governed AI platform for professional firms in highly regulated industries, today announced at its global launch broadcast that Celeste, previewed in February, is now generally available. Celeste is an expert AI coworker that runs the business of the firm, from deal screening and conflicts clearance to business development and lateral hiring. It’s grounded in each firm’s proprietary knowledge and governed by the firm’s own methods and compliance rules.

Most firms today have AI agents on every desk — drafting, modeling, and reviewing faster than ever. But few firms are growing faster. Firms are finding that AI built for the individual practitioner speeds up the practice, but not the business behind it. That’s the gap Celeste closes.

The work that runs a firm depends on what only the firm knows: its deals, clients, matters, and relationships. It runs on the firm’s own methods — the way it originates a deal, runs a conflict check, or prepares for a pipeline meeting. And it’s bound by obligations that generic AI was never built for, from ethical walls and conflicts rules to client confidentiality. Intapp has spent 20 years building that knowledge, those methods, and that governance into the systems these firms already run on. Celeste starts there.

That’s what makes Celeste different.

  • Celeste gets the firm’s work done. Celeste is an expert AI coworker built for the business workflows of the firm — the work that drives its growth and determines how efficiently it runs. It runs on its own rather than waiting to be asked.
  • Celeste works your way. Celeste encodes the firm’s own methods as playbooks — multi-step workflows that automate the firm’s best practices. It ships with a library of playbooks spanning origination, business development, intake, conflicts, pricing, fundraising, lateral hiring, and beyond, and a no-code builder so teams can easily create their own.
  • Celeste knows your firm. Every firm has access to the same models. What sets a firm apart is what those models don’t know: its deals, clients, relationships, and prior judgment. Celeste is natively integrated into the firm’s systems of record, ingests the firm’s documents, and connects to its preferred data partners through open connectors.
  • Celeste enforces your guardrails. Ethical walls, need-to-know rules, and audits apply to Celeste exactly as they apply to people. Restricted information stays restricted no matter what anyone asks, and the firm can show clients and regulators a full record of every action.

Celeste is already at work in early-adopter firms, including Hg and BakerHostetler. In private capital, Celeste turns a confidential information memorandum into a structured investment screen, drawing on the firm’s own investment criteria, mandate, and deal history. In investment banking, it maps board and management relationships to give bankers the strongest path into a mandate. In legal, it surfaces relevant matters, partner experience, and prior pitch materials for an urgent client request in minutes rather than hours. It also runs an end-to-end lateral hire lifecycle, from candidate research and conflicts pre-screening to clearance preparation and onboarding. For accounting and consulting firms, the same governed coworker works within independence and conflicts obligations from day one.

Intapp calls this Firm AI, the category of AI aimed not at the individual or the work product, but at the business of the firm itself. Horizontal assistants speed up everyday tasks. Practice AI helps produce the work product. Firm AI runs the business behind both.

Availability

Intapp Celeste is generally available now. Firms can explore the use case library, request a demonstration, or contact their Intapp account team at intapp.com.

Supporting quotes

Thad Jampol, Co-Founder and Chief Product Officer, Intapp

“Firms will run several kinds of AI: horizontal assistants for everyday work, practice AI for the work product, and Firm AI for the business of the firm itself. That last category is the hard one, and it’s the one almost nobody is building. That’s Celeste — an expert AI coworker built on a firm’s own playbooks, knowledge, and guardrails. When a conflicts team can clear 10 times the matters and a fund can screen 10 times the deals, that’s not saved time — that’s a new business model.”

Katherine Lowry, Chief Information Officer and Head of IncuBaker, BakerHostetler

“Our immediate focus is on conflicts and intake, because that’s where Celeste will have the biggest impact on our operations. Clearing conflicts faster to win engagements — and going through clearance at a much faster rate when bringing in laterals with thousands of matters — will make a real difference for our teams. What drew us to Intapp was the shared alignment on process and on governance.”

Shirin Veeran, Data, Tech & AI Strategy, Hg

“The intelligence is ours, not something generic applied to our firm. Celeste screens against our actual mandate, drawing on knowledge we have built across the firm over two decades. Having a clear, always-current view of deal progress and pipeline speed — without the usual reporting lift — is genuinely valuable to any deal team.”

Additional resources

  • Explore Intapp Celeste
  • Watch the full launch broadcast on demand at intapp.com/celeste-launch/

Connect with Intapp

  • Learn more at Intapp
  • Get more news in the Intapp newsroom
  • Follow Intapp on LinkedIn

About Intapp

Intapp (NASDAQ: INTA) is the governed AI platform for professional firms in highly regulated industries. Intapp’s vertically tailored agentic solutions are built for the specialized workflows, complex relationship networks, and professional compliance requirements of accounting, consulting, investment banking, law, private capital, and real assets firms. By applying Firm AI to core processes and data, Intapp helps partners, dealmakers, and advisors drive firm growth, manage compliance, and improve profitability. Learn why the world’s top firms trust Intapp’s industry-specific enterprise solutions at intapp.com.

Contact
Emily Martinez
Global Media and Communications Director
press@intapp.com

news.bodyHtml:
Walk into any law firm, private equity firm, investment bank, or accounting firm today and nearly every desk is using AI. Your professionals draft, build models, and review documents faster than they did a year ago. That was the right first move, and the gains are real.

But here’s the question we keep hearing from firm leaders: Our people are more productive, so why isn’t the firm growing faster?

The answer: Because AI built for the practice accelerates individuals. Meanwhile, the work that runs the firm itself — origination, screening, intake, conflicts, lateral hiring — still happens the way it always has: by hand, under deadline, by your most experienced people. And because their hours are finite, the firm rations that work — resulting in deals never screened, laterals never vetted, pitches never made.

This is what Firm AI changes — and it changes more than speed. A conflicts team that clears 20 matters a month can clear 200. A fund that screens 300 deals a year can screen 3,000, and can pursue entire categories of opportunity it used to filter out for practical reasons.

More than saved time, this is a new operating model for the firm. It’s why we built Intapp Celeste, now generally available.

Meet Celeste

Celeste is an expert AI coworker for the business of your firm. Give Celeste a goal, and it plans the steps, executes them across your firm’s systems, and brings finished work back for a professional’s judgment. It doesn’t wait to be asked — it just runs your pipeline brief every Monday morning, or starts a conflicts check the moment a new engagement lands.

Plenty of tools can answer a question about your work. Four things make Celeste a strategic coworker instead.

Celeste knows your firm

Every firm now has access to the same AI models, trained on the same public internet. What sets your firm apart is exactly what those models don’t know: your clients, your deals, your relationships, and the judgment behind every decision your firm has made. An AI without that context gives every firm the same answer.

Celeste is grounded in all of it. Natively integrated with your systems of record, Celeste inherits everything you’ve spent years configuring: your operating model, your terminology, your fields and data structures, your permissions. Celeste knows what “pipeline” and “coverage” mean at your private equity firm, and what “matter” and “key client” mean at your law firm, the way you define them.

  • Context engine. A firm profile, connector onboarding, and domain model teach Celeste your data, your terms, and your relationships, so it reasons in your firm’s language.
  • Native Intapp integration. Celeste connects across Intapp DealCloud, your compliance systems, and Intapp Time to draw on deal and matter history, relationships, and client activity.
  • Memory. Celeste remembers your patterns, decisions, and preferences, and grounds its answers in the documents you choose.

Celeste gets the work done

An assistant answers your questions and waits for the next one — but those answers aren’t finished deliverables. And besides, the work that runs a firm doesn’t arrive in the form of questions; it arrives as jobs — CIMs to screen, matters to open, Monday meetings to prep for.

But Celeste delivers finished products: IC summaries drafted, records updated, briefs sent to your inbox — with your sign-off required at the points that carry risk. And because Celeste works before you ask, and at whatever volume the work demands, it takes on jobs no firm could staff before: screening every inbound deal against your mandate, or monitoring every lateral hire from sourcing through integration.

  • Proactive agents. Celeste works in the background on schedules and events, then surfaces a curated agenda of finished work that’s ready for review.
  • Document intelligence. Celeste produces Word, PowerPoint, and Excel files in your firm’s templates and branding, and edits existing documents with tracked changes.
  • Read-and-write actions. Celeste automates follow-ups, task sequencing, and record updates across Intapp and connected systems, keeping your teams focused on client work.

Celeste works your firm’s way

Getting the work done is half the job. Doing it your way is the other half: the criteria you screen against, the order you run a conflicts check in, the way a pitch reads when it comes from your firm. Those methods are what separate you from the firm across the street — and until now they lived only in the heads of the people who use them.

Celeste encodes your methods as playbooks: multi-step agentic workflows that carry out your firm’s procedures from the first step to the finished output, so the work comes back the way your firm would have done it. Celeste ships with a library of playbooks curated by Intapp industry experts and shaped by our work with more than 1,000 firms — ready to run out of the box or tailor to how your firm operates.

  • Playbook library. Access pre-built playbooks across deal origination, compliance, lateral hiring, business development, and more.
  • No-code builder. Create your own playbooks, agents, and skills in plain language, then run them right from chat.
  • Automations. Set playbooks to run on your schedule or start automatically when something changes in your systems, and get notifications in the app or by email.

Celeste enforces your guardrails

Professional firms operate under obligations most industries don’t: ethical walls, client confidentiality, independence requirements, MNPI. Any AI that touches your firm’s data must honor every one of them the way your people do — or else your general counsel will stop the rollout, and rightly so. Celeste has those guardrails architected into its core, and applies your ethical walls and access policies through a trust and control layer that governs Celeste by the same rules as your people — so restricted information stays that way, no matter what anyone asks.

  • Guardrails. Permissions, ethical walls, and access controls run through one policy layer for trust and controls across human and AI identities, and Celeste acts only on what it’s permitted to use.
  • Human-in-the-loop review. Sensitive tasks require review, approval, or refinement of Celeste’s actions before it executes.

Celeste connects across your ecosystem

Celeste also works where your work already lives. At launch, it connects natively to Intapp DealCloud, your compliance systems, Intapp Time, Microsoft 365, Snowflake, and the open web, with Model Context Protocol (MCP) partners including Moody’s, FactSet, PitchBook, and MSCI. It also meets your teams inside the AI tools they already use, working in Microsoft Copilot, Claude, and other tools through MCP, A2A, and API. No rip and replace.

news.titleEn: Litera Relaunches Its Brand Around a Unified Vision: One AI Agent Spanning the Practice and Business of Law
news.titleZh: Litera以统一愿景重塑品牌：一个AI代理贯穿法律业务与实践
news.summaryZh: Litera今日宣布公司级品牌重塑，将自身定位为通过一个AI代理和一个数据集统一法律实践与业务的法律AI平台。此次重塑包括新品牌标识、标语“Raise The Bar”、广告活动及重新设计的网站，并计划在2026年纳什维尔的ILTACON上展示其法律AI代理Lito的下一代版本。CEO Avaneesh Marwaha称这是品牌重塑而非产品发布，是对过去18个月Lito工作的声明。Litera拥有超过15,000客户、每日超100万用户，每月执行1000万次文档比较，服务99%的Am Law 100律所。Foundation 365已部署于全球十大律所中的五家，70%的活跃Litera One账户使用Lito。新定位强调信任，对比确定性规则引擎与大型语言模型的概率性输出，广告宣称“因为‘大概’不够好”。Marwaha表示概率性AI可用于某些工作流，但实际客户工作产品必须接近100%准确。Lito可调用规则引擎，并查询律所精选的Foundation数据。Litera一直在简化产品目录，将起草产品整合为战略捆绑，并对Kira和Transact等工作流工具采取类似做法，未来战略聚焦实践、管理和增长三大支柱。Marwaha重申为起草和Kira客户保留Lito，并否认品牌重塑预示Hg将出售或IPO公司，称无新资本注入。
news.bodyHtml:
Litera, one of the most broadly deployed technology companies in the legal industry, is today unveiling a company-wide relaunch that positions it as the legal AI platform unifying the practice and business of law through one AI agent and one dataset.

The relaunch — going live today at litera.com — includes a new brand identity, the tagline “Raise The Bar,” an advertising campaign and a redesigned website.

It also sets the stage for ILTACON 2026 in Nashville next month, where Litera plans to showcase the next version of Lito, its legal AI agent, across Foundation, its GrowthTech stack, and the company’s broader product portfolio.

To be clear, today’s announcement is a rebranding, not a product launch. In an interview Monday, Avaneesh Marwaha, Litera’s chief executive officer, described it as “a branding relaunch and a statement of all the work we’ve done in Lito” during the past 18 months.

“Some organizations lead with brand and marketing splash first and then build their technology behind it,” Marwaha said. “Litera always has to deliver. We don’t get the luxury of being 80% good. So we’ve been building and delivering for the last 18 months … and I felt the brand is ready to match where we are as a business.”

One Agent, One Dataset

At the core of the new positioning is Litera’s claim that it is uniquely situated at the intersection of the practice of law — drafting, document comparison and contract review — and the business of law, including the institutional knowledge and client relationship data housed in its Foundation platform.

Litera’s new logo.

“Every AI startup in legal is selling a feature,” Marwaha said in the announcement. “We’re selling the platform those features run on. The practice of law and the business of law have run on separate systems for as long as firms have existed. That ends here: one agent, one dataset, every partner, associate, and business development lead working from the same intelligence.”

Related: On LawNext: Litera’s Avaneesh Marwaha: The CEO Who Left Before AI and Returned to Lead Through It.

Few legal technology companies can match Litera’s reach. The company says it has more than 15,000 customers and more than 1 million daily users, performs 10 million document comparisons a month, and serves 99% of the Am Law 100.

Litera also says Foundation 365 — its institutional knowledge and CRM platform built natively on Microsoft Dynamics 365 — is now deployed at five of the 10 largest law firms in the world, while 70% of active Litera One accounts use Lito.

In our interview, Marwaha described the end-to-end workflow the company is building toward: A partner could move from identifying a potential new matter, to pursuing and winning it through an RFP, to doing the work, and then to feeding the resulting experience data back into Foundation for reuse — all powered by Lito.

That workflow is now in an early-adopter program, Marwaha said, and customers will begin seeing it in the market “in the coming month or so.”

Deterministic vs. Probabilistic

A new ad takes a poke at probabilistic AI.

A central theme of the new messaging — running through the press release, advertising campaign and video spots — is trust, particularly the contrast between Litera’s deterministic, rules-based engines and the probabilistic outputs of large language models. One new ad declares, “Because probably isn’t good enough.”

“AI is table stakes. Trust is the moat,” Adam Ryan, Litera’s chief product officer, said in the announcement. “You can’t retrofit years of deterministic accuracy, and you can’t pilot your way into the Am Law 100.”

Of course, Lito itself is an LLM-based, probabilistic tool, so I asked Marwaha how he reconciles those approaches within a single platform. His answer was that they occupy different zones of risk.

He is comfortable using probabilistic AI for certain workflows and automations, but actual client work product — including document creation, proofreading, comparison and metadata cleaning — “has to be as close to 100% accurate all the time.”

He pointed to the risk illustrated by court sanctions against lawyers who fail to verify AI-generated work. A contract “latent with a 10% error rate,” he said, may not create an obvious problem at closing. But if a dispute later arises, “that’s a material issue and ripe for malpractice and risk.”

Lito, he said, can call on Litera’s rules-based engines when running automations. On the business-of-law side, it can query a firm’s curated Foundation data rather than the public domain, which he argued narrows the window for error.

Although Lito offers full model selection, Marwaha said, “we still think it needs to be bound and protected by some rules and algorithms that have been around for a while.”

A Response to Harvey?

Given the timing, it is hard not to view the relaunch against the backdrop of heavily funded AI-native startups — Harvey and Legora chief among them — that have dominated legal AI headlines. When I asked whether the rebranding and repositioning were a response to those companies, Marwaha equivocated.

“I’ve never felt I needed to respond to anybody,” he said. “But I do think this is our positioning statement.”

Litera, he said, has a “better with” story alongside Microsoft Copilot and Anthropic’s Claude — and even, he suggested, alongside the startups themselves. But he argued that workflows inside Litera’s ecosystem are “just as good, if not better,” because of the deterministic engines beneath them.

Another of Litera’s new ads.

He was also direct about where he believes the market is heading. Use cases for which firms have paid vendors $3 million to $4 million, he predicted, “are going to be out of the box from the frontier models at some point,” meaning those vendors will need to offer other advantages.

Litera, he argues, already has such advantages: its rules-based engines and its presence in the applications and systems where lawyers already work.

Notably, one selling point frequently cited by AI-native startups — integration with a law firm’s technology stack — is something Marwaha regards as table stakes for vendors that have served the market for decades.

What Else Is Changing

Separate from the rebrand, but unfolding at the same time, Litera has been simplifying its sprawling product catalog. Marwaha said the company began consolidating its drafting products into strategic bundles in spring 2025 and is now taking a similar approach to workflow tools such as Kira and Transact. It is centering its go-forward strategy on three pillars: practice, manage and grow.

As a result, he said, the redesigned website should present a cleaner and simpler view of the company’s products.

On pricing, Marwaha reaffirmed his commitment to keep Lito included for drafting and Kira customers. He said he sees no near-term change to that approach, particularly as model costs continue to fall.

Over time, he added, new workflows developed with customers could be offered as optional, separately priced skills. But those would be handled case by case, and, he said, “it’s too early to call the commercial aspects of Lito.”

I also asked whether the rebrand signals that Hg, the private equity firm that has backed Litera since 2019, is positioning the company for a sale or an IPO. Marwaha said no and noted that Litera received no new capital for the relaunch.

“We self-fund everything here,” he said. “We’re not VC-backed. We don’t have just endless bank accounts to go after.”

Asked about Litera’s relationship with Microsoft as Microsoft pushes Copilot deeper into the legal market, Marwaha said it is “tighter today than it was 10 years ago.”

He said Litera will spend considerable time over the coming quarters talking about both Copilot and Anthropic. “That is something where I’m placing my chips where I think the future of work is.”

My Take

Having followed Litera for many years, what strikes me about this relaunch is what it is not. It is neither a radical reinvention nor a pivot. Rather, it modernizes the company’s visual identity and, more importantly, sharpens its value proposition — or at least how it articulates that value proposition.

During Marwaha’s first stint as CEO, from 2016 to 2022, he oversaw a sweeping transformation of the company. Through some 14 acquisitions, Litera expanded from an exclusive focus on document productivity tools into a much broader portfolio spanning transaction management, due diligence, litigation and firm intelligence.

Since his return as CEO in October 2024, the company has continued making acquisitions while aggressively extending its Lito agentic AI across the portfolio.

While that acquisition spree transformed and expanded the company, it also left some observers wondering whether Litera had become fragmented. Just navigating its product list could be downright daunting.

This relaunch pulls those pieces into a single, unified message. The company that is already embedded in the daily workflows of nearly every large law firm says it is also best positioned to provide the AI layer running through those workflows.

The company is also smart to emphasize trust — the contrast between Litera’s deterministic, rules-based engines and the probabilistic outputs of large language models. It is easy to forget that, in much of the mechanical work of law, there is one correct result.

Marwaha may say he feels no need to respond to the Harveys and Legoras of the world. But his underlying argument — that incumbency in firms’ technology stacks and decades of deterministic accuracy are assets no startup can replicate overnight — seems squarely aimed at a market enamored of shiny new things.

How will the rebrand land with customers? Litera plans to make it a major focus at ILTACON next month, providing the first real test.

news.titleEn: Legatics’ New MCP Server Connects Your AI Tools
news.titleZh: Legatics推出新MCP服务器，连接您的AI工具
news.summaryZh: 知名交易管理平台Legatics已推出模型上下文协议（MCP）服务器，允许AI助手或代理直接连接实时的Legatics交易数据，从而构建统一的交易系统。此举紧随该公司上周推出平台内VDR-lite功能之后。通过这一举措，“Legatics成为面向人类和AI的交易基础设施层”，即法律AI工具、Legatics平台与交易数据共处同一生态系统。多数AI工具无法告知特定交易的实际进展，只能回答一般法律问题或审阅文档，无法说明未完成事项、签署状态或下一步行动，原因在于缺乏上下文。MCP服务器正是以安全、实时的方式将上下文传递给AI，这是人与代理在交易上协作的环节，也是构建交易基础设施的关键解锁点。初期将提供“读取权限”，但公司希望未来能提供“写入”能力。MacAdam称这是第一步，不是最后一步；读取权限让AI准确了解交易情况，写入权限将让其推动交易前进。交易是工作单元，AI应在此层面运作。此举具有战略意义，使Legatics在专注交易管理的同时，与快速发展的法律AI领域保持连接。
news.bodyText: Legatics, the well-known transaction management platform, has launched a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. This will allow your ‘AI assistants or agents to connect directly to live Legatics deal data’, creating a unified system for transactions. The move follows last week’s launch of the company’s own VDR-lite capability, which sits within the platform. They added that by doing this ‘Legatics becomes a transaction infrastructure layer for humans and AI’. I.e. you have your legal AI tools, you have Legatics, you have your deals – all together in one ecosystem. Rob MacAdam, Chief Product & Strategy Officer at Legatics, commented: ‘Most AI tools cannot tell you what is actually happening on a specific deal. They can answer general legal questions. They can review a document you put in front of them. They cannot tell you what is outstanding on your matter, what the signing status is or what the next step should be. That is because they do not have the context. ‘The MCP server is how that context gets to AI, securely and in real time. This is where people and agents work together on transactions, and it is the key unlock for the transaction infrastructure we are building.’ And here’s an overview of the key elements: They noted that while it will start with ‘read access’, they want to offer the ability ‘to write’, or as MacAdam put it: ‘This is the first step, not the last. Read access gives AI an accurate picture of the deal. Write access will let it move the deal forward. The transaction is the unit of work, and that is the level AI should operate at.’ An interesting move and strategically smart, as it allows Legatics to keep its focus on deal management while staying connected to the wider and fast-developing legal AI field. news.titleEn: Meet Amazon Quick For Legal
news.titleZh: 认识亚马逊 Quick For Legal
news.summaryZh: 文章称亚马逊拥有“Amazon Quick For Legal”能力，定位为“用于法律研究、合同和合规的AI助手”，但并非专为律师打造的专用法律AI产品。它主要提供结构化界面和聊天框，帮助律师完成合同起草、法律研究等需求，输出并非来自Quick for Legal本身，而是来自其调用的多种大语言模型，并运行在亚马逊Bedrock平台之上。文章认为Quick在很大程度上只是一个花哨的界面。该“For Legal”功能是作为更广泛的Quick产品的一部分逐步演化而来，Quick于2025年上市，面向多领域所有用户，并脱胎于面向商业用户的Amazon Q助手，演进过程高度迭代，因此新闻性被稀释。文章推测其未被广泛使用的原因在于，它提供的功能在当下并无太多独到之处，且没有自有数据。目前尚无迹象表明亚马逊打算大举进入法律垂直领域，但若其他公司纷纷行动、且Quick for Legal被超越，亚马逊或许会考虑聘请经验丰富的律师来构建新能力。文章提到，OpenAI（通过Codex系列仍在开发中）、Anthropic（Claude for Legal）、微软（通过前Robin AI团队的Legal Agent）、Palantir（与Kirkland & Ellis合作）以及Perplexity（Computer for Counsel）均已推出专门的法律产品，并获悉至少还有一家大型科技企业即将以非常明确的方式进入法律领域，预计2026年至2027年将有更多企业加入。
news.bodyText: Just when you wondered who else among the tech giants would cover legal, it turns out that the ‘Everything Store’ has an ‘Amazon Quick For Legal’ capability. But…it seems like it’s been here – under the radar – for some time already. First, what does it do? It says that it is ‘Your AI assistant for legal research, contracts, and compliance’. But is this a dedicated legal AI product for lawyers? Not exactly, even if there is clearly some additional tooling – albeit minimal – in place for attorneys. What it primarily provides is a structured interface and chatbox that is designed to help lawyers get answers on a range of needs, from drafting contracts to doing legal research. However, those outputs are not from Quick for Legal specifically, they are from a wide range of LLMs that it taps, and it sits on top of Amazon’s Bedrock platform. So, is Quick mainly just a fancy UI? In many ways, yes. That’s correct. See examples below. Why isn’t this big news even if it is mostly a UI? That’s a good question. This site had not seen it before, but stumbled upon it by chance a few days ago. After some research it looks like the ‘For Legal’ bit has slowly evolved as part of the wider Quick product, which came to market in 2025 and is for everyone across multiple areas, and that in turn evolved out of the Amazon Q assistant for business users. In short, it’s been a very iterative process and so the news aspect has been diluted. Another question is then: why isn’t everyone using it? Well, AL’s guess is that it just doesn’t provide much that you can’t get elsewhere these days, and it doesn’t have its own data either. And finally, will they build something better? Will they bring in dedicated legal experts – like Anthropic and OpenAI are doing – and create detailed ‘skills’ that can really add value above and beyond the UI and some relatively simple legal tooling? The answer there is: there seems to be no indication yet that Amazon wants to go into the legal vertical in a major way. But, as others do, and as they see their Quick for Legal is now largely superseded, maybe they will? As noted, that would mean really hiring experienced lawyers to build out new capabilities, but that is not impossible, as we have seen other ‘Big Tech’ players do this already. We shall see. AL has been told more ‘Big Tech’ players will soon be entering the legal tech vertical and today we have dedicated legal offerings from: OpenAI (still in development via its Codex line), Anthropic (Claude for Legal), Microsoft (Legal Agent, via the former Robin AI team), Palantir (working with Kirkland & Ellis), and Perplexity (Computer for Counsel). And AL knows of at least one more large tech business that is about to enter the legal domain in a very intentional way, very soon. So, we should not bet against it, nor many others joining in across 2026 and into 2027. More about Amazon Quick for Legal here. —

news.titleEn: How Deep is Your Fake? A 3-Minute-Guide on Labelling Obligations under the EU AI Act
news.titleZh: 你的伪造有多深？欧盟《人工智能法案》标签义务三分钟指南
news.summaryZh:
欧盟《人工智能法案》要求企业在特定情况下披露内容是否由人工智能创建或修改，该义务同样适用于使用图像生成程序等人工智能工具进行产品广告的企业。新规自2026年8月2日起可强制执行，罚款最高可达1500万欧元或全球年营业额的3%，合规重要性凸显。对于人工智能系统部署者而言，除聊天机器人披露外，标签义务仅适用于两种情形：一是旨在向公众通报公共利益事项的人工智能生成或操纵文本；二是深度伪造。

欧盟委员会指南草案将上市公司网站上包含投资者信息的人工智能操纵企业报告列为向公众通报公共利益事项的文本示例。该草案假定标签义务不适用于经过人工审查或编辑控制且由法律或自然人承担编辑责任的人工智能生成或操纵文本。对于在网站、目录、广告牌、电视和社交媒体等渠道推广或销售产品的企业，更具挑战的是披露构成深度伪造的人工智能生成或操纵图像、音频或视频内容的义务。《人工智能法案》第3(60)条将“深度伪造”定义为“类似于现有人员、物体、地点、实体或事件，且会让人错误地显得真实或可信的人工智能生成或操纵图像、音频或视频内容”。尽管将深度伪造定义扩展至人员之外有充分理由，但纳入。
news.bodyText: Find Your Next Job ! The EU Artificial Intelligence (AI) Act requires companies to disclose in certain cases whether content has been created or modified by AI. This also applies to companies that make use of AI such as image-generation programs for product advertising. Given that the new rules are enforceable from 2 August 2026, with fines up to EUR 15 million or 3% of global annual turnover, the importance of compliance with these rules is now in sharp focus. The good news is that for deployers of AI systems, besides chatbot disclosure, labelling obligations only apply in two scenarios: (i) AI-generated or manipulated texts aiming at informing the public on matters of public interest, and (ii) deep fakes[1]. Looking at all of this in more detail, what does this mean to companies that create and/or publish advertising and promotional content? As one example of AI generated or manipulated texts which inform the public on matters of public interest, the EU Commission’s Draft Guidelines (the latest version being a 2024 draft for stakeholder consultation)[2] list AI-manipulated corporate reports published on a listed company’s website which contain investor information. By contrast, the EU Commission’s Draft Guidelines assume that the labelling obligation will not apply to: A general exemption applies to AI generated or manipulated text that has undergone human review or editorial control and for which a legal or natural person holds editorial responsibility[3]. What seems more challenging for companies promoting or selling products on their websites, in catalogues, on billboards, on TV and social media or other means of advertising, is the obligation to disclose AI generated or manipulated image, audio or video content constituting a deep fake. The term “deep fake” is defined in Article 3(60) of the AI Act as “AI-generated or manipulated image, audio or video content that resembles existing persons, objects, places, entities or events and would falsely appear to a person to be authentic or truthful”. news.titleEn: Superjustice or Algorithm Tyranny? How AI is Rewriting the Rule of Law with Professor Benjamin Alarie
news.titleZh: 超级正义还是算法暴政？Benjamin Alarie教授谈AI如何改写法治
news.summaryZh: 人工智能对法律体系根基的深刻影响。多年来公众关注AI基准测试、工作场所自动化和聊天机器人幻觉，但AI已悄然侵入民主社会的基础——法律系统。如今，AI不再局限于总结判例法，而是进入司法推理、结果预测和机构治理领域。这引发了核心争议：算法暴政的开始，还是解决法律系统难以触及、积压严重且深度不平等问题的终极良方？文章将AI革命与梵蒂冈具有里程碑意义的教皇通谕《Magnifica Humanitas》进行类比，描绘AI革命的下一阶段。我们正超越模型能力，进入机构适应阶段。文章呼吁重新思考问责制、公平性以及代码时代正义的定义。内容涉及AI在司法推理、预测性结果和制度治理中的应用，以及其对法治的潜在影响。
news.bodyText:
We’ve spent years obsessing over AI benchmarks, workplace automation, and chatbot hallucinations. But while we were looking at the future of work, artificial intelligence quietly invaded the foundations of democratic society: the legal system. Today, we’re unpacking a tectonic shift with the Professor. AI isn’t just summarizing case law anymore; it’s entering the realm of judicial reasoning, predictive outcomes, and institutional governance. Is this the beginning of algorithmic tyranny, or could it be the ultimate cure for an inaccessible, backlogged, and deeply unequal legal system? Drawing striking parallels to the Vatican’s landmark papal encyclical Magnifica Humanitas , we will map out the next phase of the AI revolution. We’re moving past model capabilities and stepping into institutional adaptation. Get ready to rethink everything you know about accountability, equity, and the very definition of justice in the age of code.

news.titleEn: Briefpoint Launches Discovery Playbooks, Bringing Response Governance to the 1,000+ Law Firms That Draft Discovery on Its Platform
news.titleZh: Briefpoint推出Discovery Playbooks，为在其平台上起草证据开示的1000多家律所带来回应治理
news.summaryZh:
2026年7月13日，Briefpoint宣布推出Discovery Playbooks。该证据开示回应治理功能集可捕获律所最佳异议与回应策略，并在需要时自动重新应用。Briefpoint是证据开示自动化平台，用户覆盖全美50个州逾1000家律所。诉讼律师反复回答相同证据开示请求，但每套新回应通常从零开始，起草者翻查旧工作成果、复制粘贴或临时发挥，偏离律所立场。Discovery Playbooks消除这一流程：律师照常在Briefpoint中回应，完成后一键加入律所playbook，无需数据录入或配置；此后Briefpoint检测到已答复过的请求时，会自动关联并重新应用律所异议与回应策略。

playbook条目可按全所或特定客户、司法辖区、案件类型限定范围。辩护律所在高量案件中统一异议策略；原告律所一次回应承运人模板文书后重复使用；内部法务部门一次编码公司立场并在各事项和外部律所执行；成长型律所用于新人入职。每条条目记录来源，包括添加者、最后使用时间及使用次数，库可按文件类型、客户、案件类型和司法辖区搜索筛选。该功能包含在所有Briefpoint套餐中，不另收费，现已上线。Briefpoint由前诉讼律师Nathan Walter和前Relativity首席工程师Chris Maffin创立，已自动化逾186000份证据开示文件，为50个州和98个联邦法院的1000多家律所生成逾685000条异议，并通过SOC 2 Type II认证，符合ZDR和HIPAA。
news.bodyHtml:
New featureset learns a firm’s objection and response strategy from work it has already served — then reapplies it automatically whenever a matching request appears, on any matter

 

San Francisco, California | July 13, 2026 Briefpoint, the discovery automation platform used by more than 1,000 law firms across all 50 states, today announced Discovery Playbooks, a discovery response governance feature set that captures a firm’s best objections and response strategy and brings them back automatically – where litigators need them, when they need them.

 Litigators answer the same discovery requests over and over: the same form interrogatories in every auto case, the same document demands from the same opposing counsel, the same objections a firm has served hundreds of times. Yet each new response set typically starts from scratch, with drafters digging through old work product and copy-pasting from prior matters – or improvising and drifting from the firm’s positions.

 

Discovery Playbooks eliminates that entire workflow. Attorneys respond to discovery in Briefpoint exactly as they always have. When a response is completed, a single click adds it to the firm’s playbook – no data entry or configuration required. From then on, whenever Briefpoint detects a request the firm has already answered, it links the request to the saved playbook item and reapplies the firm’s objections and response strategy automatically.

“Your best discovery response shouldn’t be trapped in a file from 2023,” said Nathan Walter, CEO and co-founder of Briefpoint. “Every firm already has winning objection language – the problem is that it lives in old documents and senior lawyers’ heads. Playbooks turns that tribal knowledge into firm policy. You do the work once, and Briefpoint makes sure it shows up every time it’s relevant, for every litigator, on every matter.”

 

One featureset, three use cases. Because playbook entries can be scoped firm-wide or to a specific client, jurisdiction, or case type, firms across the bar use Playbooks differently:

Defense firms enforce consistent objection strategy across high-volume dockets, so positions don’t vary with whoever happens to be drafting – and contradictions between matters get caught in drafting instead of surfacing in deposition.

 Plaintiff firms answer carrier boilerplate once and reuse it everywhere, reclaiming unbillable hours spent re-drafting responses to the same template discovery in every case.

 In-house legal departments encode corporate positions once and see them enforced across every matter and every outside firm to combat impeachable response variance or, at worst, bad law.

 Growing firms use playbooks to onboard: new associates draft from the firm’s tested language on day one, and partner review becomes reviewing rather than rewriting.

 

Every playbook entry carries its provenance (who added it, when it was last used, and how many times) so when a position changes, firms know exactly what the prior language said and where it has been asserted. The playbook library is searchable and filterable by document type, client, case type, and jurisdiction.

 “Preparing discovery responses takes much less time and we are able to ensure consistency throughout the firm with respect to objections and updates in the law,” said Eileen Booth, Partner at Jacobsen & McElroy, a Briefpoint customer.

 Discovery Playbooks is included in every Briefpoint plan at no additional cost and is live now for all Briefpoint accounts. A 60-second demonstration video is available at briefpoint.ai/discovery-playbooks.

 

About Briefpoint

Briefpoint is a discovery automation platform founded by Nathan Walter, a former litigator, and Chris Maffin, a former lead engineer at Relativity. Built so cases can resolve on their merits instead of their litigation budgets, Briefpoint has automated more than 186,000 discovery documents and generated more than 685,000 objections for over 1,000 law firms in all 50 states and 98 federal courts. Briefpoint is SOC 2 Type II certified, ZDR, and HIPAA compliant. Learn more at briefpoint.ai.

 

Media Contact

Nathan Walter

CEO, Briefpoint

nwalter@briefpoint.ai

news.titleEn: The Inside View: Addleshaw Goddard’s AGPT learnings and the future of build vs buy
news.titleZh: 内部视角：Addleshaw Goddard的AGPT经验与自建与采购的未来
news.summaryZh:
在Legal IT Insider的《内部视角》最新一期节目中，Addleshaw Goddard的创新与法律技术总监Elliot White与编辑Caroline Hill坦诚讨论了该律所自建GenAI平台AGPT的经验教训，以及AI下一阶段可能促使律所重新思考某些假设的原因。AGPT托管于其Microsoft Azure租户中，White从该国际律所GenAI试点和AGPT构建之初便参与其中。White解释，AGPT主要目的从来不是创建专有工具，而是快速学习、理解技术，并帮助律师培养有效使用AI所需的技能。结果是采用率高，且对律师在实践中如何使用生成式AI有了更深入的理解。

White对市场走向的诚实评估使本期播客尤为及时。尽管Addleshaw Goddard继续投资AGPT，但代理工作流的出现带来了新挑战。White讨论了跟上快速演变的AI能力的难度，并提出了律所应在多大程度上专注于构建自身解决方案的重要问题。讨论还深入探讨了基于代币的定价等话题。随着供应商日益转向消费模式，White认为律所将需要更加成熟地针对正确任务使用正确模型，并理解AI赋能工作的真实成本。另一个有趣的讨论围绕知识可移植性。律所应仔细考虑在何处以及如何编纂知识，以便随着技术平台演变保持可移植性。对于律所领导者、创新团队以及任何试图驾驭快速变化的法律AI格局的人，本期节目提供了实践经验与战略思维的绝佳结合。
news.bodyHtml:
In the latest episode of The Inside View with Legal IT Insider, Elliot White from Addleshaw Goddard joins editor Caroline Hill for a candid discussion about what the firm has learned from building its own GenAI platform AGPT, and why the next phase of AI may see law firms rethink some of their assumptions.

White is director of innovation and legal technology at Addleshaw Goddard and has been involved from the outset in the international law firm’s GenAI pilots and the build of AGPT, which is hosted in its Microsoft Azure tenancy.

Advertisement

There are lots of conversations right now about buy v build within law firms, but few have got as much experience already as Addleshaw Goddard. White explains that AGPT was never primarily about creating a proprietary tool; it was about learning quickly, understanding the technology, and helping lawyers develop the skills needed to work effectively with AI. He says the result has been strong adoption and a much deeper understanding of how lawyers actually use generative AI in practice.

What makes this podcast particularly timely is White’s honest assessment of where the market is heading. While Addleshaw Goddard continues to invest in AGPT, the emergence of agentic workflows is creating new challenges. White discusses the difficulty of keeping pace with rapidly evolving AI capabilities and raises important questions about the extent to which law firms should be focusing on building their own solutions.

Advertisement

The discussion also provides a thoughtful exploration on topics including token-based pricing. As suppliers increasingly move towards consumption models, White argues that law firms will need to become significantly more sophisticated about using the right model for the right task and understanding the true cost of AI-enabled work.

Another interesting discussion is around knowledge portability. White argues that firms should think carefully about where and how they codify their knowledge, so it remains portable as technology platforms evolve.

For law firm leaders, innovation teams and anyone trying to navigate the fast-changing legal AI landscape, this episode offers a great combination of practical experience and strategic thinking. Definitely one to watch.

You can watch the episode on YouTube below or listen on Spotify HERE.

news.summaryZh: Intapp（纳斯达克代码：INTA）宣布扩大与穆迪的战略合作，将穆迪数据与Intapp Celeste——专为专业服务机构打造的代理式AI平台——进行新集成。法律、私募资本和会计领域的客户将从中受益。通过自然对话，Celeste可在专业人员日常使用的工作流程中直接呈现穆迪的金融风险情报、实体筛查结果、所有权结构和公司情报，无需切换上下文。从数据访问转向嵌入式智能，Intapp与穆迪帮助客户释放更大价值：交易专业人员可在Intapp DealCloud中直接获取穆迪的交易对手风险信号、所有权结构和财务健康指标，从而更快、更明智地执行交易；专业服务公司可在新业务承接和利益冲突工作流程中直接访问穆迪的实体和所有权数据，加速客户入驻并增强监管抗辩能力；私募资本和会计公司可在投资组合监控、基金尽职调查和实体验证期间直接访问穆迪的信用信号和交易对手筛查，减少手动研究并加速决策。该集成基于模型上下文协议（MCP），这一新兴开放标准用于连接AI系统与外部数据源和工具。穆迪的MCP服务器允许Celeste等AI平台以编程方式访问其数据和分析，从而提供更丰富、更具上下文、基于结构化金融情报的响应。Celeste与穆迪的MCP集成现已面向拥有有效穆迪数据订阅的Intapp客户提供。现有客户可通过Intapp客户成功团队激活该集成，Intapp方面无需额外许可。
news.bodyHtml:
Celeste now surfaces Moody’s credit risk, entity screening, and ownership data at the moment of decision — through natural conversation and without disrupting the workflow

PALO ALTO, Calif. – July 14, 2026 – Deal professionals and risk teams spend significant time switching between platforms to gather counterparty intelligence — often at the precise moment a decision is in motion. Intapp (NASDAQ: INTA) today announced an expansion of its strategic partnership with Moody’s that helps reduce that friction.

Clients across the legal, private capital, and accounting verticals will benefit from new integration between Moody’s data and Intapp Celeste, Intapp’s agentic AI platform purpose-built for professional firms.

Through natural conversation, Celeste surfaces Moody’s financial risk intelligence, entity screening results, ownership structures, and company intelligence directly within the workflows professionals use every day — no context-switching required. By moving from data access to embedded intelligence, Intapp and Moody’s enable clients to unlock greater value:

  • Deal professionals can surface Moody’s counterparty risk signals, ownership structures, and financial health indicators directly within Intapp DealCloud at the moment of decision — enabling faster, better-informed deal execution.
  • Professional services firms can directly access Moody’s entity and ownership data within new business intake and conflicts workflows — accelerating client onboarding and strengthening regulatory defensibility.
  • Private capital and accounting firms can directly access Moody’s credit signals and counterparty screening during portfolio monitoring, fund diligence, and entity verification — reducing manual research and context switching while accelerating decision-making.

“Professional services firms operate in high-stakes, relationship-intensive environments where decisions carry long-term consequences,” said Helen Rider, Head of Global Sales at Moody’s. “Moody’s data has always been designed for exactly these moments — and our expanded partnership with Intapp now puts that intelligence inside Intapp’s AI-native workflows. That’s the kind of embedded intelligence that changes how professional services firms operate.”

The Celeste and Moody’s integration is built on the Model Context Protocol (MCP), an emerging open standard for connecting AI systems to external data sources and tools. Moody’s MCP server allows its data and analytics to be accessed programmatically by AI platforms like Celeste, enabling richer, more contextual responses grounded in structured financial intelligence.

“Celeste was designed to meet professionals in their workflow — not pull them out of it,” explained Don Coleman, Chief Operating Officer at Intapp. “Integrating Moody’s intelligence through MCP is a perfect expression of that vision. Our clients can now surface counterparty risk, credit signals, and entity data through a natural conversation with Celeste, without breaking their concentration or their process. This sets a new standard for how AI serves professional services — and marks a meaningful next chapter in our partnership with Moody’s.”

The Celeste and Moody’s MCP integration is available now to Intapp customers with an active Moody’s data subscription. Existing customers can activate the integration through their Intapp customer success team; no additional licensing is required on the Intapp side.

For more information, visit intapp.com/celeste or contact your Intapp account representative.

About Intapp

Intapp (NASDAQ: INTA) is the governed AI platform for professional firms in highly regulated industries. Intapp’s vertically tailored agentic solutions are built for the specialized workflows, complex relationship networks, and professional compliance requirements of accounting, consulting, investment banking, law, private capital, and real assets firms. By applying Firm AI to core processes and data, Intapp helps partners, dealmakers, and advisors drive firm growth, manage compliance, and improve profitability. Learn why the world’s top firms trust Intapp’s industry-specific enterprise solutions at intapp.com.

news.titleEn: Another Omnibus Package – No.’VII’ – This Time on All Things AI
news.titleZh: 又一揽子简化方案——第七号——此次聚焦人工智能
news.summaryZh: 欧盟第七套简化监管负担的修订方案已获批准，将调整《欧盟人工智能法案》的适用方式，部分义务此前已生效。欧盟理事会与欧洲议会已就修改达成一致，延续此前一揽子方案思路：放缓实施节奏、减轻小企业负担，并在其他欧盟规则已设义务的领域避免双重监管，做法类似此前在《企业可持续发展报告指令》《企业尽职调查指令》及《欧盟森林砍伐条例》等ESG规则上的处理。鉴于其试图推迟的截止期限原定8月起适用，修改预计很快通过。高风险人工智能产品沿用欧盟消费品成熟的合格评定与CE标志制度，就此与需CE标志的普通产品无异。因此，当第七号方案放缓法律适用并厘清与《机械条例》等已确保安全的行业法律的重叠时，开发人工智能产品、将人工智能用作产品安全组件或首次制造含人工智能产品的企业可确信走的是一条成熟路径，但需考虑人工智能的“高风险”不仅取决于产品制度，也取决于系统本身及预期用途。律师负责解释法律，如系统是否属高风险、是否处于边界、哪些论点可避免额外监管负担、最低法律要求为何，并阐明标准与指南文件相对于实施条例的法律价值；同样重要的是，律师知道如何及何时联络技术顾问、内部专家与技术机构，以编制技术文档并建立内部体系。若法律团队既有精通CE标志与合格评定规则（如《无线电设备指令》《电池条例》《RoHS指令》）的律师，又具备数据隐私与数字资产专长，将大有助益。
news.bodyText: Find Your Next Job ! Consistent with the recent strategic shift in policy around EU regulations, the EU’s seventh package of changes to simplify/lighten their burden has just been approved and, with it, we will see changes to the way the EU’s Artificial Intelligence Act will be applied (although some obligations under this legislation are already in force). The EU’s Council of Ministers and Parliament have agreed to changes and, consistently with the overall themes of previous Omnibus packages, there is an emphasis on slowing things down, reducing burdens for smaller sized companies and seeking to avoid the application of a double regulatory burden where legal obligations under other EU rules are already in place. This is similar to what the EU has done under previous packages with ESG rules under the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive, Corporate Due Diligence Directive and the EU Deforestation Regulation (amongst other examples). The changes should be adopted imminently given that the deadlines they are seeking to delay otherwise start to apply in August. Recall that the approach to (high risk) AI products incorporates the tried and tested conformity assessment and CE marking system that we see with so many consumer products on the EU market. AI products, for all their world-changing promise and potential, are in effect treated no differently in this respect from your average widget that requires to have a CE mark. Thus, where the Omnibus VII package slows down the application of the law and clarifies the various overlaps with specific sectoral laws that already ensure safety (such as the Machinery Regulation), companies developing their products for the AI world, using AI as a safety component for products, or those venturing into the manufacture of products incorporating AI for the first time can be reassured that they are treading a well-worn path, albeit with slightly different considerations (noting that what is ‘high-risk’ in terms of AI does not only depend on the product-regime, but also the particularities of the AI system itself and its intended use). Lawyers are there to interpret the laws (e.g. does your AI system fall within a high-risk category? Is it borderline? What are the arguments that will work that will keep you away from additional regulatory burdens? What are the minimum legal requirements for AI?) and explain the legal value of standards and guidance documents as opposed to specific implementing regulations while, just as importantly, if not more, those same lawyers know how and when to liaise with technical consultants, your in-house experts, technical bodies, etc., as appropriate, to compile the necessary technical documentation and establish the appropriate inhouse systems. In that regard, it will help if your legal team includes lawyers who know their way around CE marking/conformity assessment rules because they do it on a daily basis by reference to the Radio Equipment Directive, or Batteries Regulation or RoHS Directive, for example as much as they are experts in data privacy and digital assets law.
